Chat Completions responses can contain zero-filled `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` compatibility fields alongside valid `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`. The model client preferred those aliases, so a response reporting 30,393 prompt tokens and 84 completion tokens was persisted as zero output tokens.

Use one shared usage normalizer with the actual request protocol. Chat Completions prefers prompt/completion; Responses and Anthropic prefer input/output. Aliases are fallbacks, not additional tokens. Explicit counts, including zero and counts that disagree with the reported total, are preserved; reasoning tokens are never added again. Without protocol context, a complete pair matching the total wins, including legitimate zero values. Only when neither pair matches does zero-fill recovery prefer a positive alias. Conflicting aliases retain diagnostics; when both pairs match, input/output keeps its existing precedence.

API session naming, paper vision, and evolution accounting now share the same Chat rules. Incomplete paper usage remains unknown instead of fabricating zero counts. The adapter consumes normalized internal usage events, and the metering proxy already uses the correct Chat precedence; neither needs a rule change. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested commit: `3f06f6ed76c0d6d4e97e08ef2709a1e82b1d7fa8`, based on `bb356a3f474ee6382f05420b3cf05e24d60a756e`. The follow-up adds one commit to the existing branch and changes only the shared normalizer and its unit tests; protocol-aware call sites are unchanged.

- Seven new unknown-protocol regressions all fail on the previous implementation. The complete normalization matrix now passes 19/19, including the reported `10/0/10` case, zero inputs, zero totals, matching-pair ties, and conflict diagnostics. Existing fallback tests also cover missing and inconsistent totals.
- Model typecheck: passed; the full UT layer's typecheck also passed.

The final full UT runs used the standard environment and verified distinct bound ports. An intermediate blocked-queue assertion did not reproduce in the clean candidate or base runs. items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
Startup and opening System settings loaded most of their data with `Promise.all`. One rejected request discarded every sibling that had already succeeded, so a single unhealthy endpoint blanked unrelated panels. #288 pulled the provider registry out of that batch. This change settles every read in both batches on its own, and puts the provider registry back in the same list. A failure is reported for that read only. A successful empty body is still applied, so an empty configuration stays different from a failed read.

## Settle each settings read (`App.tsx`, `settings-loads.ts`)

The two lists stay where they were. Each read applies or reports as soon as it returns, so a request that is still pending cannot hold back the ones that already succeeded. The aggregate promise resolves only after every read has settled. Callers use it to know the batch finished. The project sidebar and the address bar do not wait for that promise: `projectsLoaded` becomes true when the project list itself settles, including when that read fails. A successful empty body is still applied, so an empty configuration stays different from a failed read.

Opening System settings covers providers, models, connectors, skills, skill libraries, global settings, timeouts, quotas, sandbox network, web, memory graph, and idea tree. Startup adds projects, the model catalog, proxy settings, MCP proxy policies, and MCP sources. The reviewer-specialist read was already independent and stays that way.

With `GET /api/memory/settings` returning 500, or still pending, the provider presets, the model list, and global settings are still applied once those reads return. A failed or hung memory read no longer leaves the registry on "已添加 0/1" and "未配置" while those other reads have already succeeded, and it no longer leaves `globalSettings` unset for that reason.

## Preserve overrides when setting the default model (`default-model-override.ts`)

`onDefaultModelSet` used to copy `globalSettings` from memory. That copy is empty when `GET /api/settings` failed or has not returned, so the following `PUT` was only `{ modelId }` and `replaceGlobalSettings` replaced the stored overrides. The callback now reads `GET /api/settings` immediately before the write and changes only `modelId`. If that read throws, nothing is written. The registry's default-model row uses the same helper.

The wizard reads settings before it creates a provider or a model. If that read fails, it stops and reports the error; it does not create a row that the server would pin as the default and then refuse to delete. When the read succeeds, a later failure still writes that snapshot back before deleting the rows this attempt created. The registry default-model menu reports a rejected save through `onError` instead of leaving the promise unhandled.

This covers #291: connecting the first model after `GET /api/settings` returns 500 keeps `enabledConnectorIds`, `semanticReviewEnabled`, and `thinkingEffort`, and does not leave a new provider or model behind.

## Validation

Focused runs in WSL:

- `apps/web/tests/settings-loads.test.ts`: 6 passed / 0 failed. One rejected read does not discard fulfilled siblings, and an empty success is still applied. With memory settings rejected, both the System-settings list and the startup list still apply providers, models, and global settings. The startup list also still applies projects. A memory read that has not returned yet does not block providers, models, global settings, or the project-list settled signal. A rejected project list still marks projects settled.
- `apps/web/tests/startup-projects.test.tsx`: 1 passed / 0 failed. With `GET /api/memory/settings` still pending, the mounted App shows the project in the sidebar and moves the address bar to `/projects/project-1`.
- `apps/web/tests/default-model-override.test.ts`: 3 passed / 0 failed. Setting the default model keeps the overrides from the fresh settings read, clearing it removes only `modelId`, and a rejected settings read does not call the replace.
- `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx`: 31 passed / 0 failed. A failed settings read does not create a provider or write settings. Without a callback, the first model is merged into the overrides returned at save time.
- `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx`: the default-model menu reports a rejected save through `onError` and keeps the previous selection. The file's 14 tests passed.
- `services/api/src/store.test.ts`: rolling back the first provider model restores the previous global settings, then deletes the model and provider. Reopening the store still has those settings and no leftover rows.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not re-run on this host for this commit. The previous full runs here were on a 7.7 GiB WSL VM and did not finish cleanly (UT refused to run as root, the mocked E2E thrashed, and a research-suite download stalled on PyPI). Those layers are left to this pull request's Actions run.

## E2E user journeys

Not run for this commit. The user-visible paths are: one settings endpoint fails at startup, the same failure happens again when System settings opens, and connecting the first model after `GET /api/settings` fails keeps the other global overrides. Expected: every sibling that returned 200 is shown, the failed read shows an error, an existing model plus its global default stay visible, and the default-model write contains the overrides from a fresh settings read. The unit tests above check the load lists and the write body; they do not open a browser. #288 already ran the custom-provider journeys for the case where the preset list itself was missing.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: A failing settings endpoint no longer blanks the settings panels that loaded successfully, and setting the first default model no longer replaces the other global overrides when the settings read failed.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #290
Closes #291
Refs: #288

- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Resolve environment mode on the remote Runner itself. Reject forwarding a host-local custom proxy to a remote Runner, with recovery guidance.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace build and typecheck | Passed before rebase; upstream changes are E2E helpers/tests/docs only |
| Proxy transport, diagnostics and Runner environment tests | 28 passed |
| Model, downloader, Runner client and resolver regression tests | 41 passed |
| Targeted settings persistence / Runner policy propagation | 3 passed (overlaps Runner regression coverage) |
| Adapter hermetic tests | 234 passed; live gateway and real-model test files excluded |
| Proxy settings component tests | 4 passed |
| L1 checks | 4 passed on the rebased head |
| Browser settings journeys | 2 passed in 36.6s on the rebased head |
| Swarm mocked contracts | 9 passed before final rebase; unchanged product code |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

items.body:
CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

items.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

items.body:
## Summary

**Draft — do not merge until the full UT/ST/browser-E2E gates and remaining integration acceptance checks below are completed.** The implementation is available for review; targeted validation passed, but full local validation is incomplete.

Extract Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and expose its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools. This is the service-extraction work for #101 (part of #84), establishing a separate lifecycle and state boundary before the evolve migration in #102.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`. The candidate is `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e` (one commit; 45 changed files, including detected moves).

## 1. Independent service and state ownership

- Move `idea_tree_service`, `research_service`, the research engine, tree models, prompts and templates from evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree/src/sciencediscovery_idea_tree`.
- Remove both router registrations from the evolve server. The new package has no imports from evolve; the existing research algorithm is preserved rather than rewritten as part of the extraction.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI entry point, health endpoint, locked dependencies, shutdown cleanup and service-only authentication. Standalone startup fails closed without `SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.
- Use a dedicated state root (`SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_DATA_DIR`, defaulting under the shared data root's `idea-tree` directory), atomic JSON persistence and independently persisted research settings.
- Copy legacy tree/research records on first startup without deleting originals. A migration marker prevents re-importing stale legacy data; conflicting destination records fail startup instead of overwriting data. Import the old API catalog's settings once, then keep settings authoritative in the service.
- Serve persisted skill references so skill deletion-impact checks include autonomous research as well as historical trees and chat-run references.

## 2. Service-owned MCP tools and capability isolation

The service publishes four tool contracts:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_idea_research` | Start autonomous research with an objective and prepared evidence/materials |
| `get_idea_research` | Query the current session's research and findings |
| `control_idea_research` | Pause, continue or end research |
| `view_idea_tree` | Read a historical tree graph |

The trusted control plane provisions a five-minute capability using its service credential. The scoped MCP endpoint supports initialization, discovery, calls, ping, notifications and revocation. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from that trusted scope, not model-supplied tool arguments. Continue grants are pinned to a specific research ID. Expired scopes are rejected, active scope count is bounded, and revoking a transport scope does not terminate autonomous research. Access logging is disabled for this process to avoid logging capability URLs.

The API obtains schemas from the service and contributes them to the existing JiuwenSwarm MCP bridge/native executor. The former hard-coded create/get tool definitions in `packages/evolve` are removed. Tool discovery failure does not prevent unrelated chat tools from being used.

## 3. TypeScript client and unchanged frontend interfaces

- Replace `services/api/src/idea-tree/python-client.ts` with `IdeaTreeServiceClient` in `packages/idea-tree`. The client provides authenticated, bounded HTTP transport, dynamic tool discovery, scoped MCP research calls, settings transport and historical-tree reads.
- Route active research through the independent service rather than evolve. Preserve the research-created event, create-time chat messages and SSE forwarding.
- Keep historical compatibility types/read transport in `packages/idea-tree`; legacy mutating `tree_*` tools remain disabled.
- Preserve all six frontend paths and their existing response shapes:

| Interface | Handling after this change | Contract mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Research service command/query | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Independent research lifecycle; control plane retains chat-message creation | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | Independent service SSE, forwarded through the existing public route | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | Historical graph read from independent storage | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned settings | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |
| `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned partial update, preserving values on an empty update | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |

These are contract-case mappings, not a claim that a full baseline/candidate L1 differential run passed. The committed lifecycle golden fixture records the stable `running → paused → paused after restart → completed` projection and is asserted by the service journey; it is not a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace.

## 4. Startup, packaging and test discovery

- Provision/start the new service through `scripts/start-stack.sh` and include it in the Docker image.
- Default to loopback port `4314`; reserve `4414` for the isolated browser-test stack and include it in busy-port checks.
- Add `pnpm idea-tree:test`, relocate the existing Python tree/research tests with the service, and include the service in tagged test discovery, environment preparation and coverage roots.
- Add standalone-service documentation covering configuration, migration and the remaining control-plane boundary.

## Compatibility, migration and scope boundaries

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained startup script/Docker packaging includes the new process; custom process supervisors must launch it and provide matching service URL/token configuration.
- Run one ASGI worker: background research tasks and short-lived scopes are process-local. Research and settings are persisted; the journey verifies recovery of paused research after restart.
- The adapter still reaches these frontend routes through the existing API control plane. Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning are **not** moved into the new service by this PR.
- Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; it does not receive provider API keys. Extracting the service does not remove that callback dependency from the wider stack.
- Prepared evidence is preserved, but this PR does not implement the artifact/provenance/CAS service tracked by #98 or change its ownership.
- This PR does not claim completion of the broader JiuwenSwarm migration or the full #101 integration acceptance matrix; full public-route differential and chat/agent trace verification remain review/validation follow-ups.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, recursive workspace build |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including test TypeScript configuration |
| Independent-service Python suite | 34 passed |
| `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` + `packages/idea-tree/src/client.test.ts` under Linux | 11 passed |
| `node test/contract/run.mjs --coverage` | Mapping check passed: 151/254 repository interface rows mapped; not 151 executed tests |
| `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh` and `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh` | PASS |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` | PASS |

Full local gates were attempted in separate checkouts of the candidate and unmodified upstream baseline `5de0ff59`:

- **UT: BLOCKED / incomplete.** `pnpm ci:ut` remained in JiuwenSwarm dependency preparation, downloading/building its Python dependencies, before the shared test runner started. The candidate attempt was manually stopped after approximately ten minutes in this layer; the baseline attempt was also stopped while in the same preparation stage. Both wrappers then recorded exit code 2 (`JiuwenSwarm could not be installed`). This is an interrupted preparation attempt, not an observed product assertion failure, and it does not establish that UT would fail on a fully provisioned host. No frozen plan or planned/executed/passed test summary was generated; those counts are unavailable, not zero-pass success.
- **ST: incomplete, with one smoke passing.** Both checkouts built successfully. The first attempts failed before planning (`A revision is required`) because WSL Git could not resolve the Windows-created temporary worktree metadata. After repairing only that metadata, both retries froze two identities. The candidate's native agent-loop smoke group reports **planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1 / failed 0 / skipped 0**; the baseline emitted the same smoke's pass event. The other identity, `swarm-sdk-contract`, requires JiuwenSwarm setup, which was still preparing dependencies when the run was stopped. No complete two-identity ST summary is available. The retries reused the exact SHA's completed install/build via `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`; no test selection was removed.
- **Browser E2E: incomplete / not executed.** `pnpm ci:e2e` was invoked on both candidate and baseline; preparation reached the pinned `.e2e` dependency installation after the workspace build. The attempts were stopped during preparation. No browser plan, executed-journey count or final summary was produced. This is not a browser PASS and not evidence of a candidate-specific failure.

Remaining local verification was deliberately stopped rather than leaving background preparation jobs running. The draft status reflects these incomplete gates; a fully provisioned Linux/CI run is still required. The initial worktree metadata error was a local harness issue, not a source change; the dependency preparation attempts do not support claiming a pre-existing upstream product defect.

## E2E user journey

**PASS** — one independent-service API/CLI journey, seven numbered steps passed, zero failed/blocked/skipped. The driver launches the installed product CLI in a separate process, with an owned data directory and a local HTTP model stub; no paid model calls or external research services are used.

Command, from the repository root after installing the service:

```sh
services/idea-tree/.venv/bin/python test/api/idea-tree-service-journey.py
```

| Step | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Discover tools and save settings | Four MCP tools exposed; settings accepted by the independent process |
| 2. Start research with prepared evidence | Research enters `running`; the real engine reaches the local model callback |
| 3. Pause active research | Paused state persists; the delayed model response does not advance the paused stage |
| 4. Restart the service | Paused research and saved settings are recovered |
| 5. Read from another session | Cross-session capability cannot access the research |
| 6. Continue and consume SSE | 19 snapshots received; research completes with independently assessed candidate score 7; no model token in frames |
| 7. Check references and delete owned research | Persistent skill reference detected; owned session research removed |

This service-level journey does not substitute for the full browser stack, public API/JiuwenSwarm integration or a live-model test. Docker/release-binary execution was not locally verified.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

User impact: research is hosted in a dedicated service with explicit MCP lifecycle controls and persistent, independently owned settings/state. Existing frontend paths remain stable.

The contributor has read-only access to upstream (`push: false`, `triage: false`), so the GitHub `release:feature` label is **pending a maintainer**; it has not been applied.

items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

Paired: [GitHub #77](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/77) ↔ [GitCode !154](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/154)

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind task

---

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

基于 `origin/main`（`425e4219`，已含 #137）从零实测 Docker Compose 部署：仓库自带 `Dockerfile` 冷构建、起栈、健康检查、浏览器登录、沙箱探针、同机多实例都能跑通，但新用户按现有文档会在几处卡住，文档也没有完整列出可配置的环境变量和常见问题。本 PR 把 Docker 部署指南重写成从构建到浏览器登录的完整步骤，补齐变量表与 FAQ，修一处 Compose 转发缺口，并把 Docker 分发路径纳入 GitHub Actions 守护。

1. **部署指南（中英同步）**：Docker 节改为「前置条件 → 准备配置与数据目录 → 构建 → 启动并确认健康 → 浏览器连接 → 配置模型」五步，之后是日常管理表、数据目录、多实例、环境变量、沙箱要求、常见问题（16 条）与限制。实测发现并写进文档的四个坑：bind mount 目录不先 `mkdir -p` 时 Docker 以 root 建目录，入口以「目录不可写」退出——多实例命令原来缺这一步，照抄必失败；日志里的登录链接端口固定是容器端口 4310，改了 `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_PORT` 后要替换；首次启动会在后台创建 starter Python 环境（约 2 GB、需访问 conda-forge），不是卡住；镜像不含 evolve 与 memory-graph 边车，这两项功能在 Docker 中不可用。
2. **环境变量分层**：编排层只被 Compose 读取（`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_HOST_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_UID` / `GID`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST` / `PORT`），容器层经 `environment` 块逐个转发，镜像层由 `Dockerfile` 固定。配置参考的 Docker 表按此拆分并补齐；未转发的变量（如 `HTTP_PROXY`）说明用 `docker-compose.override.yml` 追加。
3. **Compose 转发缺口**：配置参考把 `SCIENCE_AGENT_USAGE_EXCHANGE_RATE*` 四个键和 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MICROMAMBA_BASE_URL` 列为 Docker 变量，但 `docker-compose.yml` 都没有转发，设了静默无效（与 #137 修的上下文变量同类）。四个汇率键改为转发并加入 `.env.docker.example`，空值等于内置默认（`config.ts` 的解析函数对空串返回默认值）；micromamba 镜像 URL 从 Docker 表删除——镜像已内置并播种固定版本，运行期不下载。
4. **deploy skill**：同步补上述坑与对应的排障行。
5. **GitHub Actions `docker` job**：与 `binary` 并列的分发类门禁。真实 `docker compose build`（刻意不用缓存，冷构建才是用户的首次构建）→ 按指南首启顺序起栈 → 等 `/health` → 断言部署契约：容器名由 Compose 项目名派生、`/health` 同时报告 API 与 bubblewrap runner、Compose 健康检查到达 `healthy`、`.env.docker.example` 的键到达容器环境、micromamba 播种在文档路径、容器内探针通过 → 失败时上传容器日志 → `down`。job 不预先放宽宿主 `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`：容器靠自己的 `security_opt` 取得沙箱能力，探针本身就是判据。起栈步骤按指南复制 `.env.docker.example` 并写入执行用户的 uid/gid：托管 runner 不是 uid 1000，否则容器写不进它刚创建的 bind mount；没有 `.env` 时所有转发键为空，「键到达容器」的断言也只会失败。构建期硬依赖 `https://models.dev/api.json`（`model-catalog` 阶段 `test -s`），该站点不可达时 job 会红，job 注释写明先看失败 stage。

提交：

- `3413fa99` fix(docker): forward the usage exchange-rate settings into the container

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Superseded by #212, which targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` and addresses the review feedback below.

Fixes #210. The local memory graph no longer enumerates every `next` path to build folded scope products. It visits each child once within its session and scope, follows only `scope_chain` links, and keeps the producing child's identity for surrogate edges. The same bounded walk serves group expansion.

## Query safety and chain integrity

- Cap interpreter work, traversal frontier, intermediate rows, and elapsed execution time. A limit hit rolls back the statement and returns a structured HTTP 503 response.
- Log query identity, duration, graph size, traversal and intermediate counts, and termination reason without logging graph contents.
- Rebuild scope and temporal chains by their `method` so an existing edge of another chain type is not repurposed. Exclude children from the session temporal chain by their parent marker.

## Validation

- Local memory graph suite: 174 passed, 1 deselected (`test_legacy_artifact_id_constraint_dropped` requires Neo4j server constraints), 0 failed.
- The 18-diamond branch/rejoin regression passed in 0.49 seconds under a 25-second watchdog with a 512 MiB RSS termination threshold; observed peak RSS was 91,872 KiB. It covers an affected session, a nearly empty unrelated session, cycles, mixed chain methods, cross-scope edges, product deduplication, and `via_child`. A separate regression proves that generic path queries stop at the budget and roll back writes.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: 3,167 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed. Preflight `HOST_MISMATCH`: this host is macOS/arm64 and the shared plan requires Linux/amd64. Unmodified `main` has the same failure (3,163 planned / 0 executed).
- `pnpm ci:st`: 1 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed for the same `HOST_MISMATCH`. Unmodified `main` has the same result.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: preparation reached the pinned Playwright Chromium install, which stalled on this host; the run was stopped before collection. The shared E2E plan also targets Linux/amd64 and needs to run in GitHub Actions.

## GitHub Actions (run 36247142103, commit `b39fcd9f`)

- UT: 3,174 planned / 3,174 executed / 3,174 passed.
- ST: 1 planned / 1 executed / 1 passed.
- Mocked browser E2E: 44 planned / 44 executed / 44 passed / 0 skipped.
- Docker image, x86_64 binary release, aarch64 binary release, and Coverage: passed. All seven jobs succeeded.

## E2E user journeys

- Repository mocked browser subset: PASS 44/44 on the final commit `b39fcd9f`.
- Targeted local product API journey: PASS 4/4 on `b39fcd9f` with `node test/api/memory-folded-subgraph-journey.mjs`. It starts an isolated API, Runner, and local graph; observes two scoped Papers; verifies folded aggregation, group expansion, `via_child`, and a fresh session query (3 ms). The script owns its ports, credentials, and graph data directory, and removes its processes and data afterward.
- The large 18-diamond history and structured budget error are covered by the local memory graph regression suite.

## Release

Release category: `release:performance` (label pending a maintainer; this fork account lacks permission to apply upstream labels).
User impact: Folded memory graph views stay responsive for branched historical sessions, and excessive generic graph queries terminate with a clear error instead of exhausting the host.
Compatibility and migration: None.

## Follow-up update — 2026-09-23

This update adds the pending follow-up commits to the same personal-fork PR, rather than opening a duplicate PR. Target remains `feat/jiuwenswarm`; related #107 and #136. The validation in this section supersedes earlier local results below; historical real-model results are retained for context, not presented as validation of the latest head.

### Added scope

- Isolate shared MCP request cancellation/transport failures and add bounded, credential-conscious boundary/model-argument diagnostics. Consolidate the per-run deadline compatibility change into the version-pinned transport patch; verify patch installation is repeatable.
- Add configurable per-parent subagent concurrency (1–10, default 10) in system settings, with FIFO waiting, cancellation and lifetime-scoped permits. A deployment can set 2 without changing the product default.
- Wire real model transport/text/thinking/tool-argument progress to the owning run's idle watchdog. Preserve the hard whole-run deadline; sibling activity and unowned default-route housekeeping do not renew another run.
- Enforce child model-turn limits at request admission, before calling the provider, instead of inferring turns from UI events/tool-result counts. Keep the existing `timed_out` + `Subagent exceeded maxTurns=...` lifecycle contract. Exclude explicit housekeeping and the pinned Swarm compaction instruction; unknown future compaction prompts count conservatively as task calls. This prompt compatibility predicate is not a security boundary.
- Reject HTML/empty content masquerading as a PDF before publishing download completion. Check only a bounded 1 KiB header; full PDF parsing remains a separate extraction operation. Other artifact formats retain their behavior.
- Expand Mock literature coverage to source fallback, governed download/extraction, tool-output paging, real Swarm compaction, artifact isolation/reload, child budgets/cancellation and recovery. Add a provider-503 → cancel → healthy same-session/tool-backed run.
- Include the five stratified DeepResearchBench real cases and real custom Specialist/MCP/team signoff case, with opt-in record retention. Real evaluations remain manual and are not a PR gate.

### Latest verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Node Swarm agent/model gateway/download/subagent lifecycle regressions | 111 passed, 0 skipped |
| Python Adapter suite | 212 passed, 9 skipped: 7 opt-in live gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM cases |
| Research model + literature-source fixture tests | 8 passed |
| Version-pinned Swarm/SDK compatibility and MCP boundary tests | 51 passed |
| FIFO subagent pool / UI settings draft tests | 3 passed / 1 passed |
| Actual Swarm + Mock LLM/source browser E2E | **20 passed, 0 skipped; 7.1 minutes; one worker** |
| Artifact manager and API builds | Passed |
| Documentation lint/links and CI catalog validation | Passed |

The 20 browser cases use the actual Swarm, Adapter, API, Runner and PDF extractor; only external model/source transports are scripted. They are not evidence of real-LLM research quality, a DRB score, or long-duration memory stability. The formerly failing LR-04 now proves the second child model request never reaches the model; LR-11 HTML now fails before completion.

Coverage details and reproduction prerequisites: `test/benchmarks/research-team/mock-coverage.md` and `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`. The existing research Mock gate remains enabled. **The complete new 20-case suite requires the dedicated offline-source fixture, exclusive Swarm instance and compaction configuration; it is not claimed to run in full in the default PR gate.** No real-provider credentials, raw private traces or local service configuration are committed. Latest CI results must be checked separately.

### Remaining boundaries

- A historical Swarm management-interface timeout was not reproduced by the new recovery case. Its initiating cause remains unproven; a passing controlled recovery test does not establish that the historical incident is fixed.
- No complete six-case real-LLM rerun or RACE/FACT quality score is claimed for this head. The interrupted DRB-59 run is not counted as successful.
- No new Swarm source patch was needed for the latest idle/model-turn/PDF fixes; the PR as a whole still includes the earlier version-pinned Swarm compatibility patches.
- This remains a source-checkout validation. Packaged binary/Docker compatibility, broader resource stability, and dashboard work remain outside these local results.

---

## Summary

Repair the Swarm-backed literature research path: specialist children receive their MCP tools, bind their own model connection, return explicit results/errors, and let the parent continue to a persisted report.

Targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` from the personal fork `zy95-12/sciencediscovery`. Related: #107, #136. Native Swarm delegation reuse remains a separate design discussion in #141.

## Changes and boundaries

- Retain **ScienceDiscovery `task` orchestration + Swarm execution** for main and child agents. When `subagents=task`, hide the native spawn/wait/list/send-input/close/resume tools from actual LLM requests, override generic native-delegation guidance, and reject stale native tool calls. Swarm search/fetch remain available.
- Bind a private model connection to each run/session using the real model name rather than per-run global model aliases/hot reloads. Forward bindings in stream/non-stream paths, allow idle-session rebinding, and reject active replacement. Preserve run/agent identity in credential-free lifecycle logs.
- Preserve startup and runtime errors, initial/resumed stream correlation and output ownership. Require an explicit terminal result: EOF/cancellation/failed status must not become successful completion.
- Keep MCP catalog refresh and child tool failures isolated; give the platform MCP transport a stable lifecycle owner and configured deadlines instead of competing wrappers/read timeouts. No automatic side-effect replay.
- Forward tool-call streaming progress, normalize model SSE output, and make child artifact handoff/provenance available to the parent.
- Carry six version-pinned, reviewable compatibility patches under `jiuwen_swarm/patches/workswarm0.2.6/`, plus regressions and setup/diagnostic documentation.
- Add/update a gate-enabled mocked research journey and an opt-in real DRB-59 browser journey, pinned upstream RACE/FACT evaluation support, and per-attempt result records. Research strategy, child count and source count are not prescribed by the benchmark prompt.

Merged the latest target branch and resolved the `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` conflict: source installs apply compatibility patches before virtualenv synchronization; the target branch's preinstalled path and instance initialization remain intact. The real validation below uses the source checkout, not packaged Docker/binary distributions; these distribution channels still need patch compatibility validation before claiming support for this run contract.

## Mock E2E is a PR gate; real E2E is manual only

`test/swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts` is included in the default mocked PR gate; the CI Swarm stack already enables its platform-task prerequisite. Only `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` is excluded unless **`E2E_RESEARCH=1`**. PR workflows do not set that variable. Real tests additionally require the real project and live credentials. Fast unit regressions also remain in normal CI.

Verified by test discovery: the default mocked list contains the Swarm research mock case and excludes the real case; explicit real opt-in discovers DRB-59. No scheduled benchmark/dashboard workflow was added.

Manual runs against an isolated, configured Swarm stack:

```bash
E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 npm --prefix .e2e run test:mocked -- swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts
E2E_RESEARCH=1 E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 E2E_DRB_EVALUATION=off npm --prefix .e2e run test:real -- deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts
```

See `jiuwen_swarm/README.md` and `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench/README.md` for auth, generator/Judge configuration and full evaluation. Evaluation defaults to `full`; `off` is an explicit integration-only diagnostic mode, not a quality pass.

## Validation

### Latest real run — September 23

**GLM-5.2 + actual Swarm + browser: 1 passed.** Same DRB-59 bird-migration question as the preceding failed attempt. No fixed delegation count/search-depth prompt limits.

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Actual delegation | Four platform `task` children; all completed |
| Child branches | Magnetic, celestial, olfactory/landmark, navigation disturbances |
| Recorded child turns | 9 / 25 / 16 / 15 |
| MCP activity | Successful PubMed / Europe PMC calls; child artifacts declared |
| Parent continuation | Continued research after child results and declared final report |
| Persisted report | `deepresearchbench-59.md`, 5,428 words, 30 headings, 50 distinct URL strings |
| Browser assertions | Visible artifact/preview, basic report structure, reload persistence and final handoff passed |
| Generation duration | 1,011,856 ms (~16.9 minutes) |
| Total browser test | ~23.8 minutes |
| RACE / FACT | Disabled for this run; **no quality score claimed** |

Browser validation was slowed by cgroup memory reclaim; the browser soft/hard limits were raised from 650/850 MiB to 1000/1100 MiB after checking host capacity. Assertions were unchanged; no OOM was observed. This affects timing comparisons. Raw traces remain private because they may contain credentials/research content; test services were stopped afterwards.

The earlier run failed because native subagent tools leaked into the task-mode toolset and native activity did not reset the platform idle timer. That failure is not hidden: the isolation fix addresses the task path; native-child progress forwarding remains outside this PR.

### Automated regressions

- After target-branch merge: API build, 86 affected Node tests, 190 adapter tests (9 skipped: 7 opt-in live Gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM tests), 72 engineering/CI self-tests, documentation checks, shell syntax and compatibility patch reverse-applicability checks passed.
- Delegation isolation validation: 72 Node tests and 71 adapter tests passed.
- Earlier broader validation on this change series: 189 adapter tests passed / 9 skipped; 167 affected Node tests; 23 patched Swarm/SDK regressions; workspace typecheck, architecture boundaries, native hermetic ST smoke passed.
- Actual Swarm + mocked LLM browser journey: 1 passed (44.2 s), covering child error recovery, child artifact, parent reading it, final report/UI and follow-up session rebinding. This precedes the final isolation/config-only updates.
- Evaluator unit tests: 9 passed, 1 skipped, 9 subtests passed. The skip needs an external pinned evaluator checkout; it is not counted as passing.

This is not a full repository regression run. The real E2E pass precedes the subsequent target merge/manual-collection-only changes; it was not rerun after that merge. Latest CI still needs to run on this PR head.

## Known limitations / follow-up

- arXiv returned HTTP 406; one child mixed read_tool_output query/range arguments; another used a temporary file across shell calls. All recovered or continued in the passing run; upstream availability and these ergonomics are not claimed fixed.
- Native todo tools remain visible when platform update_plan is selected. Native-child progress forwarding and full native delegation inheritance are not implemented here.
- Platform usage currently reports one invocation / 138,374 tokens for the run; this is **not a verified aggregate of all main/child requests** and must not be shown as full benchmark cost.
- No all-five-case result, official leaderboard score, or full RACE+FACT pass is claimed. A historical separate RACE run scored 47.49/100 with substituted GLM-5.2 Judge on an earlier report; it is not the score of the current passing run.
- Version-wide dashboard implementation is owned by a separate workstream. This PR supplies `benchmark-metrics.json`, exact report input and optional evaluation scorecards/usage/provenance for later ingestion; it does not implement dashboard UI, aggregation or scheduling. Missing/disabled/partial scores must not be treated as quality passes.

## Problem and behavior

Test entry points and discovery rules did not describe the same repository coverage. This change gives local development and CI one selector/runner, loads scenario metadata from adjacent `.case.yaml` files and module discovery from `.suite.yaml`, and preserves the existing test frameworks and default `pnpm test` scope.

Browser journeys move to `test/e2e/`, standalone API journeys to `test/st/api/`, and native agent smoke tests to `test/st/agent-runtime/`. Backend API and all contract scenarios are classified as ST; E2E is reserved for browser user journeys. Shared contract replay/normalization/comparison code lives once in `test/support/contract/`, with its UT alongside it; scenarios, baselines and accepted-difference policy live in `test/st/contract/`. Recursive Node/Web discovery, asset ownership checks and source/build mapping prevent silent omissions. Issue-number filenames are replaced with scenario/object names. Only two previously approved obsolete browser declarations are retired, with reasons and the remaining disabled-connector coverage gap recorded in the migration ledger.

## Directory and layer model

- Product UT stays in the owning module; test-tooling UT stays beside its implementation in `test/support/`.
- `test/st/agent-runtime/` covers direct cross-module agent collaboration.
- `test/st/api/` covers backend service chains through HTTP; `test/st/contract/` owns HTTP/event-stream scenarios and baselines. Both L1 and L2 contracts are ST.
- `test/e2e/` contains browser user journeys. There is no separate API E2E category.
- `test/support/contract/` supplies one shared contract implementation; no scenario-specific copies of the runner or normalizer are introduced.
- API IDs are `st.api.<scenario>` and all contract IDs are `st.contract.<scenario>`. `test/support/migration.json` records the moves and prior draft IDs. Browser IDs and PR/daily membership/backend matrices are unchanged.

## Scenario naming

Use lowercase kebab-case object/behavior names, without issue numbers, `journey-` / `-journey` or `l1-` / `l2-` labels. Examples:

- `test/e2e/first-run-onboarding.spec.ts` and `.case.yaml`, ID `e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding`.
- `test/st/api/child-workspace.mjs` and `.case.yaml`, ID `st.api.child-workspace`.
- `test/st/contract/cases/run-approval-denied.case.yaml`, scenario ID `run-approval-denied`, catalog ID `st.contract.run-approval-denied`.
- `session-multi-turn` describes the former `l2-two-turns` contract scenario; `run-events.json` holds run-event scenarios.

Implementation/config filenames and IDs stay aligned. Shared browser helpers are `scenario-fixtures.ts`, `scenario-report.ts` and `browser-fixture.ts`. Module UT follows module names; Python's conventional `test_*.py` discovery remains unchanged.

Step-report validation is now explicit in YAML (`reporting: steps`) rather than inferred from a `journey-` filename; all formerly marked journeys retain this enforcement. Naming validation rejects the historical test filename prefixes/suffixes.

`namingMigration` in `test/support/migration.json` records old/new paths, catalog IDs and contract scenario IDs. Baseline keys and accepted-difference case references are renamed together; expected response payloads, scenario steps and difference predicates are unchanged. External baselines using the old IDs need the same key migration. The naming migration preserved all 92 configured entries and their policies; the subsequent real-model extension below adds daily coverage, and all 88 retained browser test identities were verified after filename mapping.

## Triggers and usage

Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then:

```bash
pnpm test:list --profile pr --json
pnpm test:list --profile daily --json
pnpm test:doctor --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both
pnpm test:check
```

- PR opened/synchronize/reopened events run the configured PR policy. Pushes to `main`/`master` and manual CI dispatch use the same policy; existing binary/Docker gates remain.
- `test-daily.yml` schedules the daily policy at **00:17 UTC / 08:17 Asia/Shanghai**, with manual dispatch also declared. Scheduled execution starts when the workflow reaches the default branch.
- PR policy has **7 required entries**: both UT tiers, native deterministic ST, and four JiuwenSwarm browser scenarios. Daily policy has **82 required entries plus 54 observational contract entries** (27 scenarios × two executor labels). These are execution entries, not framework case counts.
- YAML separates `llm.mode`, supported executors and scheduled executors. Real-model/hardware/legacy gates are never enabled by selection. PR/daily executor policy cannot be overridden on the command line.
- Nonblocking entries retain FAIL/BLOCKED/etc. and produce `passed-with-observations` when required tasks pass. Full/manual selections treat every selected entry as required.
- GitHub provisions the browser stack/JiuwenSwarm dependencies; local callers must supply the prerequisites reported by `test:doctor`. CodeArts keeps its existing compatibility command scope.

See [test/README.md](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/refactor/configured-test-harness/test/README.md) for configuration examples, gates, executor limitations and report locations. Reports distinguish PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SKIPPED and NOT_RUN; external contract executor labels remain explicitly operator-declared.

## Configured subject models and assertions

Every case now explicitly declares `assertions.mode`: `deterministic`, `llm`, or `hybrid`. Real subject models are configured independently from judge models:

```yaml
llm:
  mode: real
  model:
    protocol: chat-completions
    baseUrlEnv: E2E_LLM_BASE_URL
    modelEnv: E2E_LLM_MODEL
    apiKeyEnv: E2E_LLM_TOKEN
assertions:
  mode: hybrid
  judge:
    model:
      protocol: chat-completions
      baseUrlEnv: E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL
      modelEnv: E2E_JUDGE_MODEL
      apiKeyEnv: E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    maxTokens: 1200
    maxInputCharacters: 24000
    rubric:
      - id: task-completion
        description: The answer and supplied artifact meet the requested task.
        threshold: 0.8
```

A model profile accepts exactly one literal `model` or `modelEnv`; each case may bind different environment names. Credentials are never stored in YAML. The initial transport is OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; scoring requires a model supporting its temperature/max-token parameters.

Browser cases use `assessment.check(name, callback)` for configurable programmatic assertions and `assessment.submit({task, answer, artifacts, context})` for actual bounded evidence. Deterministic mode runs checks without a judge call. LLM-only mode skips those optional assertion callbacks. Hybrid mode requires at least one successful named check and all judge thresholds to pass. Ordinary framework `expect` calls remain mandatory structural/workflow guards. Never put setup/actions inside the optional assertion callback.

Judging runs only after the test body passes. Missing evidence, missing model configuration, malformed/missing/duplicate scores, low scores, HTTP errors and timeouts cannot produce PASS. There is no automatic fallback or retry. Every criterion has an explicit threshold in [0,1]. The configured input limit rejects oversized evidence rather than silently truncating it. Reports include per-attempt assessment attachments, resolved subject/judge identities, sanitized evidence, rubric, scores, reasons, usage when supplied and latency. A framework pass without required scoring evidence is rejected by the harness. Qualitative scoring does not prove numerical correctness; keep objective calculations checked programmatically.

The initial production example is `e2e.browser.model-request`: real subject + hybrid completion/delivery checks and report-quality scoring. The other two existing real-browser files retain deterministic assertions. All non-browser runners currently support deterministic assertions; unsupported scoring/runner combinations fail configuration validation explicitly.

## Daily real-model execution and setup

`test-daily.yml` invokes independent `external:none` and `external:real` jobs through the same reusable workflow. The external tag is derived from **either** a real subject or a live judge, so stub-subject/live-judge cases cannot accidentally enter the deterministic job. PR remains deterministic and receives no model secrets.

All three real-browser files run daily on both native and JiuwenSwarm as required work: six added entries. Daily now expands to **136 entries: 82 required and 54 observational contracts**. PR remains seven required entries. The real job explicitly sets `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`; missing credentials cause required work to fail with unmet prerequisites.

Configure these repository Actions secrets for the supplied profiles:

- `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`.
- `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`.

Custom case-specific environment names must also be wired into the workflow. The implementation does not create secrets or choose a paid provider. Inspect with `pnpm test:list --profile daily --tag external:real --json`; with the six values exported and the isolated stack prerequisites ready, use `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm test:daily --tag external:real`.

`literature-review` now registers/selects the configured model rather than hardcoded DeepSeek profiles; it still depends on its Skill/connector fixtures and PubMed availability. Those remaining requirements can block daily runs. Real-project Playwright traces are disabled because registration request bodies contain model keys; step screenshots and sanitized scoring evidence remain.

Local validation includes actual Playwright fixture execution against a local HTTP judge: three expected passes, three deliberate failures (native check, missing evidence, low score), three scoring requests and five assessment attachments. This verifies execution/reporting integration without calling an external model. No real-provider or complete product E2E pass is claimed: subject/judge variables were absent in the local environment during validation.

## Validation and limitations

Rebased onto `feat/jiuwenswarm` revision `9670568`, preserving its added tests, isolation changes and accepted contract differences.

- Catalog validation: **92 execution entries, 48 suites, 437 static assets**.
- Harness/contract tooling: **65 tests passed**; CI self-tests: **53 passed**; architecture: **19 passed** plus boundary validation.
- Documentation lint and links passed across 89 Markdown files.
- Pinned Playwright collection compared with the latest target: **90 upstream identities → 88 retained identities in 47 files**; exactly the two approved retirements explain the difference. This is collection, not test execution.
- Workflow YAML parsing, shell syntax and diff whitespace checks passed. Workspace-only guest packaging was checked for the YAML runtime dependency.

A full product E2E run and remote workflow execution have **not** been certified by these checks. Contract CI targets/baseline selection remain unprovisioned; their observations report BLOCKED until supplied. Existing product failures are not suppressed or fixed by this test-engineering change.

Implements #126. The issue remains the detailed scope and trigger/usage reference; merging into this feature branch does not activate default-branch scheduled runs.

Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

## What changes

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Coverage ran with `needs.ut.result=success` and read the 07:30 package, so `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` reported incomplete coverage.

Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This change is GitHub Actions artifact metadata. Those layers do not observe the artifact store, and the contract test is what locks the flag.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. No product UI, API, CLI, or run path changes. The bug is which artifact a later GitHub Actions job downloads after a job re-run.

J5 skipped the real Nightly shard as soon as `GET /api/environment-setup` reported the managed Python base as `installing`. That string is the normal cold-start phase, and the HTTP server is already up, so a single read races the install. Real E2E treats the skip as a failed shard. Closes #286.

## Wait for the base J5 already depends on

`waitForEnvironmentSetup` reads the existing status immediately, then every 5 seconds, on one 180-second deadline shared with an in-flight read. `ready` and `failed` return at once. When the deadline passes, the last observation is returned, including the case where the first read never completes. J5 calls it inside the existing credential and health step, after `test.setTimeout(600_000)`, and still skips with `BLOCKED` when the returned state is not `ready`. The reader only GETs. Nothing starts a second install.

Mocked J3 keeps its immediate `expect(state).toBe("ready")`. The team journey and the runner are unchanged.

## Validation

Requested scope was this one real journey, on `f81767d0f11bce59294424e552d7c881873f6d3c`, model `deepseek-flash`.

- Real J5 (`test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh real`, `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`): Playwright `1 passed (1.3m)`, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Journey report PASS, 6/6 steps, 78.7s. The readiness step passed in 15.2s, inside the 180s bound. The run then completed a statistics request and opened a nonempty Markdown artifact.
- `check-e2e-meta` in that same run: 61 spec files, 0 errors, 11 legacy warnings.
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` was run locally before this pull request: 8 passed / 0 failed. It was not repeated for this submission.
- UT, ST, and mocked E2E were not run. This submission was limited to J5.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Browser journey J5 on the local product stack, tested SHA `f81767d0f11bce59294424e552d7c881873f6d3c`.

A researcher asks, in ordinary language, for a small coded mean and standard deviation and a Markdown report. Expected: the run reaches a completed state, a code-execution step is visible, and the named Markdown artifact opens with content. Actual: all six steps passed; the model run completed in the second step (61.3s) and the artifact preview was nonempty.

Command: `.ci/run-e2e.sh real` with `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`, `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`, `CI_E2E_SPEC=test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`, and a grep for the J5 title. Counts: discovered 1, executed 1, passed 1, failed 0, skipped 0.
