closed_recent.body:
## Problem and goal

Containers, restricted cloud environments, and remote compute nodes may have bubblewrap installed but prohibit the namespaces or mounts it needs. The ability to install, build, and open the workbench should be separate from the selected Runner's ability to execute code safely.

Users should not need to understand execution modes before using the product. Installation and builds should not be blocked by execution-mode requirements. Explain the limitation and offer choices only when a task actually needs code execution and the selected Runner cannot satisfy its requirements.

## Observed environments and results

On 2026-10-11, different execution environments produced different results. These observations do **not** support a blanket claim that cloud desktops cannot run sandboxes:

1. **Restricted cloud coding container:** while investigating main `cc95884428e64ae853d8758574fff5107c6347f0`, bubblewrap failed with `setting up uid map: Read-only file system`, consistent with that environment's /proc restrictions. Source installation and builds could complete, but sandbox execution remained unavailable.
2. **Tool execution session on another cloud desktop:** at main `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, the project's sandbox probe failed with `loopback: Failed to create NETLINK_ROUTE socket: Operation not permitted`.
3. **Desktop terminal on that same cloud desktop:** the same probe succeeded, and the Runner and workbench subsequently started from the desktop terminal. No sandbox disabling or host security-policy changes were required. The tool session and desktop terminal occupied different network namespaces.

Capability checks must therefore run in the **actual execution environment of the selected Runner**. A failure in an installation shell or another session must not be generalized to the entire machine. Likewise, a remote node merely appearing to be containerized does not establish adequate isolation.

## Current implementation and consequences

Code observations below refer to `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`:

- Standalone dependency installation and builds are possible, but the [one-command source startup path](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L326-L395) checks sandbox executables before installation/build. It also [waits for Runner health before proceeding with API/UI startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L626). Missing sandbox dependencies or a Runner startup failure can therefore prevent access to the workbench.
- [Runner startup preflight](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/server.ts#L1086-L1142) handles failures differently: some Linux sandbox failures only produce a warning, whereas missing/incompatible executables or unusable Seatbelt prevent startup. Process liveness or HTTP health is not equivalent to code-execution readiness.
- Internal probes already expose information such as sandboxUsable, but this is not yet an end-to-end capability and recovery contract spanning Runner registration, task dispatch, and the UI.
- [Code tool bindings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts#L174-L219) do not provide a dedicated just-in-time choice flow for unavailable sandbox execution. Generic permission to run code is not consent to unsandboxed execution.
- [Ordinary code execution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/executor.ts#L933-L1003) still depends on bubblewrap/Seatbelt; there is no general-purpose unsandboxed backend. The direct connection setting means a direct connection to a Runner, not unsandboxed execution.
- The [existing permission mechanism](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/permissions/index.ts#L28-L80) may provide an interaction foundation, but it does not establish that execution-mode switching, dedicated consent, and reliable recovery already exist.

User impact:
1. Users who only want to install, build, configure models, or browse the workbench may be blocked by local compute prerequisites.
2. A service may appear connected, yet fail when code is executed, making sandbox, network, dependency, and model failures difficult to distinguish.
3. Users with an available remote Runner may still have to troubleshoot local execution; restricted-environment users lack an actionable in-product next step.
4. Silently falling back to direct execution would remove isolation without informed consent, increasing exposure of files, processes, and credentials.

## Expected behavior

1. **Decouple installation, builds, and workbench startup from execution readiness.** Allow installation/build and non-execution configuration/browsing when the local Runner is unavailable. Clearly indicate compute limitations rather than claiming full readiness.
2. **Probe capabilities per Runner.** Distinguish connectivity, dependencies, sandbox availability, and execution readiness; retain structured failure reasons and validate them at the actual execution location.
3. **Ask only when execution requires a decision.** Use an available safe execution path by default. When blocked, explain why and offer an available Runner, environment repair, or cancellation. Do not force users to choose modes during installation.
4. **If direct-execution fallback is supported, design it explicitly.** Reuse task orchestration and artifact handling, branching at the execution backend. Never silently downgrade. Explain the affected scope and obtain dedicated consent first; authorization scope, lifetime, and invalidation require design review.
5. **Retain product responsibility for safety.** An assertion that the external environment is controlled must not replace validation, hazardous-action controls, auditing, cancellation, or recovery. This issue does not request disabling host security policies or bypassing platform restrictions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Independent installation/build completes in three cases: bwrap missing, bwrap present but namespace creation denied, and a working sandbox.
- [ ] When local compute is unavailable, the workbench supports permitted non-execution flows and clearly reports limited capabilities.
- [ ] Preflight results belong to the selected Runner's actual execution environment, not another shell or node.
- [ ] A task requiring code execution reports the blocking reason and allows an available Runner or cancellation; normal environments do not gain unnecessary prompts.
- [ ] If direct execution is implemented, it requires consent distinct from generic code permission, has no silent fallback, and produces auditable records.
- [ ] Tests cover rejection/cancellation, repeated execution, Runner changes, capability changes, and process restarts; already completed side effects must not be duplicated.

## Related issues and scope

- #38 covers the mismatch between serve readiness and actual compute readiness. This issue additionally covers installation/startup decoupling, actual-Runner capability probes, just-in-time interaction, and fallback design.
- #29 covers actionable dependency preflight guidance.
- #264 separately tracks proxy, micromamba download, and SOCKS dependency installation usability.
- These are requirements and design proposals, not a claim that an unsandboxed backend already exists. Delivery staging and the precise direct-execution authorization contract remain design decisions.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Decouple sandbox readiness from installation and workbench startup; offer choices when execution is blocked

Current product UI (recent `openJiuwen/sciencediscovery` main behavior).

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #89](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/89) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Write a long, domain-heavy analysis prompt in the composer and send it.

## What I saw instead

When sending fails (expired local token → 401, network error, provider rate limit → 429, busy backend), only a red toast is shown. The composer text, references, and annotations were already cleared, with no restore, no undo, and no retry. Minutes of writing are gone.

## Code pointer

`submitMessage` in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` clears the draft **before** the request is made:

```ts
setMessage("");
setComposerReferences([]);
setPendingAnnotations([]);
```

Only afterwards does it call `client.streamMessage`; the catch path shows the error but never restores the cleared state.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Clear the composer only after the backend accepts the message; on failure, immediately restore the text, references, and annotations.
- Offer a "resend" action next to the failure notice.

Science users routinely write long statistical-methods-plus-plotting instructions; losing the draft costs far more than in a casual chat app.

Reproduction sketch: type a long prompt, send, and make the request fail (invalidate the token or stop the backend); observe the composer is empty.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8), Chrome, verified against `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Composer text is cleared before the request is accepted and is not restored on failure, losing long prompts

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #92](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/92) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Paste my LLM provider's API key and get the agent working.

## What I saw instead

"Connecting a model" currently requires hopping across two separate settings pages, four times:

1. Open system settings → "Models & capabilities → Model registry";
2. Click "+ Add Provider", pick a preset (e.g. DeepSeek) or custom, paste the API token, save;
3. Still not usable: find the concrete model in the provider's expanded list and click "Add" to create a model entry;
4. Still not usable: switch to "General → Global defaults" and select it in the "task model" dropdown (entries like `test · deepseek-v4-flash · ... · model default`).

Nowhere in the flow is there a link for "where do I get a key", nor any hint that "calls are billed by the provider".

*(Screenshots of the model registry page and the global defaults page are available in the cross-tracked GitCode issue above.)*

## Why this is confusing

- The user's mental model is "paste the key and it works", but the design splits provider, model discovery, model entry, and the global default task model into four layers — cognitive overload for researchers.
- Entry names conflict: the README points to `Global defaults`, the empty state says "model registry", the English UI says `Models` — three names for the same thing.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Provide a single-step connection wizard: pick a provider (DeepSeek / Zhipu / OpenAI / …) → paste the API key → click "Test and enable", which verifies connectivity, registers a recommended main model, and sets it as the global default task model.
- Under the API key input, add one line of guidance: a link to the provider's key page, plus "model calls are billed at the provider's standard rates".

Design note: the wizard orchestrates the existing four-layer configuration without changing the underlying model structure; the manual configuration path can remain for advanced users.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Connecting a model requires hopping across settings pages; provide a single-step connection wizard

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #88](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/88) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4310` for the first time after starting ScienceDiscovery, and see a welcoming entry point to get started.

## What I saw instead

The page immediately opened a settings dialog with **three overlapping red errors at the same time**:

1. A toast in the top-right corner: `Request error: Unauthorized`;
2. A warning bar above the dialog: `Settings error: Unauthorized`;
3. A red alert inside the dialog body: `Access token rejected: The local API rejected this token. Paste the access token the server printed when it started, then save.`

The input field is labeled `Local API token`, and there is no other onboarding content on the page.

*(A screenshot of the three overlapping red errors is available in the cross-tracked GitCode issue above.)*

## Why this is confusing

- Three stacked "unauthorized / rejected" messages right after opening the page make users assume the installation is broken.
- `Local API token` reads like the API key of an LLM provider (OpenAI / DeepSeek). Pasting a model API key gets rejected again with more red text — a dead end.
- The actual token must be found in the server's startup terminal log. If the server runs in the background, in a container, or was started by someone else, users have no idea where to look.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Deduplicate the three errors: when no token is configured, show a single clear guide (where the token lives in the startup log, how to paste and save it) instead of toast + warning bar + in-dialog alert all at once.
- Distinguish "local service access token" from "external model API key" in naming and copy, so users stop pasting model keys into the local token field.
- Open question (not decided): whether loopback (`127.0.0.1`) access should be passwordless by default or issue a one-click session credential — listed here as an option only; it needs a security review first.

## Reproduction

1. Start ScienceDiscovery (`serve`).
2. Open the service URL with a fresh browser profile (no prior localStorage).
3. Observe the toast, warning bar, and in-dialog error appearing simultaneously.

Code pointer: the auth and settings-loading paths in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` trigger three separate error surfaces on a 401 instead of converging on one guide.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8), Chrome, Simplified Chinese UI, verified against `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: First visit without a token shows three overlapping Unauthorized errors, and "Local API token" is easily mistaken for a model API key

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #99](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/99) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Find the installer for my OS on the project homepage/README, download it, and run it.

## What I saw instead

- The Installation section of `README.md` only says: `Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide.` — with no Releases download link at all.
- Following that link, `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` opens with a comparison of three deployment modes, and the single-file binary section then teaches how to **build the binary from source** with the packaging script.
- Meanwhile, the v0.2.0 GitHub release already ships ready-made binaries — `ScienceDiscovery-0.2.0-linux-x86_64` and `ScienceDiscovery-0.2.0-linux-aarch64` — but no entry point directs users to them.

## Why this is confusing

Most researchers will never build from source; the docs funnel "give me the binary" users into "build it yourself" developer documentation. A user has already asked how to obtain the binary in #1; related README/tutorial discussions are in #27 and #26.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Put a direct GitHub Releases link in the most prominent spot of the README (before Quick start), explaining which asset to pick per OS/architecture.
- Include verification instructions (how to check the release assets' SHA-256).
- Layer `deployment.md` so "download the released binary" comes before "build from source".
- Align the naming of configuration entry points across docs (`Global defaults` vs "model registry" vs `Models`).

Docs baseline: `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).

`ContextEngine.register_processor`、`ContextEngine.register_window_mutator`、`agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 的 `import jiuwenswarm`。每块 JiuwenSwarm 能力先定义一个 `Protocol`（port），再在 `adapters/swarm/` 下写适配器实现。** 理由：JiuwenSwarm 是产品不是 SDK（包名 `workswarm`，版本 `0.2.5.beta1`，无公开 API 声明）。把 import 点收敛到一个目录，漂移的爆炸半径就是那个目录；每块可以独立决策、独立回滚；agent-core 保持独立可见。 ### 3.2 进程拓扑 ```mermaid flowchart TB UI["apps/web（React，不变）"] UI -->|"REST + SSE，37 类事件"| API subgraph API["sd-api（Node，:4310，保留）"] A1["http/ · store.ts · 静态托管"] A2["设置 / 模型 / 用量 / MCP 治理 / 权限 / 插件"] A3["agent-client（新增）：驱动 sd-agent"] A4["internal（新增）：科学域服务路由"] end subgraph AGENT["sd-agent（Python，新增）"] L0["L0：import openjiuwen

`sd-api` 的 REST/SSE 契约**不变**；`sd-api` 与 `sd-agent` 之间用**本项目自定义的窄契约**（不实现 JiuwenSwarm 的 148 个 `ReqMethod`）；科学域服务沿用现有的环回 + 内部 token；JiuwenSwarm 的接触面只有 `adapters/swarm/`。 --- ## 四、代码结构与迁移映射 ### 4.1 新增 `services/agent/` ``` services/agent/ ├── pyproject.toml │ dependencies = [ "openjiuwen==" ] ← L0 硬依赖 │ optional-dependencies: │ swarm-skill / swarm-hub = [ "workswarm==" ] ← L1 按块可选 ├── scripts/check_layers.py ← 分层护栏 └── src/sciencediscovery_agent/ ├── runtime/ ═ L0：只 import openjiuwen ═ │ assembly.py（DeepAgentConfig → create_deep_agent） │ session.py · events.py（→ 37 类 SSE）· model.py · permissions.py ├── context/ ═ L0：上下文三语义 ═ │ processors.py（register_processor） │ window.py（register_window_mutator） │ projections.py（active_skills / plan_state / trust 标注） ├── science/ ═ L2：只依赖 ports/ ═ │ rails/（证据门禁 · 评审检查点 · 溯源记录） │ tools/（执行 · 证据 · 图谱 · 论文） │ explore/（Provider 实现：PUCT / idea-tree） ├── ports/ ═ L1 抽象：纯 Protocol，零依赖 ═ │ skill_store · skill_hub · sandbox · session_store · scheduler ├── adapters/ │ native/ ═ 兜底实现，不依赖 JiuwenSwarm ═ │ swarm/ ═ ★ 唯一允许 import jiuwenswarm ═ └── transport/ ═ 与 sd-api 的窄契约 ═ ``` `check_layers.py` 六条断言进 CI： 1. `runtime/` `context/` `science/` 不得出现 `import jiuwenswarm` 2. `ports/` 不得 import `openjiuwen` 与 `jiuwenswarm`（纯 Protocol） 3. `adapters/native/` 不得 import `jiuwenswarm` 4. `adapters/swarm/` 是唯一允许的目录 5. **每个 `adapters/swarm/.py` 必须有同名的 `adapters/native/.py` 兜底** 6. `science/` 不得 import `adapters/` 第 5 条是关键：没有兜底，「可选」就是假的。 ### 4.2 迁移映射 | 现有 | 行数 | 去向 | 替代者 | |---|---:|---|---| | `packages/runtime-core` | 626 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/single_agent` + `core/runner` | | `packages/context` | 2,439 | ❌ 删，语义迁 `sd-agent/context/` | L0 `core/context_engine` 23,999 | | `packages/model` | 1,465 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/foundation/llm` | | `packages/tools` + `workspace`（工具部分） | 约 3,400 | ❌ 删 | L0 `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `packages/specialist` + `orchestration` + `plan` | 3,190 | ❌ 删 | L0 `agent_teams` + `harness/rails` | | 外壳成为 `internal/` 域服务 | — | | `packages/schema` `mcp` `mcp-sources` `skill` `plugin-sdk` `executor` `sandbox-capability` | 约 13,000 | ✅ 保留 Node | — | | `services/api/native-agent` | 1,121 | ❌ 删 | — | | `services/api/{runs,agent-run,bootstrap}` | 5,112 | ◐ 改写为 `sd-agent` 客户端 | — | | `services/api` 其余 | 约 25,000 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `services/runner` | 8,798 | ✅ 保留（M2 可选把隔离原语换成 jiuwenbox） | — | | `services/{evolve,memory-graph,paper,gateway}` | 23,045 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `skills/` 17 个 | 3,641 | ✅ 保留，经 `ports/skill_store` 读取 | — | | `services/launcher` + `scripts/binary-release` | 3,203+ | ◐ payload 增 Python 运行时 | — | | **新增** `services/agent/` | 约 8,000–13,000 | ➕ | — | | **新增** `services/api/src/{agent-client,internal}` | 约 3,500–6,000 | ➕ | — | **后端非测试 TypeScript 82,367 行中，保留约 66,400 行（约 81%）。** --- ## 五、改基础算法的路径（这些缝全部在 agent-core） ### 5.1 上下文组装 `openjiuwen/core/context_engine/` 是完整插件架构：`ModelContext(ABC)`（抽象方法含 `get_context_window()`）、`ContextProcessor`（钩子 `on_add_messages` / `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### 6.2 C 型按块实测 | 块 | 依赖 `common.config` | 依赖 `common.utils` | `sys.path` 副作用 | **C 型等级** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Skill Hub**（`marketplace/hub_client` + 3 个兄弟文件） | **0** | **0** | **无** | **无** | | **Skill 文件/归档原语**（`skill_files` `archive_store`） | 0 | 0 | 无 | **无** | | **jiuwenbox** | 0 | 0 | 无（本机 HTTP 服务） | **无** | | cron store | 0 | 1（一个路径函数） | 无 | **低** | | **Skill 包管理**（`skill_manager.py` 8,841 行） | **4** | 1 | **有** | **高** | | 会话存储 / 项目 Git | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高**（且与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 双主） | | 产品 rails / tools | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高** | 由此修订接入策略： - **Skill Hub**：四个文件干净到可以直接 import，也可以照抄（Apache-2.0）。零 C 型侵入。 - **jiuwenbox**：**它已经是独立组件**——自带 `pyproject.toml`（`name = "jiuwenbox"`），依赖只有 pydantic/pyyaml/httpx/fastapi/uvicorn/python-multipart/mcp，**不依赖 `workswarm`**，Python 代码对 `jiuwenswarm` 零引用；JiuwenSwarm 自己也是通过 HTTP 调它。我们可以 `pip install "jiuwenbox @ git+#subdirectory=jiuwenbox"`，零侵入。 - **cron**：只要一个路径函数。建议照抄 cron 表达式与 store 语义到 `adapters/native/`，不为一个函数引入 `common.utils`。 - **Skill 包管理**：8,841 行会带来全套 C 型侵入。三个选择：① 在 `sd-agent` 独立进程里接受它；② 只取 `skill_files` + `archive_store` 两个干净原语，打包逻辑自己写；③ 不接。 - **会话存储**：明确不接，避免与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 形成双主；会话回溯用 L0 的 `core/session/vcs` 底座自己做产品化。 **新增设计约束**：`adapters/swarm/` 每个适配器要在文件头声明它拖进来的 C 型侵入，由 `check_layers.py` 校验声明与实际 import 一致；未声明的 import 直接失败。 ### 6.3 A 型：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 源码的场景，已缩到 2 条 本方案下**不再适用**的四条：新增 `ReqMethod`（我们不跑 AgentServer）、改 `agent_adapter`（我们自己装配）、换协作调度内核（走 agent-core 的 seam）、复用 JiuwenSwarm 前端组件（前端用我们自己的）。 仍然适用的： | # | 场景 | 触发条件 | 处置 | |---|---|---|---| | **A1** | jiuwenbox 增加 macOS 隔离后端 | 要保住 macOS 源码模式**同时**采用 jiuwenbox（jiuwenbox 目前 Linux-only；我们的 `seatbelt.ts` 在 47 个文件被引用） | 上游 PR；或不采用 jiuwenbox，继续用 `services/runner` | | **A2** | `skill_manager` 解耦工作区与全局 config | 要接 Skill 包管理，且不接受 6.1 的 C 型侵入 | 上游 PR（改为构造参数注入）；短期用 6.2 的选择② | 另有 A3（`common/config.py` 去掉导入期 `sys.path` 变更）只在「后端完全合并为单一 Python 进程」的形态下出现；本方案的 Node + sidecar 形态天然规避。 ### 6.4 B 型：建议向上游提出的扩展点 | # | 对象 | 诉求 | 不给的代价 | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider` 与 `ContextEngine.register_processor` 的**覆盖生效时机窗口** | 改基础算法只能依赖未文档化的时机 | | B2 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_window_mutator` 在处理器链中的**执行点** | 窗口权威降级为尽力而为 | | B3 | JiuwenSwarm | 给出**可外部复用模块清单**并脱离 beta | `adapters/swarm/` 全部建立在内部模块上 | | B4 | JiuwenSwarm | **Skill Hub HTTP API 版本化**（现有 `hub_asset_port.py` 是 Python 端口稳定声明，HTTP 层无版本） | 被动跟随；最坏退回本地库 | | B5 | JiuwenSwarm | `skill_manager` 路径/config **改为注入式** | 见 A2 | | B6 | JiuwenSwarm | `common/config.py` 提供**无副作用导入模式** | 单进程形态下有静默 shadow 风险 | | B7 | JiuwenSwarm | jiuwenbox 发布到 PyPI | 便利性诉求，可用 git 子目录安装替代 | **B1、B2 最该优先推动**——「改基础算法」的能力完全取决于它们。 ### 6.5 反向：我们会不会侵入 JiuwenSwarm 不会，且是结构性的：单向依赖（`workswarm` 按 extra 引入、jiuwenbox 按本机服务引入），JiuwenSwarm 对我们零依赖；我们不跑它的进程、不实现它的协议、不改它的配置语义。若要贡献科学能力，走 Rail 插件 / Skill / MCP 的正向 PR，对它是加法。 --- ## 七、工作量 估算口径：同语言搬运约 800–1,500 行/人周；跨语言重写含测试约 250–400 行/人周；协议与语义对齐按耦合点计。不含产品需求变更与跨团队协同开销。**未做原型验证，第 0 阶段完成后需重新校准。** | 阶段 | 内容 | 乐观 | 可能 | 悲观 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | M0-a | 证伪 spike（四个判据，见第八节） | 2 | 3 | 5 | | M0-b | `sd-agent` 骨架 + `sd-api` 的 `agent-client` + 37 类事件映射 | 10 | 14 | 22 | | M0-c | 分层护栏、`ports/` 定稿、`adapters/native/` 兜底 | 3 | 4 | 6 | | M1-a | 工具面迁移 + 13,675 行域包加 HTTP 外壳 | 12 | 17 | 26 | | M1-b | 上下文三语义 + 证据门禁与评审检查点 | 6 | 9 | 15 | | M1-c | 科学探索 Provider（PUCT / idea-tree） | 8 | 12 | 20 | | M2-a~d | 按块接 JiuwenSwarm（Hub / Skill 包 / jiuwenbox / cron） | 15 | 22 | 36 | | M3-a | 分发：Python 运行时进单可执行文件 payload（双架构）、Docker | 8 | 11 | 17 | | M3-b | 测试与 CI：增 Python 层；E2E 大部保留（REST/SSE 与 Web 不变） | 6 | 9 | 14 | | **合计（M2 全接）** | | **70** | **101** | **161 人周** | | **不接任何 JiuwenSwarm 块** | | **55** | **79** | **125 人周** | **M2 各块彼此独立**，可以只接 Skill Hub 不接 jiuwenbox，或反过来。这是本方案与「整体二选一」的主要差别：**JiuwenSwarm 从一次性决策变成逐块定价**。 **不可逆点**：M1-a 完成后，工具实现不再留在 Node 侧。M0 全程可回滚。 --- ## 八、第 0 阶段的证伪判据 | # | 判据 | 决定什么 | |---|---|---| | ① | `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: 后端迁移设计——agent-core 作为独立依赖层，JiuwenSwarm 按块复用（架构、代码结构与侵入分析）

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

Nightly trial run [38107013490](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38107013490) (real model, built-in agent loop) was cancelled by hand during its fourth journey. By then three of its ten journeys had already failed: DRB-59, DRB-64 and DRB-58, each after 83–90 minutes. Nothing that was uploaded says why:

- The job log (and `run.log`) has one `✘` line per journey, and no error.
- Each journey report says **FAIL** with "0 / 0 steps passed", and no error.
- `test-results/` is missing. That is where `benchmark-metrics.json` (run status, delivery, error, sub-agents), `error-context.md` and the trace would be. `summary.txt` is missing too.

What could be reconstructed from `stack.log` timing alone: DRB-58 used up its 90-minute run budget. DRB-59 and DRB-64 ended on their own after 83–84 minutes, well inside their 120-minute budget, and then failed at the delivery assertion. Whether those two runs failed, or completed without a readable report, can no longer be told.

## Why

1. **Per-test evidence is copied only on exit.** Playwright writes `test-results/` to `.e2e/test-results`, which is outside the uploaded results directory. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` copies it there only in its EXIT trap. When a job is cancelled, the runner sends SIGINT, then SIGTERM about 7.5 s later, then kills the process tree about 2.5 s after that. bash runs the trap only once Playwright has exited, and Playwright was still tearing down the running journey: its `finally` alone waits up to 30 s for the run to cancel. So the copy never happens. A job timeout or a lost runner has the same effect.
2. **The `list` reporter prints failure details only when the whole run ends.** As each test ends, it prints just the `✘` line.
3. **Journey reports only record errors raised inside `journey.step()`.** The reports themselves are written into the results as each journey ends, which is why they survived. But the benchmark journeys assert in the test body, so their reports carry no error at all.

## Expected

Every journey that has finished leaves its evidence in the uploaded results at the moment it finishes. Its failure reason can be read in the job log and in its journey report without waiting for the rest of the run, whether or not the run ends normally.

## Proposal

- `run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`, and `test/playwright.config.ts` uses it as `outputDir` (falling back to `.e2e/test-results`). The exit trap then copies only the HTML report, which Playwright renders once the run ends anyway.
- A journey report that failed without a failed step gets a "failure reason" section from `testInfo.errors`. It is redacted and truncated like step errors already are.
- When a journey fails, print the first lines of its error after its `journey report (FAIL)` line: the assertion message and expected/received, without the stack, and redacted.

Not in scope: for a cancelled layer, the shared-plan summary still reports "no frozen plan reported … the layer stopped before it collected its tests", because the shared runner writes its accounting only after Playwright exits. With the evidence above, a cancelled run can be diagnosed regardless.

Related: #233 (a delivery failure does not carry the run's own error).
closed_recent.title: bug(e2e): A cancelled or killed E2E run loses the failure evidence of journeys that already finished

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

A real research run that has already been working can stop because the model gateway rejects one tool call whose arguments do not parse. The same happens to a subagent that has already finished its work. The page then tells the user to check the model configuration.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-59** ran for 20.2 minutes. Both subagents completed. The session contained `navigation_cues_summary.md`, `navigation_cues_sources.json`, `disturbance_summary.md`, and `disturbance_sources.json`, and the page showed 167K usage. The required `deepresearchbench-59.md` was not among them. The final answer was empty and the run status was `failed`.

The request error on the failure page was:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell); gateway request chatcmpl-a2101146-60b8-4549-a033-1fe6f70bcfa0
```

The same DRB-59 passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) in 1.3 hours. The gateway and model id had already completed two subagents in the failing run.

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), the same failure ended two more journeys, once on an MCP tool rather than `run_shell`. All three events below are logged as `"truncated":false` in the server log's `[model-arguments]` line. The server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Where it failed | Gateway request | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | Main run, after 23 minutes. Both subagents had completed, and the main agent had just said it would write the report. | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `run_shell` | Run `failed`, empty final answer. The session had three files from the subagents (two source packages and coverage notes); the required `deepresearchbench-64.md` was never declared. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt. Its `deliverable_check` MCP call had already returned `ok: true`; it failed while writing `signoff.json`. | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `run_shell` | Subagent `failed`. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt, on its `deliverable_check` call, which was to carry the full 26,226-byte report. | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | MCP `deliverable_check` | Subagent `failed`. The checker never received the call. |

In TC-E2E-01 all five research specialists had completed within 37 minutes and `evidence_brief.md` (26,226 bytes) existed. The two signoff failures and their re-dispatches used the remaining time; the third signoff attempt was still running when the 55-minute test budget ran out, and the test cancelled the run, which had no final answer. How the test reports a run cut off by its budget is #239.

## Why one call ends the run

Code at `90db5b8e`; these files are unchanged on main at `9189206d`.

1. `packages/model/src/client.ts` parses each assembled tool call with `JSON.parse` ([L221-L230](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L221-L230)) and sets `argsParseError` on failure.
2. In the JiuwenSwarm model gateway, `rejectInvalidArguments` ([L220-L228](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L220-L228)) lets truncated turns through to the output-limit recovery, but throws for any non-truncated call with `argsParseError`. The gateway answers that turn with an error (an SSE error event once streaming has started, otherwise HTTP 502). Swarm does not retry the turn, and `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` ([L363-L367](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L363-L367)) turns it into the error of the run or subagent.
3. `classifyRunFailure` ([services/api/src/run-failure.ts L28-L49](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/run-failure.ts#L28-L49)) matches none of its markers for this message and falls through to `semantic-error`. The Web UI renders that class as `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`: "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry."

The same condition is handled three different ways:

- Native runtime: `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` ([L334-L338](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/tools/src/registry.ts#L334-L338)) returns `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` with `retryable: true` to the model as a tool result, and the model can re-issue the call.
- Swarm, truncated call: the calls are withheld and the turn goes through bounded output-limit recovery. In Nightly 37875334064 two such events (03:57 and 04:42 UTC) did not end their runs, and those journeys (DRB-58, DRB-62) passed.
- Swarm, non-truncated call: the run or subagent fails.

Passing the call through unchanged would be worse: the gateway re-serializes calls from their parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`, [L123-L125](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L123-L125)), so Swarm would execute the tool with `{}`.

## Where it fails: in ScienceDiscovery, before JiuwenSwarm sees the call

Every model request from JiuwenSwarm passes two ScienceDiscovery layers before it reaches the provider:

```text
JiuwenSwarm -> adapter /llm/<token>/v1/chat/completions (services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py)
            -> Node model gateway (services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts)
            -> packages/model client -> provider
```

`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` points Swarm's model at `modelGateway.url` ([L555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L555)), and the adapter route forwards to that URL. The gateway drops the whole turn before Swarm receives the tool call. Swarm only gets an error for its model request; it does not retry that request, and its agent loop ends.

JiuwenSwarm's own handling would not end the run. JiuwenSwarm `workswarm0.2.6` pins agent-core (`openjiuwen`) at `ad0c9dfb`, whose `openjiuwen/core/single_agent/ability_manager.py` parses tool arguments in `_parse_tool_arguments_with_repair`: `json.loads`, then a bracket-balancing repair, and if both fail `execute` raises `AbilityExecutionError` whose `ToolMessage` (`Invalid tool arguments JSON: …`) is returned to the model as the tool result, "so it can self-correct". The native ScienceDiscovery runtime does the same with `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`.

A second ScienceDiscovery layer would reject the same call for platform tools. The adapter's `StreamingToolRewriter` parses the complete arguments of each platform tool with `json.loads` at `finish_reason` to append the run tag ([L328](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L328)), and on failure ends the stream with `invalid streamed platform tool arguments` ([L362-L366](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L362-L366)). It was not reached in these runs because the gateway had already stopped the turn. Simply passing the call through to Swarm would hit this layer, and would also put unparseable arguments into the history replayed to the provider.

## Expected

- A non-truncated call whose arguments do not parse is not executed, and the model is told which call failed and why so that it can re-issue it, with a bounded number of attempts (the same shape as the truncated-call recovery, or a bounded re-sample in the gateway). One bad call does not end a run that has been working for 20 to 40 minutes, and does not fail a subagent that has already finished its work.
- This holds for every tool, including MCP tools, in the main run and in subagents.
- If recovery is exhausted, the run error says that the model produced an invalid tool call, with the tool name and gateway request id. The user-facing text does not tell the user to check the model configuration when the same model has already been calling tools in that run.
- The Actions log for the journey includes this error instead of only `delivery.status` `"failed"` (#233).

## Evidence limits

Neither Nightly captured the raw argument strings or the parser messages, so whether the model emitted malformed JSON or the stream assembler lost part of the arguments is not known. Making that distinguishable is #246.

> Complements the still-open #46 (its release-link, verification, ordering, and naming
> asks are tracked there). Related: #1, #27, #29, #35, #38.

## Summary

The rewritten READMEs now answer two of the onboarding questions at the README level. They
name release 0.2.0 and the arm64 asset, so a reader can obtain the binary, and the
Requirements table maps the binary, source, and Docker paths to host requirements. What
remains sits in the deployment guide and in one link convention. The three-mode comparison
still has no operating-system column, so the OS facts are scattered across the local-mode,
Docker, and artifact-name lines. The binary section still opens by building from source,
with no walkthrough from a published release asset to `serve`. Binary and local modes have
no first-run troubleshooting block, while Docker does. And the README download command
pins a version and a filename, so the command goes stale at the next release. Neither
README states that the prebuilt binary is the shortest path and that the other modes are
in the deployment guide, and the deployment guide never states what it is for.
I would like those things fixed, in both languages.

## Current state

- `README.md` and `README_zh.md` are both 103 lines. The installation section (README line
  24, paragraph to line 36) names release 0.2.0 (line 26), gives a fixed-version download
  command (lines 29-31), distinguishes the local service token from a model API key (line
  34), and mentions the arm64 asset, Bubblewrap as the only host dependency, and the
  deployment guide for source and Docker (line 36). The Requirements section (line 71,
  table lines 73-77, columns Path and Host requirements) already maps the three paths to
  operating systems.
- The deployment guide is 443 lines in English and 451 in Chinese. It opens with a
  three-mode comparison (EN lines 5-15, header line 7). The table columns are Mode, What
  the user receives, Host dependencies, and Intended use. No column states supported
  operating systems.
- Operating-system support is scattered. The binary artifact names appear at lines 24-25,
  local mode states Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x64/arm64 at line 147, and the Docker
  prerequisites state Linux x86_64 or aarch64 at line 189.
- The binary section opens with `### Build and run` (line 19) and teaches building the
  artifact from source. Nothing walks a reader from a published release asset to `serve`.
- The local service token versus a model API key is explained in the README (line 34) and
  the quick start (`docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md`, line 44). Token rejection
  recovery appears in the quick start (line 30) and in the Docker FAQ (deployment guide line 406),
  but the installation section does not link a recovery passage directly. #35 shows the
  confusion is real.
- The guide's only FAQ-style troubleshooting sits inside the Docker section (EN
  `### Frequently asked questions`, line 394, running to the `### Limitations` heading at
  line 426). It covers build failures, data-directory permissions, port conflicts, token
  rejection (line 406), degraded health, and sandbox failures. Binary mode documents
  Bubblewrap (lines 64-77) and local mode carries a Seatbelt note (lines 150 and 177), but
  neither mode has an FAQ covering token rejection, degraded health, or port conflicts.
  The quick start explains a `degraded` status at line 38 without linking a recovery
  passage.
- Neither README frames the prebuilt binary as the shortest path; line 36 only notes that
  source and Docker are covered in the deployment guide. The deployment guide opens by
  pointing back at the README's shortest path (line 3), but never states what the guide
  itself is for, so a reader has to infer why they would open it.
- #1 asked how to obtain the binary. The rewritten README now names release 0.2.0 and the
  fixed-version download command, so that question is answered at the README level. #46
  asked for release links, SHA-256 verification instructions, a deployment guide led by
  downloading rather than building, and aligned configuration entry names. The decision
  and recovery layers above are still open.

## What to write

1. Add a supported-operating-systems column to the three-mode comparison in both
   deployment guides (binary: Linux x86_64/aarch64, source: Linux and macOS, Docker:
   Linux).
2. Lead the binary section with downloading a published release asset, then give the
   build-from-source procedure.
3. Add a first-run troubleshooting block for binary and local modes (Docker already has
   one), covering at least token rejection and where the Connection settings live, a
   `degraded` health status, a missing `bwrap`, and where the logs are. Link it from the
   README or the quick start.
4. Change the README download command (lines 29-31) to point at the generic Releases page,
   or use clearly labeled version and architecture placeholders and explain how to choose
   the asset from the Release page.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

The `CI` workflow executes the Node and Python unit tests twice.

1. The `UT` job runs `pnpm ci:ut`. That is the gate: with the tagged test plan from #126 it runs the UT slice of the shared plan, selected from source tags and a fixed profile, with every Node test file in a worker of its own and the Python suites through the plan's pytest adapter. The job fails unless every planned case executes and passes. It records no coverage.
2. The `Coverage` job then checks the repository out again and runs `pnpm coverage:node` and `node scripts/run-python-coverage.mjs`, which execute the unit tests a second time under instrumentation. With the plan from #126 they select the very same cases the gate just ran. On a pull request the second run covers only the directories the diff touched; on the nightly schedule it repeats the whole suite.

The second run costs a full test execution per pipeline, and it is a second execution path. The numbers it reports describe a run that is not the one that gated the change. Whenever the two paths differ in how they execute a test — process isolation, interpreter setup, which cases a directory contains — the coverage run passes or fails on its own terms, independently of the gate. Two concrete ways this goes wrong:

- Running a Python service's whole test directory executes cases the gate's profile deliberately leaves out, such as the `status:external` cases in `services/memory-graph` that need a live Neo4j. On a runner without Neo4j those fail the Coverage job while the gate is green.
- Running a directory's Node test files in one shared process lets files interfere with each other's globals. The gate runs each file in its own worker, so cases that pass in the gate can fail under coverage.

## Expected behaviour

- The job that runs the plan records coverage while it runs it. Node workers run with `--experimental-test-coverage` in the same per-file isolation the gate already uses; the Python suites run with `coverage run` in front of the same pytest invocation.
- That job uploads the coverage data as an artifact.
- The `Coverage` job depends on it, downloads the artifact, merges the data and writes the summary. It executes no test. If the producing job failed, the summary is built from whatever was uploaded and states that the job failed; nothing is re-run to fill the gap.
- Pull requests and the nightly run report on exactly the plan the gate ran. There is no separate diff-based selection of what to measure.
- ST and the mocked browser E2E do not load product modules into a measured process, so they contribute no module coverage. The summary says so instead of reporting numbers for them.
- Test selection does not change: source tags and a fixed profile, never the runner's services, credentials or host.

## Acceptance

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no step in the `Coverage` job that runs a test command.
- The coverage files the `Coverage` job reports on come from the gate job's own run.
- A local run of the UT layer produces the same coverage files, and the reporting command runs on them without executing any test.

### 🚀 Background Description


The coverage job currently generates and uploads Node.js and Python JSON summary artifacts, but the Actions run page does not expose the results directly. Contributors must download artifacts to see what was scanned and the aggregate coverage, unlike E2E results that are visible in the run summary.

This feature should make coverage results visible without introducing a minimum percentage gate.

### Design Ideas

Write a repository-owned Markdown renderer to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` from the existing `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Show Node.js and Python separately.
- Label full, incremental, skipped, failed, or unavailable scans.
- Show measured files/groups and available line, branch, and function totals.
- List selected groups for incremental scans.
- Keep coverage informational: no minimum percentage.
- Preserve current failure semantics and artifact uploads.

### Involved Public APIs

None. This changes only GitHub Actions reporting and repository-owned CI scripts.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The change touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the existing Node.js/Python coverage scripts and selector rules, and the operational CI contract in `.ci/README.md`. Runtime APIs and product behavior are unaffected.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Unit-test the summary renderer for full, incremental, skipped, failed, and unavailable results.
- Test that changes to the renderer select full Node.js and Python coverage.
- Parse the workflow YAML after editing.
- Run the WSL build, recursive workspace tests, and architecture checks.
- Confirm coverage remains informational and coverage test failures still fail the job.

An implementation is prepared on `wyhohyw:codex/coverage-actions-summary`; a Draft PR will link this issue.

### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery contains maintained Python services whose tests are not represented by the Node.js coverage percentage. A Node-only number must not be presented as whole-repository coverage.

This issue adds a separate Python coverage pipeline using mature Python tooling. It complements the Node.js coverage issue #137 while keeping the two languages' commands, reports, and scope independently auditable.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Use `coverage.py` as the coverage engine; do not implement a custom Python tracer.
- Preserve existing test frameworks:
  - `services/gateway` and `services/paper`: `unittest`
  - `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve`: `pytest`
- Run each existing suite under `coverage run --branch --parallel-mode`, then use `coverage combine`.
- Measure production source directories, not test files.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines and branches. Keep service/path groups separate.

### CI execution

- Reuse existing CI and nightly workflows rather than adding a standalone coverage workflow.
- PR/default-branch runs should select affected Python services where the dependency/selector mapping is reliable. A partial run must be explicitly marked partial and must never be displayed as whole-Python coverage.
- The existing nightly run should execute the complete Python coverage scope and publish the authoritative baseline.
- Coverage remains informational initially; existing test failures still fail the job.

### Reports and artifact

- Generate `coverage.py` JSON as the structured source consumed by the board.
- Optionally generate Cobertura XML for future GitHub Code Quality integration and LCOV/HTML for local diagnosis, without making a paid GitHub feature a prerequisite.
- Upload one SHA-qualified Actions artifact containing aggregate and per-service JSON summaries plus run identity metadata.
- Use repository default artifact retention.

### Dashboard

- Display Node.js and Python coverage as separate first-class metrics.
- If an overall line percentage is shown, compute it from summed covered/total lines:
  `(node covered + python covered) / (node total + python total)`.
- Never average percentages directly.
- Label nightly baselines as authoritative and partial/incremental results explicitly.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

This feature adds an internal Python coverage artifact contract. It should align with the Node summary's run/SHA/mode/group metadata while retaining Python-specific metrics and source paths.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/gateway` and `services/paper` keep their existing `unittest` commands.
- `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve` keep their existing `pytest` commands and extras.
- CI test selection and nightly scheduling determine whether the result is partial or authoritative.
- The status board consumes the structured Actions artifact; it does not run Python tests itself.
- GitHub Code Quality can consume Cobertura XML later, but this feature must work without enabling the paid service.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add focused coverage runs for every maintained Python service and verify existing tests still execute with the same pass/fail semantics.
- Test combining parallel coverage data from `unittest` and `pytest` environments.
- Verify branch coverage is enabled and test files are excluded from production totals.
- Verify missing/failed service runs cannot produce an authoritative aggregate.
- Verify partial PR results and complete nightly baselines have distinct metadata.
- Validate JSON totals against `coverage report` for representative services.
- Add board parser/rendering tests for Python-only, Node-only, combined, missing, and stale artifacts.
- Verify overall coverage uses summed covered/total values, not the arithmetic mean of percentages.
- Run the complete repository test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- Node.js coverage tracking: #137
- Node.js WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- coverage.py documentation: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/

Non-goals: migrating all Python tests to one framework, implementing a custom coverage engine, or requiring GitHub Code Quality/another paid service.

closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery runs Node.js tests in CI but does not yet publish a durable, machine-readable coverage result tied to the exact workflow run and commit. Maintainers should be able to inspect coverage in GitHub Actions, while the status board should consume the same CI evidence without running tests itself or parsing unstable console text.

This issue covers **Node.js coverage only**. Python coverage should be tracked separately so that the tools, test commands, scope, and percentages remain explicit.

The current work-in-progress implementation is PR #134.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Reuse the repository's existing built Node.js tests; do not introduce another test tier or migrate test frameworks.
- Run them with Node.js 22's built-in `--experimental-test-coverage` collector (V8 coverage).
- Group results by workspace/path and keep repository CI-script tests as explicit groups.
- Exclude test sources from production-source totals.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines, branches, and functions rather than storing percentages alone.

### CI execution

- Integrate coverage into the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; do not add a second coverage workflow.
- For pull requests and default-branch pushes, select changed Node.js workspaces and their transitive dependents. Changes to shared coverage infrastructure select every group.
- Reuse the existing nightly workflow for a complete, authoritative all-group baseline.
- Skip coverage for release-only calls.
- Test failures still fail the job. Coverage percentages are informational initially and do not introduce a new threshold gate.

### Actions artifact

- Generate LCOV only as a local intermediate.
- Upload one SHA-qualified artifact containing aggregate and per-group JSON summaries.
- Include source SHA, base SHA, generation time, mode (`incremental` or `full`), selected groups, and whether the result is authoritative.
- Use the repository's default artifact retention; do not introduce independent 30/90-day policies.

### Status-board consumption

- The board downloads the structured summary through the GitHub Actions Artifacts API. It does not execute tests and does not infer coverage from log text.
- Show the latest full nightly baseline, per-path line/branch/function coverage, nightly history, and recent PR affected-group results.
- A homepage value composed from later default-branch group summaries must be labelled as an estimate until the next full nightly run recalibrates it.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

The feature adds an internal CI artifact contract for coverage summaries. Consumers must treat the run identity, SHA, mode, selected groups, and authoritative flag as part of that contract.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Existing CI and nightly workflows provide the execution environment.
- Existing Node workspace dependency metadata is used to expand changed workspaces to transitive dependents.
- The companion status board reads the Actions artifact and renders the coverage page.
- Browser/TSX, Python, and Playwright coverage are explicitly excluded from this issue and must not be represented as covered by the Node percentage.
- GitHub Code Quality/Cobertura upload can be evaluated separately; it is not required for the initial board integration.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add selector tests for changed workspaces, transitive dependents, shared-infrastructure full selection, and irrelevant-path skips.
- Add aggregation tests that exclude test sources and preserve aggregate and per-group covered/total values.
- Validate that PR/default-branch CI publishes affected-group summaries from the existing CI workflow.
- Validate that nightly publishes a complete authoritative baseline without a second workflow.
- Verify that every artifact is tied to its workflow run/SHA and contains only the structured JSON required by consumers.
- Verify that test failures still fail the coverage job.
- Add status-board tests distinguishing authoritative nightly data, incremental/PR data, estimates, and UT/ST/E2E artifacts.
- Run the repository's complete existing test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- Design in the implementation branch: `docs/designs/test-coverage.v3.md`

Acceptance boundary: the resulting percentage covers built Node.js workspace tests and repository CI-script tests only. It must never be presented as whole-repository coverage.

## Summary

ScienceMemory currently only works if the user installs and runs an external **Neo4j 5.x** server. That is a heavy prerequisite for what is, in most local runs, a small per-session graph. I would like a **fallback backend that persists the graph as plain text files on the local disk** and is used automatically when Neo4j is not configured or not reachable, with Neo4j kept as the opt-in backend for larger/shared deployments.

## Current behaviour

Per `docs/en/how-to/science-memory-setup.md`:

- None of the three deployment modes (single-file binary, Docker, source local mode) bundle Neo4j — ScienceMemory "needs an external Neo4j server".
- The user has to either run `docker run ... neo4j:5` or add the Neo4j apt/dnf repo and `systemctl enable --now neo4j`, then set an initial password and fill in HTTP address / user / password in System configuration → Memory.
- Until that is done, the feature stays off: health reports `needs-password`, or `degraded` when Neo4j is unreachable, and nothing is recorded.

In code the coupling is total: everything under `services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/` speaks Cypher over Neo4j's HTTP Transactional API — roughly 160 `MERGE`/`MATCH` statements in `persistence.py`, 45 in `query.py`, 39 in `search_graph.py`, plus `constraints.py`, all going through the single `Neo4jHandle` in `neo4j_driver.py`.

## Why this is a problem

1. **Install cost is out of proportion to the data.** A typical session's graph is a few hundred Task / ToolCall / Code / Artifact / Paper / WebPage nodes and their edges. Standing up a JVM graph database (plus a container runtime or a distro package + systemd unit + initial password) to hold that is a lot of setup for a single-user local run.
2. **Many target environments cannot do it.** Offline / air-gapped clusters, shared login nodes without root or Docker, corporate laptops with restricted package sources, CI sandboxes — in all of these the documented install paths (Docker Hub pull, `deb.neo4j.com` / `dnf` repo, `sudo systemctl`) are simply unavailable.
3. **Silent degradation makes it look broken.** The graceful degrade is the right default, but the net effect for a new user is that a documented feature quietly records nothing, and the only way out is a multi-step external install.
4. **It blocks the "just try it" path.** Someone evaluating ScienceDiscovery from the binary or `start-stack.sh` cannot see provenance/traceability — the thing ScienceMemory exists to demonstrate — without first becoming a Neo4j operator.

## Proposal

Introduce a storage-backend seam and ship a Neo4j-free default.

1. **Backend interface.** `neo4j_driver.handle` / `session()` is already the single chokepoint that `persistence` / `query` / `constraints` / `search_graph` / `server` go through (the HTTP session deliberately mirrors the Bolt `Session`/`Result`/`Record` surface). Turn that into an explicit backend protocol rather than a Neo4j-specific handle.
2. **Local file backend (new default).** Persist nodes and edges as human-readable text under the existing data directory — e.g. append-only JSONL (`nodes.jsonl`, `edges.jsonl`) per session or per workspace, or a single JSON graph document. This is a good fit because:
   - all writes are already `MERGE` on a unique key and idempotent across retries, so an append log with last-write-wins on the key replays cleanly;
   - the read side is a bounded, known set of queries (session chain, artifact lineage, citation/evidence chain, search), not arbitrary Cypher — they can be served by an in-memory index built from the file on load;
   - the data volume is small enough to hold in memory for the lifetime of the sidecar.
   (If a pure-text file turns out to be too weak for the query side, an embedded SQLite/`kuzu` store would still remove the external-server requirement — but a text format has the extra benefit of being greppable, diffable, and easy to attach to a bug report or commit.)
3. **Selection rules.** Backend chosen by configuration: `local` (default, no credentials needed) vs `neo4j` (current behaviour). When Neo4j is configured but unreachable, either keep degrading as today or fall back to the local backend — whichever the maintainers prefer — but the *unconfigured* case should land on `local` and report `healthy`, not `needs-password`.
4. **Migration / export.** A one-way importer from the local file store into Neo4j, so a user who starts locally and later outgrows it can move their history over.

## Benefits

- ScienceMemory works out of the box in all three deployment modes, with zero external services.
- Works in offline, rootless, and container-less environments.
- The graph becomes inspectable with ordinary tools (`grep`, `jq`, a diff) and easy to share when reporting a problem.
- Neo4j remains available and unchanged for users who want its scale and its browser/query tooling.

## Open questions

- Preferred on-disk format: JSONL append log, single JSON document, or something else already used elsewhere in the repo?
- Scope of the local backend: per-session files, or one store for all sessions with a session index?
- Should the local backend serve the same `/health` states, adding something like `healthy (local)`, or reuse `healthy` as-is?

Happy to prototype the backend seam plus a JSONL implementation if the direction is acceptable.

## Summary

The web UI has a solid i18n system — 2442 English keys and 2441 Chinese ones, with only a `test.englishFallback` key missing — but three places sit outside it. The visible result: **an English-locale user gets a half-Chinese Idea Tree**.

## 1. Idea Tree renders hardcoded Chinese regardless of locale

`detectLocale()` in `apps/web/src/i18n/locale.ts` returns `en` for any browser whose `navigator.languages` does not start with `zh`, so this is the default path for non-Chinese users, not an edge case. These strings are Chinese literals in JSX, never passed through `t()`:

| File | Hardcoded lines | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` | 14 | `重试`, `重新连接`, `暂停`, `继续`, `查看研究进度 →`, `第 {r.round} / {maxRounds} 轮` |
| `IdeaResearchLabels.ts` | 11 | `构思方向与改进`, `设计候选`, `聚合评估`, `已中断`, `正在暂停` |
| `IdeaTreeSettingsEditor.tsx` | 9 | `科研模板`, `通用科研假设探索`, `水处理材料设计`, `快速：少量路径，快速判断` |
| `IdeaTreeExplorer.tsx` | 5 | — |
| `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx` | 5 | `Idea Tree 研究已启动`, `正在读取实时进度…`, `节点 {id}` |
| `IdeaTreeView.tsx` | 1 | `查看旧树（只读） →` |
| `IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx` | 1 | `方向` |

What makes this jarring rather than merely untranslated: **the other half of the same feature is translated.** `ideaTree.phase.preflight_research`, `ideaTree.phase.building_tree`, `ideaTree.maxDepth`, `ideaTree.maxRounds` and friends all live in the catalog. So an English user sees "Building Idea Tree" and "Max depth" next to `暂停`, `继续`, and `第 1 / 5 轮` in the same panel.

Some of these are also inline object literals rather than keys, e.g. in both `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` and `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx`:

```
{running: "执行中", completed: "已完成", stopped: "已停止", failed: "失败"}[activity.status]
```

## 2. `plugins/settings.tsx` implements its own translation mechanism

Eight sites use inline ternaries instead of the catalog:

```
<summary>{zh ? "可选扩展" : "Optional extensions"}</summary>
<option value="enabled">{zh ? "启用" : "Enabled"}</option>
```

and the plugin manifest table carries parallel `name`/`zh` and `description`/`descriptionZh` fields. It works today, but it is a second translation system running beside a 2442-key catalog: new strings land in whichever one the author happens to touch, and nothing keeps the two in sync.

## 3. A reviewable subset of the catalog is untranslated

49 keys have byte-identical English and Chinese values. Many are correct — `Gemini`, `DeepSeek`, `MiniMax`, `OpenAI Chat Completions`, `Anthropic Messages`, `Client ID`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `English`, `{celsius} °C`. But these look like genuine gaps:

- **Memory graph relation labels**, the entire set: `node.relation.produces` = "produces", `.next` = "next", `.extracts` = "extracts", `.supports` = "supports", `.stated_in` = "stated in", `.supersedes` = "supersedes", `.input` = "input". Every edge label in the Chinese memory-graph view is English.
- **Idea Tree prompt labels**: `ideaTree.designPrompt` = "Designer prompt", `.assessorPrompt` = "Assessor system prompt", `.aggregatorPrompt` = "Aggregator prompt".
- **Common nouns**: `settings.skills` / `search.skills` / `settings.groups.skills.label` / `skillManager.tabSkills` = "Skills"; `runtime.status.runner` / `runnerWorkspaces.runnerLabel` = "Runner"; `remote.runnersTitle` = "Runners"; `subagent.role` = "SubAgent"; `skillManager.eyebrow` = "Agent Skills".
- **Interpolated labels**: `app.epoch` = "Epoch {id}", `skillLibrary.head` = "Head {id}", `settings.skillLibraryHead` = "Head {version}", `runnerWorkspaces.agentId` = "Agent {id}", `subagent.tokens` = "{count} tokens", `csv.schemaVersion` = "schema v{version}", `evolve.chart.rollout` = "rollout".

## Reproduction

1. Open the UI in a browser whose language is not Chinese (or set the language switch to English).
2. Start an Idea Tree research run.
3. The research card, timeline card, and Idea Tree settings render Chinese labels and buttons.

## Suggested fix

1. Move every user-visible Idea Tree string into `messages.ts` and call `t()`, including the inline status maps in `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` and `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx` and the label maps in `IdeaResearchLabels.ts`.
2. Fold `plugins/settings.tsx` into the catalog, and decide whether plugin manifests should carry per-locale display names or catalog keys.
3. Translate the subset in §3 — the `node.relation.*` set in particular, since it is every edge label in the memory graph.
4. **Add a guard.** The repository already runs static checks via `pnpm architecture:check` (`scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, `scripts/component-boundaries.mjs`). A check in the same spirit — fail on a CJK string literal in `apps/web/src/**/*.tsx` outside `i18n/` and outside comments — would keep this from coming back. Today that check would flag 45 lines across 7 files, all listed above.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Idea Tree feature renders fully in English under the `en` locale and fully in Chinese under `zh-CN`.
- [ ] No user-visible string bypasses the message catalog (plugin settings included).
- [ ] The `node.relation.*` labels are translated.
- [ ] A static check fails the build when a new hardcoded CJK literal appears in a component.

## Summary

Docs describe adding a **custom MCP server**, but ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** has no settings surface for it and the documented HTTP routes return **404**. End-to-end custom MCP cannot be demoed on this binary.

## Repro

1. Local ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 (`http://127.0.0.1:4310`).
2. Open **System configuration**. Groups present include Global defaults, Sandbox network, Network proxies, Skills, Specialists, Permissions, Connection, etc.
3. There is **no** “MCP servers / Custom / Add server” item. Bundle strings have no `mcp/servers`, `Add server`, or `Custom MCP`.
4. **Network proxies** only lists bundled sources (`biomed`, `uniprot`) and **Add proxy server** — not an MCP server.
5. Authenticated API:
   - `GET /api/mcp/servers` → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
   - `POST /api/mcp/servers` (trivial stdio body) → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
6. Contrast: `GET /api/mcp/sources` returns the 12 bundled connectors (all `unavailable` with empty `availableTools` on this instance — separate readiness bug, see #325).

Docs that claim the feature: [Configure custom MCP](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/advanced-setup/configure-custom-mcp.html).

Observed during Scenario 2 Case C (project **自定义扩展演示**), recorded 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Either ship a working custom-MCP settings page + `/api/mcp/servers` CRUD matching the docs, **or**
- Document that custom MCP is not in 0.2.0 and hide/relabel the docs until it ships.

## Actual

UI and API for user-added MCP servers are absent (404). Users following the docs hit a dead end.

## Priority

**High** among functional gaps for “custom extension” journeys — blocks the whole Case C path.

## Related

- #325 — Session-enabled bundled connectors do not expose MCP tools (catalog/readiness)
- Distinct from proxy policy under Network proxies

## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
items.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable
