## Summary

The README is the first and often only page a visitor reads, and right now it does not do the three jobs it should: **say clearly what this is and who it is for, summarize the core capabilities in a scannable form, and hand the reader a path into the tutorials.** I would like it reworked around those three.

## Current state

`README.md` and `README_zh.md` are 57 lines each: intro sentence → security warning → Project positioning → Features → Related documents → Requirements → Installation → Quick start → License.

Concrete problems:

1. **The pitch is one sentence, and the second thing a visitor reads is a disclaimer.** Line 3 carries the whole value proposition; lines 7–8 are a `[!WARNING]` block about loopback binding, bearer tokens, TLS termination, and sandbox boundaries. That warning is correct and should stay in the README — but placing it above everything else means a first-time reader meets the caveats before they have any idea what the product does.

2. **"Project positioning" does not describe positioning, and the two languages disagree.** The English section is an architecture paragraph ("A browser UI communicates with a Node control API. Each agent run is driven by a Python Gateway…"). The Chinese section at the same position is a **verbatim copy of the intro sentence at line 12**. So one language repeats itself and the other answers a different question entirely.

3. **The feature list is dense prose with no links and an unsourced number.** Four bullets, each a 2–3 line paragraph. None of them links to anything — not a doc, not a tutorial, not a screenshot. The claim "over 300 cross-domain Skills" appears **only in the two READMEs and nowhere else in the repository or docs**, while `skills/` ships 18. Whatever the 300 refers to, a reader cannot verify it or find out how to reach those skills.

4. **No visuals at all.** Both READMEs contain zero images (`grep -c '!\['` → 0), while `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures — `project.png`, `task.png`, `model.png`, `skill.png`, `connector.png`, `permission.png`, `memory.png`, `quotas.png`, `evidence1–4.jpg`, and more. A product whose pitch is "watch the whole research workflow and trace every deliverable" shows the reader nothing.

5. **Exactly one tutorial link, buried at line 51 of 57**, mid-paragraph, after a `curl` health check. Nothing in the Features section points at how to actually try any of those features.

6. **The Installation section is a stub.** In full: "Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide." It never says where to get an executable — which is precisely what [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) asked.

## Proposal

Restructure both READMEs to this order:

1. **Title + one-line pitch + badges.** One sentence a researcher recognizes themselves in. Keep the existing positioning sentence if it tests well; just make it the hero line, not a paragraph competing with three other paragraphs.
2. **One screenshot or short GIF** of a real session — timeline, a generated artifact, the provenance view. Reuse what is already in `docs/images/`.
3. **"What you can do with it" — a scannable feature table**, one row per capability, each row linking to the tutorial or how-to that exercises it. Sketch:

   | Capability | What it means | Try it |
   |---|---|---|
   | Literature and data connectors | One-click access to paper and data repositories | `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md`, literature tutorial |
   | Sandboxed code execution | Agents write and run Python/R/shell in a fail-closed sandbox | dataset-analysis tutorial |
   | Task decomposition and skills | Complex tasks broken down and dispatched across skills | skills tutorial |
   | Full-chain traceability | Code, environment, logs, and evidence for every deliverable | `explanation/review-provenance.md`, tracing tutorial |

   The "Try it" column is the part that matters: every claim becomes something the reader can go do. The tutorial targets come from [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26); until those pages exist, the column points at the pages that do.
4. **Get started in three steps** — download, run, first task — with a real download location, then straight into the quick-start tutorial.
5. **Then** requirements, deployment paths, the security warning, contributing, and license. Keep the warning prominent and unsoftened, just below the getting-started path rather than above the pitch.

Also: either source the "300+ Skills" claim (link to wherever that library lives) or restate it in terms a reader can check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can tell within the first screen what the product does, for whom, and what it costs them to try.
- [ ] Every feature claim links to a page that demonstrates or documents it.
- [ ] At least one screenshot or GIF of the product appears above the fold.
- [ ] The tutorial entry point is a prominent link, not a clause in a paragraph.
- [ ] "Installation" says where to obtain a binary.
- [ ] The security warning is still present and unsoftened.
- [ ] `README.md` and `README_zh.md` have the same structure and make the same claims; the Chinese "项目定位" section no longer duplicates the intro verbatim.
- [ ] The "300+ Skills" figure is sourced or restated.

## Open questions

- Is there a public download or release page the README can link to, or is distribution internal for now?
- Screenshot or animated GIF — and can one be captured from a build that is safe to publish (no tokens, no internal hostnames)?
- What does the "300+ Skills" number count?
- Should the README carry the feature table, or stay short and delegate to a docs landing page once [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) publishes one?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (docs site + content completeness), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (tutorial series), [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) (onboarding experience), [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) (finding the download).

## Summary

When a dependency is missing, `scripts/start-stack.sh` prints one sentence naming the requirement and exits. It never says how to satisfy it or where to read more, so the first thing a new user meets is a dead end.

## Current behaviour

`scripts/start-stack.sh` (lines 212–250):

```bash
require_command() { # <command> <failure message>
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null || { echo "$2" >&2; exit 1; }
}

require_command node   "Node.js 22.19+ is required."
require_command pnpm   "pnpm 11.1.2 is required."
require_command python3 "Python 3 is required for workspace analysis."
require_command uv     "uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments."
require_command curl   "curl is required for local service startup checks."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_BWRAP_PATH:-bwrap}" "bubblewrap is required for isolated Linux execution."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH:-/usr/bin/sandbox-exec}" "macOS sandbox-exec is required for isolated execution."
```

So on a fresh machine the entire output is:

```
pnpm 11.1.2 is required.
```

and the process exits 1.

One check already does better and is worth copying — the Node version gate reports what it found:

```
Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.
```

That is the right shape; it is just missing the "and here is how to fix it" half, and the other seven checks do not even report the found version.

## Why this matters

The target audience is researchers, not Node developers. "pnpm 11.1.2 is required" assumes the reader knows what pnpm is, that it is installed through corepack or npm, and that the version is pinned deliberately. `uv` and `bubblewrap` are worse — neither is something a scientist would have encountered, and `bwrap` is not even the name printed in the error, so searching for "bubblewrap" and searching for the binary give different results.

The information exists: `README.md` has a requirements table, and `docs/*/how-to/deployment.md` has per-platform install commands. The failure message just never points there. This is the same class of stumble reported in [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) — the product is reachable but the path to it is not explained.

## Proposal

Extend `require_command` to take a remedy, and print three things on failure: what is missing, what was found (when anything was), and one concrete next step.

```
uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments; not found on PATH.
Install:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Details:  docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes
```

Specifically:

- **node / pnpm** — name the version manager the project expects (corepack, `npm i -g pnpm@11.1.2`, or whatever is canonical here) rather than leaving the reader to pick.
- **uv** — the official install line, plus the note that it is only needed for source mode.
- **bubblewrap** — the package name per distro (`apt install bubblewrap`, `dnf install bubblewrap`) and the fact that the binary is `bwrap`, since the error names one and `command -v` looks for the other.
- **sandbox-exec** — say it ships with macOS, so "missing" almost always means a restricted parent sandbox rather than something to install; `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` already explains this, and the error should link to it.
- Report the found version wherever a version gate exists, as the Node check already does.
- Collect all failures before exiting instead of stopping at the first one, so a user on a bare machine learns everything they need in one run rather than in five.

Keep each message to two or three lines — this is not a place for a wall of text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every preflight failure names the missing dependency, what was found (if anything), and a concrete install step or doc link.
- [ ] The doc link resolves to a section that actually covers that dependency.
- [ ] The bubblewrap message reconciles the package name with the `bwrap` binary name.
- [ ] A machine missing several dependencies reports them all in one run.
- [ ] The messages stay short enough to read in a terminal.

## Open question

Should the install commands live in the script, or should the script print only a doc anchor and keep the platform-specific commands in the deployment guide? Inline commands are more immediately useful; a single doc anchor is easier to keep correct.
oldest.title: [Feature]: Dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing

oldest.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery ships a real command-line client — `ScienceDiscovery run` — that can drive a full agent task, stream JSONL, read from stdin, and be scripted. **The README never mentions it in either language.** A researcher who wants to batch a hundred runs from a job script has no way to learn the capability exists short of running `help`.

## What already exists

From `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` (the binary's own `help` output):

```text
Commands:
  serve                    Start the Web UI, control API and sandbox runner
  run [input] [options]    Run an agent task via a running serve (CLI client)
  extract --to <dir>       Unpack the embedded runtime payload without starting it
  version                  Print the release version and bundled runtime versions
  help                     Show this message
```

`run` takes 13 options: `--content`, `--stdin`, `--session`, `--project`, `--model`, `--skills`, `--connectors`, `--approval`, `--auto-approve`, `--review`, `--token`, `--output <jsonl|text>`, `--timeout`.

`services/launcher/src/run.ts` documents the behaviour that makes it scriptable:

- **text mode** (default on a TTY): the answer streams to stdout, status and progress to stderr — so `run "question" > answer.md` yields a clean file.
- **jsonl mode** (default when piped): every event is one JSON line on stdout, errors included, so a downstream `jq` never meets a non-JSON line.

This is a genuinely useful capability for the target audience: reproducible batch runs from a job script, a run per dataset, output piped straight into an analysis pipeline.

## The gap

1. **Neither README mentions it.** `README.md` and `README_zh.md` contain no occurrence of "CLI", "command line", "命令行", "headless", `jsonl`, or `ScienceDiscovery run`. Quick start shows only `./ScienceDiscovery serve`.

2. **The English deployment guide omits the command entirely.** The two guides disagree:

   | Guide | Commands listed |
   |---|---|
   | `docs/zh/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, **`run`**, `extract`, `version`, `help` |
   | `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, `extract`, `version`, `help` |

   The Chinese guide also carries a worked example and the mode/approval rules; the English guide has none of it. So today the CLI is documented **only in Chinese**.

3. There is no `reference/cli.md` in either language — raised separately in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).

## Proposal

Add a short **Command line** section to `README.md` and `README_zh.md`, after Quick start — four or five lines, not a manual:

````markdown
## Command line

Besides the Web UI, a running `serve` can be driven from the terminal:

```bash
./ScienceDiscovery serve &                      # start the stack
./ScienceDiscovery run "Summarize these results" > answer.md
cat prompt.txt | ./ScienceDiscovery run --stdin --auto-approve | jq .
```

`run` connects to the same control plane as the browser and reads the token
from the data directory, so no extra setup is needed when `run` and `serve`
share a `--data-dir`. On a TTY the answer goes to stdout and progress to
stderr; when piped it emits JSONL, and a non-interactive run must pass
`--auto-approve` because it cannot answer permission prompts.
See [CLI reference](docs/en/reference/cli.md) for every command and option.
````

And alongside it:

- Add `run` to the command list in `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` so the two languages match, porting the example and the text/jsonl and approval rules from the Chinese guide.
- If the README grows a feature table ([#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27)), give scripted/batch use a row of its own — it is a differentiator worth stating, not a footnote.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both READMEs introduce the CLI with at least one runnable example.
- [ ] The README states the TTY/pipe output-mode difference and the `--auto-approve` requirement for non-interactive runs, so a first scripted attempt does not fail unexplained.
- [ ] `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` lists `run` alongside `serve`, `extract`, `version`, and `help`.
- [ ] The English and Chinese command lists match.
- [ ] The README links to a CLI reference once one exists.

## Open questions

- Does the README keep a short teaser and delegate details to the deployment guide / CLI reference, or carry a slightly fuller example?
- Should the example use the binary (`./ScienceDiscovery run`) only, or also show the source-mode equivalent?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (a `reference/cli.md` and the docs site), [#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27) (README rework).
oldest.title: [Docs]: Introduce the command-line interface in the README

oldest.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery cannot run on Windows in any form. The word "windows" does not appear in `README.md` or in either deployment guide — it is not a documented limitation, it is simply absent. Comparable open-source research workbenches ship Windows desktop builds, so this excludes a large share of the researchers we are aiming at.

## What blocks Windows today

| Layer | Current state |
|---|---|
| Sandbox | `SandboxProvider = "bubblewrap" \| "seatbelt"` (`packages/sandbox-capability/src/index.ts:34`). No Windows provider exists. |
| Platform branch | `services/launcher/src/serve.ts:213`: `process.platform === "darwin" ? "darwin" : "linux"` — everything non-macOS is assumed Linux. |
| Shell | `packages/executor/src/environment.ts:85` hardcodes `/bin/bash` (macOS) or `/usr/bin/bash` (Linux). |
| Binary packaging | `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:131` emits `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-linux-<arch>` only. |
| Startup script | `scripts/start-stack.sh` is bash, and its `uname -s` switch exits with "Native sandbox execution is unsupported on …" for anything but Darwin/Linux. |
| Runner SEA | Linux x64/arm64 only. |
| Docker path | README marks it Linux-only (needs host unprivileged user namespaces). |

The crux is the sandbox. Code execution is deliberately fail-closed, and there is no Windows equivalent of Bubblewrap, so Windows support is a sandbox question first and a packaging question second. `--skip-sandbox-check` must **not** become the Windows story: shipping a platform where `run_shell` executes unsandboxed would quietly break the security contract the README states.

## Proposal

Treat this as two tracks with very different costs.

### Track A — a supported WSL2 path (small, do this first)

WSL2 is a real Linux kernel with user namespaces, so Bubblewrap works there. Most of the work is verification and documentation rather than code:

- Test the binary and source mode under WSL2 (Ubuntu), including Bubblewrap with unprivileged user namespaces.
- Make preflight detect WSL and give WSL-specific guidance instead of generic Linux text.
- Document the path in the deployment guide: which distro, how to reach the UI from the Windows browser (WSL2 forwards `localhost` by default), where the data directory lives, and the performance caveat about working under `/mnt/c` versus the Linux filesystem.
- Mention Docker Desktop with the WSL2 backend as the second option, and state whether the unprivileged-userns requirement holds inside that VM.

This unblocks Windows users in days, not months, and costs no new sandbox code.

### Track B — native Windows (large, needs a design first)

Requires, at minimum:

- A Windows sandbox provider. Candidates: AppContainer plus a restricted token and Job Objects (in-process, no extra install, weaker than Bubblewrap); Windows Sandbox (strong, but Pro/Enterprise only and heavyweight per-execution); a Hyper-V utility VM. Each needs its own threat-model write-up against what Bubblewrap currently guarantees.
- Replacing the hardcoded bash execution path with a platform-aware shell spec.
- Windows path handling across workspaces, CAS, and the data directory.
- A win32 SEA for the runner and a Windows packaging target.
- A decision on what `scientific_capability`/micromamba provisioning means on Windows.

This should start as an RFC that states which sandbox guarantees survive, not as an implementation PR.

## Acceptance criteria

**Track A**
- [ ] The deployment guide has a tested WSL2 section (EN + ZH).
- [ ] Preflight recognizes WSL and prints WSL-appropriate remediation.
- [ ] A WSL2 run passes the same sandbox probe as native Linux, or the difference is documented.
- [ ] The README's requirements table names Windows explicitly — supported via WSL2 — instead of staying silent.

**Track B**
- [ ] A design document states the Windows sandbox provider and how its guarantees compare to Bubblewrap.
- [ ] No Windows path ships that runs user code outside a sandbox by default.

## Open questions

- Is Windows in scope for the product at all, or is the intended answer "use WSL2"? Either is fine — but the README should say which.
- If native Windows is in scope, which sandbox primitive is acceptable to the security review?
- Does the Ascend NPU path have any Windows story, or is remote compute the answer there?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Support Windows — a tested WSL2 path now, native Windows as a design question

## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Notify users of new releases, and support self-update

## Summary

Remote execution today reaches exactly two kinds of target: a machine you can SSH into, and a Slurm cluster. There is no way to run a job on cloud compute — no serverless GPU, no Kubernetes, no cloud VM. A researcher without an HPC allocation or a GPU workstation has no path to accelerated compute at all.

## Current state

The remote-compute model is already well factored, which is why this is an extension rather than a rewrite:

- `RemoteHostConnectionKind = "direct" | "ssh"` — the product either deploys a Runner SEA over SSH (verified host key, SHA-256 checked upload, HTTP tunneled through SSH) or connects to a runner the user started.
- `RemoteJobCard` carries `command`, `inputPaths`, `outputs`, `resources`, `targetAlias`, and `mode: "slurm" | "ssh"`.
- Jobs pass through an approval step (`approvedAt`) before anything runs.
- The host probe records CPU, memory, architecture, scratch paths, and whether Slurm is present — and accepts Linux only.
- Ascend NPU has a dedicated host broker.

So the concepts a cloud backend needs — a job card, declared inputs and outputs, a resource request, an approval gate, a target registry — all exist. What is missing is a third `mode`.

## Why it matters

The Slurm and SSH paths assume the user already has institutional compute. Everyone else — an individual researcher, a small lab, anyone whose cluster queue is full — is limited to the local sandbox. Meanwhile a comparable open-source workbench offers user-owned serverless GPU runs bound to an approved image digest, which is exactly the "I need a GPU for twenty minutes" case we cannot serve.

## Proposal

### 1. A `cloud` job mode behind the existing card + approval model

Define a small provider interface — submit(image digest, command, inputs, resources) → poll status → fetch outputs → report cost — and let backends implement it. The job card, the approval UI, and the output staging stay as they are.

### 2. First backend: Kubernetes Job

Recommended as the first implementation, ahead of any specific vendor:

- works against on-prem clusters, every major cloud, and local clusters for testing;
- no vendor lock-in in a project whose selling point is being model- and vendor-agnostic;
- resource requests, GPU scheduling, and namespaces map cleanly onto `RemoteJobResources`;
- credentials are the user's own kubeconfig, not a service we broker.

A serverless GPU provider can follow once the interface has one real implementation behind it.

### 3. Keep the security contract explicit

Cloud execution is a bigger step than SSH to a known host, because **data leaves the workstation**. So:

- the approval card must show exactly which files are uploaded, where, and to whose account;
- image references must be content-addressed digests, not mutable tags;
- credentials stay user-owned; the product must never proxy compute through an account we control;
- an air-gapped deployment must be able to disable cloud targets entirely;
- show an estimated cost before approval — the governance and quota machinery already exists to hang this on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A third job mode exists alongside `ssh` and `slurm`, reusing the current job-card and approval flow.
- [ ] At least one backend runs a GPU job end to end: inputs uploaded, job executed, outputs retrieved into the workspace.
- [ ] The approval card states what data leaves the machine and where it goes.
- [ ] Image references are digests.
- [ ] Cloud targets can be disabled by policy for restricted deployments.
- [ ] Failure modes — quota exceeded, image pull failure, job evicted — surface as actionable errors, not a stalled job.

## Open questions

- Kubernetes first, or a serverless GPU provider first for time-to-value?
- Should the cloud backend reuse the Runner SEA inside the container, or invoke the sandboxed executor directly?
- How should cost estimation work when pricing is provider-specific — a per-target rate the user configures?
- Does the Ascend NPU broker share this interface, or stay a separate path?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Support general cloud compute as a third remote job mode

## Summary

Docs describe adding a **custom MCP server**, but ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** has no settings surface for it and the documented HTTP routes return **404**. End-to-end custom MCP cannot be demoed on this binary.

## Repro

1. Local ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 (`http://127.0.0.1:4310`).
2. Open **System configuration**. Groups present include Global defaults, Sandbox network, Network proxies, Skills, Specialists, Permissions, Connection, etc.
3. There is **no** “MCP servers / Custom / Add server” item. Bundle strings have no `mcp/servers`, `Add server`, or `Custom MCP`.
4. **Network proxies** only lists bundled sources (`biomed`, `uniprot`) and **Add proxy server** — not an MCP server.
5. Authenticated API:
   - `GET /api/mcp/servers` → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
   - `POST /api/mcp/servers` (trivial stdio body) → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
6. Contrast: `GET /api/mcp/sources` returns the 12 bundled connectors (all `unavailable` with empty `availableTools` on this instance — separate readiness bug, see #325).

Docs that claim the feature: [Configure custom MCP](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/advanced-setup/configure-custom-mcp.html).

Observed during Scenario 2 Case C (project **自定义扩展演示**), recorded 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Either ship a working custom-MCP settings page + `/api/mcp/servers` CRUD matching the docs, **or**
- Document that custom MCP is not in 0.2.0 and hide/relabel the docs until it ships.

## Actual

UI and API for user-added MCP servers are absent (404). Users following the docs hit a dead end.

## Priority

**High** among functional gaps for “custom extension” journeys — blocks the whole Case C path.

## Related

- #325 — Session-enabled bundled connectors do not expose MCP tools (catalog/readiness)
- Distinct from proxy policy under Network proxies

## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
recent.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable

## Summary

Product `web_fetch` on clearly public HTTPS URLs (e.g. `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/...`, `https://export.arxiv.org/...`, Europe PMC) fails with `INVALID_INPUT` and the message **"local and private network URLs are not allowed"**. That string is produced by the control-plane SSRF guard when DNS resolution returns no addresses or any blocked address — so public hosts are being **misclassified** (or DNS failure is labeled as “private”), not correctly blocked as private SSRF targets.

This is **distinct** from Session MCP connector exposure ([#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325)): `web_fetch` is the global Web capability (vendor fetch via Jina/Tavily/Exa), not the PubMed/arXiv MCP path.

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0**, Session with Web tools available (`web` connector / product `web_fetch`).
2. Agent calls `web_fetch` with a public literature URL, e.g.:
   - `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>/`
   - `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?...`
   - Europe PMC article HTTPS URLs
3. Tool returns `INVALID_INPUT` with *"local and private network URLs are not allowed"* (and/or the same text in the attempt error).

Observed alongside literature run `dad3a25d…` (session `27148ad0…`) when MCP literature tools were also missing.

## Expected

- Public, globally routable HTTP(S) hostnames that resolve to public address space must pass `assertPublicUrl` and proceed to the configured fetch provider (default Jina Reader, etc.).
- DNS **failure** / unresolvable host must return a distinct, actionable error (e.g. host could not be resolved), **not** the private-network SSRF message.
- Loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / ULA / multicast rejection remains correct for true SSRF cases.

## Actual

Public literature URLs fail with the private-network message before (or instead of) a normal upstream fetch attempt.

## Code path (path is correct; classification / messaging is wrong)

Documented in `docs/en/reference/web-tools.md`:

```text
Agent web_fetch
  → packages/data-source/src/web/workspace-tools.ts (workspace binding)
  → packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts  WebBroker.fetch
       - parses URL, requires http(s), no credentials
       - permission.requirePrivilege({ action: "host", resource: hostname })
  → NativeWebProviderClient.invoke (packages/data-source/src/web/native/index.ts)
       - await assertPublicUrl(input.request)   ← failure mapped to WebProviderError(..., "invalid-input")
  → fetchJina / fetchTavily / fetchExa (packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts)
       - outbound to vendor endpoints from config/external-urls.json (`web.jina_endpoints`, etc.)
```

SSRF guard: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` → `assertPublicUrl`:

- Rejects non-http(s), credentials, `localhost`.
- Resolves hostname via `dns.promises.lookup(..., { all: true })`.
- Throws `PublicUrlError("local and private network URLs are not allowed")` when:
  - `addresses.length === 0` (**DNS failure / empty result — same message as private**), or
  - `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` (any resolved address in private/loopback/link-local/ULA/multicast/etc.).

Broker maps `invalid-input` → product `INVALID_INPUT` (`packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts` `invocationError`).

## Why public URLs can hit this

Likely causes (environment + guard semantics):

1. **DNS lookup failed or returned no records** on the API/control-plane host → empty `addresses` → identical “private network” error (misleading).
2. **Over-strict multi-address policy**: if *any* A/AAAA record is blocked, the whole URL is rejected even when a public address also exists.
3. Broken/sinkhole DNS returning private/ULA for external names (true SSRF-style resolution — message would then be accurate, but operators still need clearer diagnostics).

**Not** the sandbox network allowlist (`SandboxNetworkSettings` / bubblewrap): product Web runs on the Node control plane and uses Web proxy settings / vendor endpoints. Connector `networkHosts` apply to MCP governance URL checks, not to `assertPublicUrl`.

## Impact

- Agents cannot open public paper landing pages / API URLs via `web_fetch` when DNS or classification fails, even though `web_search` may still work.
- Error text steers debugging toward “private network / SSRF” instead of DNS, proxy, or dual-stack resolution.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Split error messages: unresolvable vs non-public address vs localhost literal.
- Log resolved addresses (or failure reason) on the WebInvocation attempt for supportability.
- Revisit `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` vs requiring at least one public address / family policy.
- Add regression tests for: public hostname resolving to public IPv4; DNS empty; mixed public+ULA; literal `127.0.0.1`.

## Related

- [#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325) — Session-enabled arXiv/PubMed MCP tools not injected (separate root cause; literature should prefer MCP, not `web_fetch`).

## Labels

bug, needs triage
recent.title: [Bug]: web_fetch rejects public PubMed/arXiv URLs as "local and private network"

## Summary

System configuration → Skills → Import offers **Folder**, but the desktop/file control only accepts a **file path**. Choosing a skill package directory is rejected. ## Problem

Pushing a version tag starts `.github/workflows/release.yml`. After the L5 gate passes, the `publish` job runs `gh release create` and the GitHub Release becomes public immediately. Nobody reviews the gate result, the generated notes, or the attached binaries before the release shows up on the Releases page.

## Desired flow

Keep the current order up to the gate: tag push, resolve the version, run the release gate. When the gate is green, create the GitHub Release as a **draft** (`gh release create --draft`). A person with write access reviews that draft and publishes it from the Releases page. That publish action is the human review. Do not add a GitHub Environment required-reviewer gate.

## Behavior to preserve

- The tag filter, version parsing, and the hyphen-means-prerelease rule stay. When the version contains a hyphen, pass `--prerelease` together with `--draft`. Publishing the draft later must leave that prerelease flag in place, so a prerelease still does not become Latest.
- A failed gate still creates no Release and uploads no assets. The git tag remains.
- If a release for that tag already exists, whether it is a draft or already published, keep today's path: `gh release upload --clobber` only. Do not publish a draft from the workflow, do not turn a published release back into a draft, and do not run `gh release edit --draft=false`.
- The publish job stays idempotent. A re-run after a failed upload must not be blocked by a draft the first attempt already created.
- Keep publishing the binaries the gate already smoke-tested. Do not rebuild them in the publish job. Keep the SHA256 check and the requirement that both architectures are present.
- Do not add required reviewers to the `nightly-ci-ds` environment. Merge-queue, nightly, and release real-E2E jobs share it for model credentials. Putting a reviewer on it would pause those jobs.
- `scripts/release-notes.mjs` already skips drafts when it chooses the previous release (`previousTagFrom` drops `isDraft`). Leave that unless a test shows this change breaks note generation. A draft must not become the comparison baseline for a later release.

## Docs that currently describe immediate publication

Update only the sentences that say a successful gate publishes a public, downloadable Release:

- The header comments in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a tag push "publishes" the release, and assets "become downloadable" once the called workflow is green).
- The L5 row in `.ci/README.md` ("Blocks Release/assets").
- The L5 row in `.agents/skills/ci/SKILL.md`, which says failure blocks Release/assets publication.

New meaning: the gate blocks creating the draft Release and its assets. The draft is not a public release until a person publishes it. The tag is still created before the workflow runs, and a failed gate still does not delete that tag.

## Out of scope

- Do not move, delete, or re-push existing tags, including `v0.3.0-rc1`.
- Do not re-run or edit a Release workflow run that has already started.
- The new behavior applies to tag pushes after this change is on the default branch.

## Acceptance

- `gh release create` in the publish job includes `--draft`.
- The already-exists branch only replaces assets with `gh release upload --clobber`.
- Prerelease detection is unchanged, and a hyphenated version is still created as a prerelease draft.
- The three docs above match this behavior.
- `nightly-ci-ds` has no new protection rules.
recent.title: [Feature]: Create the GitHub Release as a draft after the release gate

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`** 与 [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta) 同属 **0.3.0 正式版前的预发布版本**：在既有 JiuwenSwarm 科研工作台能力之上，继续收敛质量与工程化交付，为正式版做候选验证。

上一版本为 `0.3.0-beta`（2026-09-30）。本版本汇总 **2026-10-01 → 2026-10-16**（Asia/Shanghai）已合并进 `main` 的变更。

> 本文是面向社区征求意见的 **Release Note 草案**，不是正式发版公告；正式 GitHub Release / tag 将另发。

## Release Note 草案

### 新功能

- **L1–L5 多级 CI 门禁**：按 PR → merge → daily → release 分层累积质量检查，Nightly/Release 真实 E2E 与 hermetic 检查并行落地（#259，相关 #280、#255、#258）。

### 主要修复

- **沙箱 / Runner 未就绪**：启动与 Runner 就绪解耦；执行仍 fail-closed；Agent 可通过 `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` 等待，并弹出重试/切换/取消恢复卡片；区分「展示等待」与「授权修复」（#275 / #265，#282）。
- **不可解析 tool call**：长科研 run 中改为扣留并恢复，不再误报为模型配置错误并整段结束主/子 Agent（#247 / #236）。
- **自定义模型设置**：任一设置接口失败时保留 provider 预设，避免 Custom provider 空表单卡死（#288 / #281）。
- **交付签收**：接受带可选章节号的 Methods/Results/References，避免临近预算误触发重写（#294 / #292）。
- **产物提交**：CAS ref commit 复用已校验对象元数据，降低长轨迹提交开销（#250；#230 仍开）。
- **真实 E2E 稳定化**：J5 等待托管 Python（#287 / #286）；主 Agent run 链完成后再做终局断言（#253）；中断时保留已完成旅程证据（#266 / #263）；Nightly flaky 断言（#207、#279）；L3 改为真实用户旅程（#272）。
- **CI 配套**：job 重跑覆盖同名 artifact（#302 / #301）；分数与诊断产物分离（#240）；Mock E2E 四 worker、UT 并行等（#273、#277、#268、#242）；Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 恢复进 daily/release，Nightly 结构化挂载 `science-research-team`（#270、#306）。

### 行为变更

- 启动不再强依赖本地沙箱可用；未就绪时执行被拒绝，需经恢复流程后再下发（#275）。
- Nightly Biomni 挂载 `science-research-team` 后，分数不可与 beta 裸题基线直接对比（#306）。

# English version

## Release positioning

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`**, like [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta), is a **pre-release ahead of the formal 0.3.0**. It builds on the existing JiuwenSwarm scientific workbench and continues to tighten quality and delivery engineering as a release candidate.

The previous version is `0.3.0-beta` (2026-09-30). This draft covers changes merged into `main` from **2026-10-01 through 2026-10-16** (Asia/Shanghai).

> This is a **community draft** for feedback, not a formal release announcement. The GitHub Release / tag will be published separately.

## Draft release notes

### New features

- **L1–L5 multi-level CI gates**: layered quality checks across PR → merge → daily → release, with Nightly/Release real E2E alongside hermetic checks (#259; related #280, #255, #258).

### Major fixes

- **Sandbox / Runner not ready**: decouple workbench startup from Runner readiness; execution remains fail-closed; the Agent can wait via `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` and present retry / switch / cancel recovery cards; distinguish “show waiting UI” from “authorize repair” (#275 / #265, #282).
- **Unparseable tool calls**: hold and recover during long research runs instead of misreporting a model-configuration error and killing the main or sub-Agent (#247 / #236).
- **Custom model settings**: keep provider presets when any settings request fails, avoiding a stuck empty Custom provider form (#288 / #281).
- **Deliverable acceptance**: accept Methods/Results/References headings with optional section numbers so near-budget rewrites are not triggered incorrectly (#294 / #292).
- **Artifact commits**: reuse validated object metadata on the CAS ref-commit path to cut long-trajectory commit cost (#250; #230 remains open).
- **Real E2E stabilization**: wait for managed Python on J5 (#287 / #286); assert only after the main Agent run chain completes (#253); retain completed-journey evidence on interrupt (#266 / #263); Nightly flaky assertions (#207, #279); L3 as real user journeys (#272).
- **CI follow-ups**: overwrite same-named artifacts on job re-run (#302 / #301); separate score and diagnostic artifacts (#240); Mock E2E four workers and UT parallelism (#273, #277, #268, #242); restore Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 to daily/release and structurally attach `science-research-team` on Nightly (#270, #306).

### Behavior changes

- Startup no longer requires a ready local sandbox; execution is rejected until recovery completes (#275).
- After Nightly Biomni attaches `science-research-team`, scores are not directly comparable to the beta bare-prompt baseline (#306).

## Summary

On the L5 real E2E run ([38734441039](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38734441039), commit `768688fa`, product code identical to `844947da`, judge `deepseek-flash` at temperature 0), BiomniBench-da-13-3 and BiomniBench-da-14-1 scores move much more than the other research cases. Each case was scored four times (three initial runs plus one rerun of the low attempt). All four scores count.

| Case | Scores | Mean |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| da-13-3 | 78 / 59 / 78 / 100 | 78.75 |
| da-14-1 | 83 / 100 / 100 / 93 | 94.00 |

The spread is not one cause. Some points move because a later answer actually meets a written requirement. The rest move because the same kind of answer receives different grades. This issue tracks the case and rubric changes. It does not ask for another research rerun.

The formal L5 numbers are in the test-result comment on #343: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/343#issuecomment-6207027843

## What changed across the four grades

The judge reads both the trace and the answer. Each of the eight answers was scored once. Levels below are A/B across the four runs, in order.

| Case | Criterion | Levels | Where the points go | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| da-13-3 | 3, rank significant proteins by absolute effect size | B / B / B / A | rerun +13 | The runs. The first three rank by adjusted p. The rerun lists a top set by absolute estimate for each phenotype in the trace. |
| da-13-3 | 4, biological explanation of the shared proteins | A / B / A / A | run 2 −14 | Ambiguous rubric, applied inconsistently. None of the four answers states the mechanism the A level asks for. Run 2 is the one marked B. |
| da-13-3 | 5, place the result back in the study frame | B / B / B / A | rerun +9 | The runs. Only the rerun states that the proteome tracks a treatment-driven increase in fat mass and that body composition and hormones act together, with a citation. |
| da-13-3 | 6, source reliability | A / B / A / A | run 2 −5 | Ambiguous rubric. All four answers have a reference list and some unsourced functional claims. Run 2 has the fullest citations and is the only B. |
| da-14-1 | Not the rubric's 21 endotype scores | 38, 26, 38, then 37 columns reduced to 26 | no score gap by itself | Both. The task text the agent sees does not say 21, and the rubric does not name which 21 columns. Every run still fails to narrow to that set. |
| da-14-1 | 1, load and check the score columns | B / A / A / B | run 1 and the rerun, −7 each | Ambiguous rubric. A 38-column answer is B once and A once. A 26-column answer is also A once and B once. The completeness notes are similar. |
| da-14-1 | 2, correlation matrix | B / A / A / A | run 1 −10 | Ambiguous rubric. Runs 1 and 3 both compute a full 38×38 Spearman matrix. One is marked B for not being 21×21. The other is marked A for being broader than 21×21. |

Point values used for the check: da-13-3 criteria 1–6 are A/B = 15/8, 15/7, 25/12, 27/13, 18/9, 0/−5. da-14-1 criteria 1–2 are A/B = 15/8, 20/10. Each scorecard sums to the published total.

## What this does not separate

Temperature is 0 and each request returned on the first try, but every request had a different trace and answer. That does not measure how often the judge would change its grade given the same input.

## Follow-up

- Do not rerun the research tasks to chase these scores.
- Score each of the eight existing answers several times, unchanged, and report how often the grade moves.
- Name the 21 endotype-score columns in the task text or in the rubric.
- Rewrite da-13-3 criteria 4 and 6 so an A is a checklist a second reader can mark without guessing.

Evidence is the `quality-scorecard.json`, `answer.txt`, and `trace.md` artifacts on run 38734441039 (`real-e2e-evidence-a2-research-1-r1` and `-r3` for da-13-3 attempt 2; `real-e2e-evidence-a1-research-2-r1` and `-r4` for da-14-1 attempt 1; the other two attempts are the matching `-r1` artifacts).

## Summary

In multi-step science demos, the agent repeatedly hits **tool-call failures** that it then recovers from on retry. Tasks still complete, but the timeline fills with failed cards and wasted turns. Two concrete patterns showed up in Scenario 2/3.

## Repro / observations

### A. Specialist `task` missing required prompt (Scenario 2 Case B)

1. Create custom specialist **CSV质检专员** bound to skill `csv-quality-check`.
2. Start a session with that specialist selected; upload CSV; ask for a quality check **without** naming the skill.
3. Parent `read_skill` completes; first `task` **fails** (missing required prompt field); retry **completes** with `specialistId` and skill path.
4. Subagent eventually COMPLETED; parent re-checks and declares artifacts.

Session `378644b7-…`, project **自定义扩展演示**.

### B. lmfit `conf_interval` signature (Scenario 3 Case A)

1. Domain-allowlist sandbox; `environment_create` task env; `environment_install` lmfit **1.3.4** from PyPI.
2. Fit Michaelis–Menten; two `run_python` calls **fail** on lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention; later calls succeed after the agent fixes the call.
3. Final fit OK (Vmax/Km/R²), but timeline shows two failed Python cards.

Session `ae359b61-…`, project **科学计算演示**, 2026-10-16.

Similar soft failures also appeared in Scenario 1 (`run_shell` / `run_python` fail-then-complete).

## Expected

- Specialist delegation: first `task` payload should always include required fields (prompt) when the product launches a specialist subagent — schema/validation before the card is shown as failed.
- Scientific library helpers: either pin known-good call patterns in skills/examples, or catch common `conf_interval` / API mismatches with a clearer error that steers the next call without two opaque failures.
- Prefer failing closed in the UI with a one-line “retrying with fixed args” rather than raw failed tool cards as the default narrative.

## Actual

Runs complete via model self-repair, but users see multiple **failed** tool cards and longer wall time for routine fits / specialist handoffs.

## Priority

**Medium** — reliability / polish of the tool loop; not a hard blocker when Always-allow is on.

## Related

- #330 — engineering-heavy timeline makes these failures more alarming than they are
- #327 — long runs already lack incremental progress
recent.title: [Bug]: Agent tool calls fail then recover mid-run (task missing prompt; lmfit conf_interval signature)

## Summary

Uploading a PDF through the workspace **Drop files** control does not go through the paper-reader pipeline. Paper reader stays at **0 parsed**, and the agent only sees a raw file (often with almost no extractable scientific content unless it scrapes bytes itself).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, new session in a data-analysis project.
2. Drop `experiment_notes.pdf` (+ optional CSV) via **Drop files**.
3. Ask the agent to read the PDF notes and fit kinetics from the CSV (no network).
4. Observe: Paper reader counter remains **0 parsed**. Agent reports extracting only the single plain line from the PDF and explicitly notes missing protocol/units/replicates. Units come from the CSV header, not from structured paper parse.

Observed Scenario 1 Case B (session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**), 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Dropping a PDF into the workspace should either:
  - enqueue it for paper-reader parsing (same as the dedicated paper input), **or**
  - clearly label the upload as “file only / not paper-parsed” so users do not assume literature extraction ran.
- If Drop files is intentionally file-only, the empty/paper UI should not imply paper intake for that artifact.

## Actual

PDF is a workspace file only. Paper reader stays **0 parsed**. Structured literature extraction does not run on Drop-files PDFs.

## Priority

**Medium–High** for any “upload paper + analyze” flow; easy to misread as a successful paper ingest.

## Related

Not the same as empty-session CSV intro (#328). Speaks to intake path consistency between Drop files and paper-reader.

## Summary

On first paint after opening the app, the sidebar can show **Projects 0** even when projects already exist, and the **Add project** button appears clickable but does nothing until global settings have finished loading. A later click opens Create Project. Easy to read as “broken UI”.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 (`http://127.0.0.1:4310`), Scenarios 1–2:

1. Open app (Local API already connected).
2. Sidebar briefly / initially shows **Projects 0** while a catalog project (e.g. 文献调研演示) already exists.
3. Click **Add project** once → no dialog.
4. After settings load, a later click opens **Create Project**.

Same pattern noted again when starting Scenario 2.

## Expected

- Disable or show a loading state on **Add project** until settings/catalog are ready.
- Do not render **Projects 0** when the catalog already has entries (show skeleton / previous count / spinner).
- Prefer one click → dialog once ready, never a silent no-op.

## Priority

**Medium** — first-run / return-user trust issue.

## Related

May share root causes with settings-load races tracked elsewhere (e.g. #290 / #291 family); this issue is the **user-visible Add project / Projects count** symptom.

## Summary

The workspace **Artifacts** list appears **project-scoped**: while working in session B, files from session A in the same project still show up (sometimes grouped under the other session’s name). Not a data-loss bug — the model still read the correct uploads — but the list is noisy and easy to mis-click.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 demos:

- Scenario 1: session B’s file count included session A artifacts.
- Scenario 2: during Specialist session, Case A reports still listed under “Skill csv-quality-check” while new files appeared under “Specialist CSV质检”.

## Why this may be intentional

Project-level sharing can be desirable (reuse a CSV across sessions, compare outputs). This issue is filed **low priority** to force an explicit product decision, not to demand an immediate change.

## Design questions (need a call)

1. Should Artifacts default to **current session only**, with an opt-in “Show project files”?
2. Or keep project scope but visually separate **This session** vs **Other sessions** with clearer hierarchy?
3. Should uploads be session-private by default and only promoted to project library on pin/share?

## Expected after a design pass

Whatever the choice, the panel should make scope obvious so users do not think another session’s outputs belong to the active run.

## Priority

**Low** — polish / information architecture; confirm against intended project-workspace model before changing.

## Related

Not a substitute for timeline density (#330).

## Summary

With the **Memory graph** disabled, the agent still attempts (or is expected to use) `declare_claim`, but claims cannot be recorded. The model falls back to saying so in chat instead of writing durable claims. That is a broken / half-wired tool surface rather than a clean capability gate.

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 with Memory graph off (default or global setting on this instance).
2. Run a data-analysis session that finishes with findings (Scenario 1 Case B: enzyme kinetics fit).
3. Observe run: model states that `declare_claim` could not record claims because memory graph is disabled; continues without faking citations.

Session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**, 2026-10-15.

## Expected

One of:

1. When Memory is off, **do not expose** `declare_claim` (and related claim tools) in the agent tool set; or
2. Expose the tools but return a **structured, user-visible** “Memory disabled — enable in Settings” failure that the UI surfaces, not a silent omit / prose apology; or
3. Keep Memory on by default for research sessions so claim capture works out of the box.

## Actual

Claim recording is unavailable; the agent narrates the limitation. Users get neither claims nor a clear settings affordance tied to the failed tool.

## Priority

**Medium** — does not block analysis artifacts, but breaks the claim / evidence graph contract whenever Memory is off.

## Related

Timeline opacity (#330) makes this failure even harder to notice.

## Summary

Every new session defaults to **Ask for dangerous actions**, even inside a project where the user already set **Always allow** on prior sessions. There is no project- or global-level default, so demos and repeated analysis require toggling the composer control every time.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 local demos (Scenarios 1–3, 2026-10-15/16):

- New project opens an Untitled session with approval = Ask.
- User must flip the composer control to **Always allow** (`aria-pressed=true`) before tools run smoothly.
- Creating another session in the same project resets to Ask again — not inherited from the sibling session or project.

Affects projects **数据分析演示**, **自定义扩展演示**, **科学计算演示**.

## Why it hurts

For trusted local sandboxes and scripted demos, re-confirming every session adds friction and invites accidental runs still on Ask (more interrupt cards) or forgetting to tighten back later.

## Expected

- Remember last choice per project, **or**
- Offer a project/global default (Ask / Always allow) that new sessions inherit, with a clear per-session override.

## Priority

**Medium** usability — repeated friction, not a functional blocker.

## Related

Distinct from sandbox egress solicitation (#324).

recent.body:
## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session **timeline is too engineering-oriented**. Parallel tool cards, subagent workspace paths, and token/turn counters dominate the main pane, so a researcher cannot quickly see *what is happening for the research task*. Progress that does exist is buried (e.g. a sidebar tooltip like `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`) while the main area stays on a large **INPUT** dump.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, ~7 min raw screen recording):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards filled the timeline with long specialist prompts (INPUT), UUIDs / `subagents/…` paths, model name, turn counts, and token usage.
- Primary status was often just `Running` / `Tool is running…`.
- The more human-readable status (`PubMed search … · running`) appeared mainly as a **sidebar hover tooltip**, not as the main-pane headline.
- Researchers scanning the UI struggled to answer: which searcher is doing what, what failed, how many papers so far, when synthesis starts.

## Why this is a serious usability problem
This is a research workbench UX issue, not mere polish:

1. Cognitive load: engineering telemetry (paths, tokens, raw INPUT) competes with the research narrative.
2. Progress opacity: meaningful status is secondary (tooltip / deep in cards) while the main column looks like a developer console.
3. Trust: when retrieval degrades (no MCP tools, sandbox/network failures), the timeline does not make the failure mode obvious at a glance.

Related but distinct from #327 (no incremental progress at all). Here the problem is **information hierarchy / audience**: even when something is updating, the wrong details are foregrounded.

## Expected behavior
For literature / research sessions (and ideally by default for non-debug users):

1. Timeline cards should lead with a **human-readable phase** (e.g. “Searching PubMed for clinical CRISPR/SCD papers”, “Source unavailable”, “Synthesizing 5 papers”).
2. Keep subagent paths, full INPUT blobs, token/turn stats behind an expand/debug control — not the default above-the-fold view.
3. Surface parallel branches as short labeled lanes (clinical vs mechanism) rather than two giant opaque tool cards.
4. Put the same status that today only appears in the sidebar tooltip into the main timeline card header.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Default “Researcher” timeline vs optional “Developer / debug” density.
- Collapse tool INPUT by default; show a one-line summary + live status.
- Promote connector/search failures into the card status line as soon as they happen.

## Priority
**High among usability issues** for research users (serious scanability / trust problem), though not a functional crash.

## Related
- #327 — long runs only show `Tool is running…` (progress missing)
- #325 — connectors enabled but MCP tools omitted (functional bug that makes the opaque timeline worse)
- #324 — sandbox egress should ask for permission
recent.title: Usability: session timeline is too engineering-heavy for researchers (tool cards, subagent paths, tokens)

stale.author: openjiuwen-collaboration-bot[bot]
stale.body:
### 🚀 背景描述

ScienceDiscovery 已通过 operational logger 将服务日志写入数据目录下的 `logs/`，默认位置为 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/`。其中 `api.log` 已包含 API 启动、部分组件状态与未分类异常，`runner.log` 记录 Runner 请求和沙箱执行，`run.log` 记录 Agent Run 生命周期。

当前缺口集中在 **Agent/LLM 看不到的框架内部链路**：

- MCP 客户端连接、重连、关闭及工具目录加载缺少完整的成功/失败日志；
- MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 被忽略，进程启动或协议握手失败时缺少服务端原始线索；
- MCP 代理配置解析和运行时切换存在静默失败，且日志无法区分“配置了代理”和“当前传输实际应用代理”；
- 远端 Runner 的主机探测、直连、断线与 SSH 隧道错误主要停留在内存状态中，进程退出后难以追溯；
- 启动阶段部分组件初始化失败缺少统一、可检索的阶段事件。

本功能的目标是复用现有滚动日志，为这些框架链路补齐结构化、可关联、经过脱敏且有体积上限的诊断事件，让开发人员在 MCP、代理、远端 Runner 或启动组件发生故障时，能够仅通过日志定位失败阶段、目标、错误类别、耗时和重试情况。

本方案不是 Agent 操作审计能力，不要求 Agent 或 LLM 感知这些日志。

### 设计思路

#### 1. 存储与日志形式

- 复用现有 `<dataDir>/logs/api.log`，默认即 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/api.log`；
- 继续使用 operational logger 的文本行格式、级别过滤和滚动策略；
- 沿用 `SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_LEVEL`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS` 配置；
- 默认单文件上限 10 MiB、保留 5 个备份；
- 不新增独立 audit JSONL、日志索引、日志文件清单、数据库表或 UI。

日志事件采用稳定事件名和扁平字段，例如：

```text
2026-09-10T08:00:00.000Z INFO [api] event=mcp.connection.succeeded serverId=... transport=stdio durationMs=42
```

#### 2. 覆盖范围

| 链路 | 需要记录的事件 | 关键字段 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 框架启动 | 组件初始化开始、成功、失败 | `component`、`durationMs`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 连接 | 开始、成功、失败、关闭、关闭失败 | `serverId`、`transport`、`endpointProtocol`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| MCP 工具目录 | 全部加载成功、单服务加载失败 | `serverId`、`toolCount`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 代理 | 配置加载、配置变更、解析失败 | `proxyMode`、`proxyApplied`、代理协议与主机 |
| MCP 调用 | 非语义性传输/服务端/超时/限流失败及重试调度 | `serverId`、`toolName`、`requestId`、`attempt`、`delayMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端主机 | SSH 主机探测开始、成功、失败 | `hostId`、`host`、`port`、`durationMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端 Runner | 连接开始、成功、失败、断线、关闭 | `runnerId`、`connectionMode`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| SSH 隧道 | 转发、stream、socket 失败 | `hostId`、`runnerId`、`errorCode`、`error` |

启动组件首批覆盖 Skill Catalog、自定义 MCP Server、Session Store、Artifact 恢复和 Run 恢复。已有 Runner、Memory Graph 等模块的日志继续使用原通道，本功能不重复记录其业务载荷。

#### 3. MCP stdio stderr

MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 从忽略改为受控采集：

- 内存中最多保留 4 KiB 尾部，避免持续输出导致内存增长；
- 仅在连接、调用或关闭失败时附带最后 4 个非空行；
- 单条日志中的 stderr 摘要不超过 1 KiB；
- 成功路径不输出 stderr 内容；
- 摘要进入日志前执行统一脱敏。

该内容用于保留 MCP Server 自身的启动报错、依赖缺失、协议错误等直接证据，同时避免把完整进程输出写入日志。

#### 4. 代理语义

日志必须区分：

- `proxyMode`：当前解析到的代理配置模式；
- `proxyApplied`：当前 MCP transport 是否实际应用了该代理。

例如 stdio transport 不经过 HTTP 代理；HTTP/SSE transport 若底层实现尚未接入代理，也不能仅因存在代理配置就记录为已应用。日志只记录代理协议和主机，不记录完整 URL、用户名、密码或敏感查询参数。

#### 5. 脱敏、体积与可靠性边界

- 统一通过 `redactLogValue` 处理日志字段；
- 脱敏 Authorization/Bearer、token、secret、password、cookie、URL userinfo 及敏感 query 参数；
- 不记录 `args`、`body`、`content`、`input`、`messages`、`output`、`prompt`、`request`、`response`、完整 stdout/stderr 等大载荷；
- 错误消息及 stderr 摘要设置明确长度上限；
- 用户会话内容、模型输入输出、工具参数、工具结果正文不进入框架诊断日志；
- operational logger 保持 best-effort，日志目录创建、写入或轮转失败不能打断服务主路径。

#### 6. 代码落点

- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`：框架组件初始化，以及 MCP/远端计算 logger 注入；
- `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts`：MCP 连接、目录、代理、调用重试与受控 stderr；
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts`：主机探测、远端 Runner 与 SSH 隧道生命周期；
- `packages/operational-logging/src/index.ts`：URL 凭据和敏感查询参数脱敏。

#### 7. 明确不在本功能范围内

- 不提供日志查看、搜索或下载 UI；
- 不生成日志索引或所有日志文件的清单；
- 不新增 Agent 可见事件，也不改变 Agent、Tool、MCP 的业务返回值；
- 不把用户会话、LLM 请求/响应、工具输入/输出复制到框架日志；
- 不实现代理健康检查、自动故障转移或代理管理面板；
- 不将本日志定义为不可篡改的合规审计账本；
- 不在本轮扩展 Paper Worker、模型供应商 SDK、Web Search 或 Memory Graph 的业务级事件。若后续确认这些模块存在框架故障不可定位的缺口，再分别补充稳定事件。

### 涉及到的对外API

无对外 API、SSE schema 或 UI 变更。

内部构造接口增加可选的结构化 logger 注入：

- MCP Node Client 使用 API 现有 operational logger；
- Remote Compute 依赖最小 `info/warn/error` logger 契约，避免 executor package 反向依赖 service；
- 未注入 logger 时保持兼容，不改变已有调用行为。

运维侧继续使用现有日志环境变量，不增加新的必填配置。

### 与其他模块的相关性描述

- `services/api`：作为 composition root 注入已有 operational logger，并记录启动阶段和基础设施 adapter 的生命周期；
- `packages/executor`：通过最小 logger 接口记录 Remote Compute 生命周期，不反向依赖 API service；
- `packages/operational-logging`：继续负责文件写入、级别过滤、轮转和集中脱敏；
- MCP Tool Registry、Agent Runtime、SSE 与 UI：业务接口和事件 schema 不变，不接收本功能新增的框架诊断事件；
- Runner 与 Memory Graph：保留各自已有日志通道，不将既有业务日志重复写入 `api.log`。

### 测试设计与测试计划

#### 功能测试

- [ ] API 启动成功时，组件初始化产生 start/ready 事件并包含耗时；初始化失败时产生 failed 事件且原异常行为不变；
- [ ] MCP stdio Server 正常连接、加载工具目录和关闭时，事件顺序及 `serverId`、`transport`、`durationMs` 正确；
- [ ] MCP Server 不存在、握手失败或调用失败时，记录错误码、有限错误消息和重试信息；
- [ ] MCP stdio 子进程输出大量 stderr 时，仅保留 4 KiB 尾部，失败日志最多包含最后 4 行/1 KiB；成功日志不泄露 stderr；
- [ ] HTTP/SSE/stdio 各 transport 的 `proxyMode` 与 `proxyApplied` 符合真实应用情况；运行时代理变更产生变更事件；
- [ ] 远端 Runner 直连成功、连接失败、断线和关闭均产生对应事件；
- [ ] SSH 主机探测及隧道 forward/stream/socket 失败包含可关联的 `hostId`/`runnerId`。

#### 安全与可靠性测试

- [ ] URL 中的用户名、密码、token/secret 等查询参数不可出现在日志；
- [ ] Authorization/Bearer、password、cookie 等敏感字段不可出现在日志；
- [ ] 工具参数、响应正文、用户会话和 LLM 内容不进入框架日志；
- [ ] 错误消息、stderr 和重复事件在极端输入下不会突破体积边界；
- [ ] 日志写入与轮转失败不会改变 MCP、远端 Runner 或 API 初始化主路径结果；
- [ ] 轮转继续遵守 `maxBytes`/`maxBackups` 配置。

#### 工程验证

- [ ] MCP、Remote Compute、operational logging 定向单测通过；
- [ ] `packages/operational-logging`、`packages/executor`、`services/api` 类型检查通过；
- [ ] 架构依赖检查通过，executor 不反向依赖 API service；
- [ ] 在 Linux/WSL 环境完成涉及真实子进程与文件轮转的回归验证。

stale.author: hsliuustc0106
stale.body:
## Goal

Make ScienceDiscovery a useful, approachable research product. A researcher should be able to understand what it can help with, get started with clear guidance, complete a task, and return to their work confidently.

The first experience we should deliver is simple:

**Open the app → connect a model → upload a CSV and ask a question → receive a useful chart → refine and save the result.**

The application should handle routine setup and organization, ask only for decisions that matter, and explain the next step in plain language. Technical details should be available when needed.

## Why this matters

During a trial of release 0.2.0, a new user encountered welcome cards that did not navigate, confusing model setup, unexplained `Unauthorized` messages, and an interface that opened even though analysis could not run on that computer. These problems prevented the user from experiencing the product's value.

This evidence comes from one installation. Check fixes in the current release and development branch before opening duplicate work. Related public feedback includes [difficulty finding the download](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1).

## Improvements

### 1. Make the starting point obvious

- Explain the product with one concrete example and show its finished result.
- Provide prominent **Get started**, **Try an example**, and **Watch the walkthrough** actions.
- Make every suggested action work. Clearly explain unavailable actions and how to enable them.
- Offer a visible English/中文 switch and consistent wording throughout the experience.

### 2. Guide the user through setup

- Provide one recommended download and setup path for each supported computer type.
- Ask for the minimum information needed to connect a model, with helpful defaults and a clear connection test. Explain any required API key, where to obtain it, and that provider usage may incur charges.
- Handle the app's internal connection automatically where possible. If a user must reconnect, take them directly to a guided recovery step.
- Check that analysis can actually run before showing the app as ready. Explain compatibility problems early and provide a concrete next action.
- Keep advanced configuration accessible outside the ordinary setup flow.

### 3. Make everyday work feel straightforward

- Let users start with a question or a file. Create the initial project/session automatically for the guided example.
- Show understandable progress based on what is happening, such as reading data or preparing a chart. Make waiting, required input, completion, and failure easy to distinguish.
- Provide visible stop/retry actions where appropriate. Preserve the user's question and files when something fails.
- Explain errors in plain language with a recovery action; place diagnostic details behind an expandable option.
- Present the result clearly, with an explanation, supporting evidence, and access to the producing code. Make follow-up requests, saving/exporting, and returning later easy to discover.

### 4. Provide two videos that help people understand the product

**Video 1 — From opening the app to a first result (5–7 minutes).** Show a real released version: download/open, connect a model, upload the supplied CSV, ask a question, inspect the chart, request a change, and reopen the saved work. Provide the sample file, prompt, transcript, and English/Chinese captions. Show required preparation and label accelerated waits.

**Video 2 — The same task with and without ScienceDiscovery (6–8 minutes).** Use IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 to compare the same model in direct conversation and in ScienceDiscovery. Focus on the viewer's experience: what they ask, how much guidance they provide, how understandable and complete the answer is, and how easily they can inspect or continue the work. Also report actual time and cost.

Keep the problem, model, and budgets comparable; review the mathematical proofs and report the observed outcome, including ties or failures. The problem's answer is the family `f(x) = x + c`, with `c >= 0`; describe it as the complete solution family. See the [original problem](https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2026/2026_eng.pdf) and [published reference proof](https://github.com/AxiomMath/IMO2026/blob/main/IMO2026/Q5/solution.lean).

Both videos must reflect working released behavior. Their purpose is to explain the experience and demonstrate useful outcomes. Test the app's guidance with new users, including people who have not watched the videos, and fix the points where they get stuck.

### 5. Make feedback and contribution welcoming

- Provide an obvious way to ask for help or report a problem without requiring users to understand the architecture.
- Explain where contributions are reviewed and how GitHub visitors reach that destination. The [current contribution guide](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/907382ce42e1ebfe77e24281905dec0607aaf003/CONTRIBUTING.md) routes code contributions to GitCode.
- Offer a short first-contribution guide and a few bounded tasks with named reviewers. Useful examples include improving a confusing screen, contributing an analysis example, or fixing a connector.
- Document checks newcomers can run without paid model access or special hardware, and how maintainers help with the remaining validation.

## How we know this is better

- [ ] A new user can explain what ScienceDiscovery does and identify how to start.
- [ ] On a supported computer, the user can complete the sample analysis, refine the result, and reopen the saved work without live maintainer assistance.
- [ ] Setup problems are explained before the user starts dependent work; failures preserve their inputs and offer a clear next step.
- [ ] The main journey works in English and Chinese, and the displayed controls and instructions match the released app.
- [ ] Both videos are linked from the project entry page, use actual runs, and include the materials needed to follow or inspect them.
- [ ] A new contributor can find a suitable task, run the relevant checks, submit a change, and understand the review process.

Observe ten unfamiliar users and use eight completing the sample journey without intervention as an initial target. Also record where users get stuck, whether they return the following week, and whether contributors return for another contribution. These are proposed targets, not current results.

## Delivery

Prioritize the first-use journey and recovery from the problems already observed. Validate the downloadable release, record the videos, and improve the experience with a small pilot group before broader promotion. Give each follow-up a named owner.

items.body:
Folder import was offered unconditionally even when a browser lacks directory selection. Disable its button and input in that case, explain ZIP/Git alternatives in English and Chinese, and clarify that a lone SKILL.md imports instructions only. Supported browsers retain the existing complete-folder ZIP pipeline.

Closes #339.

## Changes

- Check native `webkitdirectory` support before enabling Folder.
- Explain ZIP/Git recovery both beside the Folder option and when selected files lack relative paths.
- Add regressions for supported/unsupported controls and file-only picker results; extend J11 to check the unsupported-browser guidance before importing a full folder.

Browser feature detection cannot determine whether an external automation/file-picker wrapper accepts directory paths. Such hosts receive explicit ZIP/Git guidance even when the underlying browser exposes directory support. This does not claim to repair that external picker.

## Validation

Candidate: `238406dc` (runtime fix in `e0887307`).

- Targeted web UT: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web exec tsx --test tests/SkillManager.test.tsx tests/skill-folder-import.test.tsx`).
- Web dependency build: **PASS**, 16 workspace packages, serialized (`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=1 --filter '@sciencediscovery/web^...' build`).
- Web typecheck: **PASS** (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck`).
- E2E metadata: **62 specs, 0 errors, 11 existing legacy warnings** (`node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`).
- Diff whitespace check: **PASS**.

Required full gates remain **BLOCKED/incomplete**, so this PR is draft:

- `pnpm ci:ut`: bounded attempt exited 124 after 120 seconds during JiuwenSwarm setup/startup, before test execution. Its owned instance was stopped by cleanup. This attempt started on `e0887307`; the subsequent commit only corrects navigation in the new browser test.
- `pnpm ci:st` and `pnpm ci:e2e`: exited 1 during preparation; their `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` failed with `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR: unable to open database file`. A targeted install using an explicit writable store succeeded, but the full-layer installer still failed.
- Bubblewrap preflight separately failed: `Creating new namespace failed: Operation not permitted`.
- None of the full layers produced planned/executed/passed test accounting. No baseline worktree was run; these preparation limitations are not claimed as proven upstream regressions. All build/install/test commands used the shared resource lock. No paid model runs were performed.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED** — browser J11 now checks disabled Folder plus ZIP/Git alternatives on a simulated unsupported browser, restores support, then exercises existing invalid-folder refusal and complete-package import with a readable supporting file. Browser execution did not begin because full E2E preparation failed. The originating host/automation wrapper was unavailable and was not reproduced. Full CI and browser journey validation are required before marking this PR ready.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: unsupported browsers no longer offer an enabled Folder action; complete-package alternatives are explicit.

Compatibility and migration: none.
