## Follow-up update — 2026-09-23

This update adds the pending follow-up commits to the same personal-fork PR, rather than opening a duplicate PR. Target remains `feat/jiuwenswarm`; related #107 and #136. The validation in this section supersedes earlier local results below; historical real-model results are retained for context, not presented as validation of the latest head.

### Added scope

- Isolate shared MCP request cancellation/transport failures and add bounded, credential-conscious boundary/model-argument diagnostics. Consolidate the per-run deadline compatibility change into the version-pinned transport patch; verify patch installation is repeatable.
- Add configurable per-parent subagent concurrency (1–10, default 10) in system settings, with FIFO waiting, cancellation and lifetime-scoped permits. A deployment can set 2 without changing the product default.
- Wire real model transport/text/thinking/tool-argument progress to the owning run's idle watchdog. Preserve the hard whole-run deadline; sibling activity and unowned default-route housekeeping do not renew another run.
- Enforce child model-turn limits at request admission, before calling the provider, instead of inferring turns from UI events/tool-result counts. Keep the existing `timed_out` + `Subagent exceeded maxTurns=...` lifecycle contract. Exclude explicit housekeeping and the pinned Swarm compaction instruction; unknown future compaction prompts count conservatively as task calls. This prompt compatibility predicate is not a security boundary.
- Reject HTML/empty content masquerading as a PDF before publishing download completion. Check only a bounded 1 KiB header; full PDF parsing remains a separate extraction operation. Other artifact formats retain their behavior.
- Expand Mock literature coverage to source fallback, governed download/extraction, tool-output paging, real Swarm compaction, artifact isolation/reload, child budgets/cancellation and recovery. Add a provider-503 → cancel → healthy same-session/tool-backed run.
- Include the five stratified DeepResearchBench real cases and real custom Specialist/MCP/team signoff case, with opt-in record retention. Real evaluations remain manual and are not a PR gate.

### Latest verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Node Swarm agent/model gateway/download/subagent lifecycle regressions | 111 passed, 0 skipped |
| Python Adapter suite | 212 passed, 9 skipped: 7 opt-in live gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM cases |
| Research model + literature-source fixture tests | 8 passed |
| Version-pinned Swarm/SDK compatibility and MCP boundary tests | 51 passed |
| FIFO subagent pool / UI settings draft tests | 3 passed / 1 passed |
| Actual Swarm + Mock LLM/source browser E2E | **20 passed, 0 skipped; 7.1 minutes; one worker** |
| Artifact manager and API builds | Passed |
| Documentation lint/links and CI catalog validation | Passed |

The 20 browser cases use the actual Swarm, Adapter, API, Runner and PDF extractor; only external model/source transports are scripted. They are not evidence of real-LLM research quality, a DRB score, or long-duration memory stability. The formerly failing LR-04 now proves the second child model request never reaches the model; LR-11 HTML now fails before completion.

Coverage details and reproduction prerequisites: `test/benchmarks/research-team/mock-coverage.md` and `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`. The existing research Mock gate remains enabled. **The complete new 20-case suite requires the dedicated offline-source fixture, exclusive Swarm instance and compaction configuration; it is not claimed to run in full in the default PR gate.** No real-provider credentials, raw private traces or local service configuration are committed. Latest CI results must be checked separately.

### Remaining boundaries

- A historical Swarm management-interface timeout was not reproduced by the new recovery case. Its initiating cause remains unproven; a passing controlled recovery test does not establish that the historical incident is fixed.
- No complete six-case real-LLM rerun or RACE/FACT quality score is claimed for this head. The interrupted DRB-59 run is not counted as successful.
- No new Swarm source patch was needed for the latest idle/model-turn/PDF fixes; the PR as a whole still includes the earlier version-pinned Swarm compatibility patches.
- This remains a source-checkout validation. Packaged binary/Docker compatibility, broader resource stability, and dashboard work remain outside these local results.

---

## Summary

Repair the Swarm-backed literature research path: specialist children receive their MCP tools, bind their own model connection, return explicit results/errors, and let the parent continue to a persisted report.

Targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` from the personal fork `zy95-12/sciencediscovery`. Related: #107, #136. Native Swarm delegation reuse remains a separate design discussion in #141.

## Changes and boundaries

- Retain **ScienceDiscovery `task` orchestration + Swarm execution** for main and child agents. When `subagents=task`, hide the native spawn/wait/list/send-input/close/resume tools from actual LLM requests, override generic native-delegation guidance, and reject stale native tool calls. Swarm search/fetch remain available.
- Bind a private model connection to each run/session using the real model name rather than per-run global model aliases/hot reloads. Forward bindings in stream/non-stream paths, allow idle-session rebinding, and reject active replacement. Preserve run/agent identity in credential-free lifecycle logs.
- Preserve startup and runtime errors, initial/resumed stream correlation and output ownership. Require an explicit terminal result: EOF/cancellation/failed status must not become successful completion.
- Keep MCP catalog refresh and child tool failures isolated; give the platform MCP transport a stable lifecycle owner and configured deadlines instead of competing wrappers/read timeouts. No automatic side-effect replay.
- Forward tool-call streaming progress, normalize model SSE output, and make child artifact handoff/provenance available to the parent.
- Carry six version-pinned, reviewable compatibility patches under `jiuwen_swarm/patches/workswarm0.2.6/`, plus regressions and setup/diagnostic documentation.
- Add/update a gate-enabled mocked research journey and an opt-in real DRB-59 browser journey, pinned upstream RACE/FACT evaluation support, and per-attempt result records. Research strategy, child count and source count are not prescribed by the benchmark prompt.

Merged the latest target branch and resolved the `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` conflict: source installs apply compatibility patches before virtualenv synchronization; the target branch's preinstalled path and instance initialization remain intact. The real validation below uses the source checkout, not packaged Docker/binary distributions; these distribution channels still need patch compatibility validation before claiming support for this run contract.

## Mock E2E is a PR gate; real E2E is manual only

`test/swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts` is included in the default mocked PR gate; the CI Swarm stack already enables its platform-task prerequisite. Only `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` is excluded unless **`E2E_RESEARCH=1`**. PR workflows do not set that variable. Real tests additionally require the real project and live credentials. Fast unit regressions also remain in normal CI.

Verified by test discovery: the default mocked list contains the Swarm research mock case and excludes the real case; explicit real opt-in discovers DRB-59. No scheduled benchmark/dashboard workflow was added.

Manual runs against an isolated, configured Swarm stack:

```bash
E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 npm --prefix .e2e run test:mocked -- swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts
E2E_RESEARCH=1 E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 E2E_DRB_EVALUATION=off npm --prefix .e2e run test:real -- deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts
```

See `jiuwen_swarm/README.md` and `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench/README.md` for auth, generator/Judge configuration and full evaluation. Evaluation defaults to `full`; `off` is an explicit integration-only diagnostic mode, not a quality pass.

## Validation

### Latest real run — September 23

**GLM-5.2 + actual Swarm + browser: 1 passed.** Same DRB-59 bird-migration question as the preceding failed attempt. No fixed delegation count/search-depth prompt limits.

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Actual delegation | Four platform `task` children; all completed |
| Child branches | Magnetic, celestial, olfactory/landmark, navigation disturbances |
| Recorded child turns | 9 / 25 / 16 / 15 |
| MCP activity | Successful PubMed / Europe PMC calls; child artifacts declared |
| Parent continuation | Continued research after child results and declared final report |
| Persisted report | `deepresearchbench-59.md`, 5,428 words, 30 headings, 50 distinct URL strings |
| Browser assertions | Visible artifact/preview, basic report structure, reload persistence and final handoff passed |
| Generation duration | 1,011,856 ms (~16.9 minutes) |
| Total browser test | ~23.8 minutes |
| RACE / FACT | Disabled for this run; **no quality score claimed** |

Browser validation was slowed by cgroup memory reclaim; the browser soft/hard limits were raised from 650/850 MiB to 1000/1100 MiB after checking host capacity. Assertions were unchanged; no OOM was observed. This affects timing comparisons. Raw traces remain private because they may contain credentials/research content; test services were stopped afterwards.

The earlier run failed because native subagent tools leaked into the task-mode toolset and native activity did not reset the platform idle timer. That failure is not hidden: the isolation fix addresses the task path; native-child progress forwarding remains outside this PR.

### Automated regressions

- After target-branch merge: API build, 86 affected Node tests, 190 adapter tests (9 skipped: 7 opt-in live Gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM tests), 72 engineering/CI self-tests, documentation checks, shell syntax and compatibility patch reverse-applicability checks passed.
- Delegation isolation validation: 72 Node tests and 71 adapter tests passed.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
## Problem and behavior

Test entry points and discovery rules did not describe the same repository coverage. This change gives local development and CI one selector/runner, loads scenario metadata from adjacent `.case.yaml` files and module discovery from `.suite.yaml`, and preserves the existing test frameworks and default `pnpm test` scope.

Browser journeys move to `test/e2e/`, standalone API journeys to `test/st/api/`, and native agent smoke tests to `test/st/agent-runtime/`. Backend API and all contract scenarios are classified as ST; E2E is reserved for browser user journeys. Shared contract replay/normalization/comparison code lives once in `test/support/contract/`, with its UT alongside it; scenarios, baselines and accepted-difference policy live in `test/st/contract/`. Recursive Node/Web discovery, asset ownership checks and source/build mapping prevent silent omissions. Issue-number filenames are replaced with scenario/object names. Only two previously approved obsolete browser declarations are retired, with reasons and the remaining disabled-connector coverage gap recorded in the migration ledger.

## Directory and layer model

- Product UT stays in the owning module; test-tooling UT stays beside its implementation in `test/support/`.
- `test/st/agent-runtime/` covers direct cross-module agent collaboration.
- `test/st/api/` covers backend service chains through HTTP; `test/st/contract/` owns HTTP/event-stream scenarios and baselines. Both L1 and L2 contracts are ST.
- `test/e2e/` contains browser user journeys. There is no separate API E2E category.
- `test/support/contract/` supplies one shared contract implementation; no scenario-specific copies of the runner or normalizer are introduced.
- API IDs are `st.api.<scenario>` and all contract IDs are `st.contract.<scenario>`. `test/support/migration.json` records the moves and prior draft IDs. Browser IDs and PR/daily membership/backend matrices are unchanged.

## Scenario naming

Use lowercase kebab-case object/behavior names, without issue numbers, `journey-` / `-journey` or `l1-` / `l2-` labels. Examples:

- `test/e2e/first-run-onboarding.spec.ts` and `.case.yaml`, ID `e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding`.
- `test/st/api/child-workspace.mjs` and `.case.yaml`, ID `st.api.child-workspace`.
- `test/st/contract/cases/run-approval-denied.case.yaml`, scenario ID `run-approval-denied`, catalog ID `st.contract.run-approval-denied`.
- `session-multi-turn` describes the former `l2-two-turns` contract scenario; `run-events.json` holds run-event scenarios.

Implementation/config filenames and IDs stay aligned. Shared browser helpers are `scenario-fixtures.ts`, `scenario-report.ts` and `browser-fixture.ts`. Module UT follows module names; Python's conventional `test_*.py` discovery remains unchanged.

Step-report validation is now explicit in YAML (`reporting: steps`) rather than inferred from a `journey-` filename; all formerly marked journeys retain this enforcement. Naming validation rejects the historical test filename prefixes/suffixes.

`namingMigration` in `test/support/migration.json` records old/new paths, catalog IDs and contract scenario IDs. Baseline keys and accepted-difference case references are renamed together; expected response payloads, scenario steps and difference predicates are unchanged. External baselines using the old IDs need the same key migration. The naming migration preserved all 92 configured entries and their policies; the subsequent real-model extension below adds daily coverage, and all 88 retained browser test identities were verified after filename mapping.

## Triggers and usage

Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then:

```bash
pnpm test:list --profile pr --json
pnpm test:list --profile daily --json
pnpm test:doctor --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both
pnpm test:check
```

- PR opened/synchronize/reopened events run the configured PR policy. Pushes to `main`/`master` and manual CI dispatch use the same policy; existing binary/Docker gates remain.
- `test-daily.yml` schedules the daily policy at **00:17 UTC / 08:17 Asia/Shanghai**, with manual dispatch also declared. Scheduled execution starts when the workflow reaches the default branch.
- PR policy has **7 required entries**: both UT tiers, native deterministic ST, and four JiuwenSwarm browser scenarios. Daily policy has **82 required entries plus 54 observational contract entries** (27 scenarios × two executor labels). These are execution entries, not framework case counts.
- YAML separates `llm.mode`, supported executors and scheduled executors. Real-model/hardware/legacy gates are never enabled by selection. PR/daily executor policy cannot be overridden on the command line.
- Nonblocking entries retain FAIL/BLOCKED/etc. and produce `passed-with-observations` when required tasks pass. Full/manual selections treat every selected entry as required.
- GitHub provisions the browser stack/JiuwenSwarm dependencies; local callers must supply the prerequisites reported by `test:doctor`. CodeArts keeps its existing compatibility command scope.

See [test/README.md](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/refactor/configured-test-harness/test/README.md) for configuration examples, gates, executor limitations and report locations. Reports distinguish PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SKIPPED and NOT_RUN; external contract executor labels remain explicitly operator-declared.

## Configured subject models and assertions

Every case now explicitly declares `assertions.mode`: `deterministic`, `llm`, or `hybrid`. Real subject models are configured independently from judge models:

```yaml
llm:
  mode: real
  model:
    protocol: chat-completions
    baseUrlEnv: E2E_LLM_BASE_URL
    modelEnv: E2E_LLM_MODEL
    apiKeyEnv: E2E_LLM_TOKEN
assertions:
  mode: hybrid
  judge:
    model:
      protocol: chat-completions
      baseUrlEnv: E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL
      modelEnv: E2E_JUDGE_MODEL
      apiKeyEnv: E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    maxTokens: 1200
    maxInputCharacters: 24000
    rubric:
      - id: task-completion
        description: The answer and supplied artifact meet the requested task.
        threshold: 0.8
```

A model profile accepts exactly one literal `model` or `modelEnv`; each case may bind different environment names. Credentials are never stored in YAML. The initial transport is OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; scoring requires a model supporting its temperature/max-token parameters.

Browser cases use `assessment.check(name, callback)` for configurable programmatic assertions and `assessment.submit({task, answer, artifacts, context})` for actual bounded evidence. Deterministic mode runs checks without a judge call. LLM-only mode skips those optional assertion callbacks. Hybrid mode requires at least one successful named check and all judge thresholds to pass. Ordinary framework `expect` calls remain mandatory structural/workflow guards. Never put setup/actions inside the optional assertion callback.

Judging runs only after the test body passes. Missing evidence, missing model configuration, malformed/missing/duplicate scores, low scores, HTTP errors and timeouts cannot produce PASS. There is no automatic fallback or retry. Every criterion has an explicit threshold in [0,1]. The configured input limit rejects oversized evidence rather than silently truncating it. Reports include per-attempt assessment attachments, resolved subject/judge identities, sanitized evidence, rubric, scores, reasons, usage when supplied and latency. A framework pass without required scoring evidence is rejected by the harness. Qualitative scoring does not prove numerical correctness; keep objective calculations checked programmatically.

The initial production example is `e2e.browser.model-request`: real subject + hybrid completion/delivery checks and report-quality scoring. The other two existing real-browser files retain deterministic assertions. All non-browser runners currently support deterministic assertions; unsupported scoring/runner combinations fail configuration validation explicitly.

## Daily real-model execution and setup

`test-daily.yml` invokes independent `external:none` and `external:real` jobs through the same reusable workflow. The external tag is derived from **either** a real subject or a live judge, so stub-subject/live-judge cases cannot accidentally enter the deterministic job. PR remains deterministic and receives no model secrets.

All three real-browser files run daily on both native and JiuwenSwarm as required work: six added entries. Daily now expands to **136 entries: 82 required and 54 observational contracts**. PR remains seven required entries. The real job explicitly sets `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`; missing credentials cause required work to fail with unmet prerequisites.

Configure these repository Actions secrets for the supplied profiles:

- `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`.
- `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`.

Custom case-specific environment names must also be wired into the workflow. The implementation does not create secrets or choose a paid provider. Inspect with `pnpm test:list --profile daily --tag external:real --json`; with the six values exported and the isolated stack prerequisites ready, use `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm test:daily --tag external:real`.

`literature-review` now registers/selects the configured model rather than hardcoded DeepSeek profiles; it still depends on its Skill/connector fixtures and PubMed availability. Those remaining requirements can block daily runs. Real-project Playwright traces are disabled because registration request bodies contain model keys; step screenshots and sanitized scoring evidence remain.

Local validation includes actual Playwright fixture execution against a local HTTP judge: three expected passes, three deliberate failures (native check, missing evidence, low score), three scoring requests and five assessment attachments. This verifies execution/reporting integration without calling an external model. No real-provider or complete product E2E pass is claimed: subject/judge variables were absent in the local environment during validation.

## Validation and limitations

Rebased onto `feat/jiuwenswarm` revision `9670568`, preserving its added tests, isolation changes and accepted contract differences.

- Catalog validation: **92 execution entries, 48 suites, 437 static assets**.
- Harness/contract tooling: **65 tests passed**; CI self-tests: **53 passed**; architecture: **19 passed** plus boundary validation.
- Documentation lint and links passed across 89 Markdown files.
- Pinned Playwright collection compared with the latest target: **90 upstream identities → 88 retained identities in 47 files**; exactly the two approved retirements explain the difference. This is collection, not test execution.
- Workflow YAML parsing, shell syntax and diff whitespace checks passed. Workspace-only guest packaging was checked for the YAML runtime dependency.

A full product E2E run and remote workflow execution have **not** been certified by these checks. Contract CI targets/baseline selection remain unprovisioned; their observations report BLOCKED until supplied. Existing product failures are not suppressed or fixed by this test-engineering change.

Implements #126. The issue remains the detailed scope and trigger/usage reference; merging into this feature branch does not activate default-branch scheduled runs.

Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Coverage ran with `needs.ut.result=success` and read the 07:30 package, so `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` reported incomplete coverage.

Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.

Not applicable. No product UI, API, CLI, or run path changes. The bug is which artifact a later GitHub Actions job downloads after a job re-run.

`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` sets `E2E_DRB_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` to `2400000`. The local default stays one hour. The DeepResearchBench README's daily evaluation budget matches this deadline. Research shard jobs remain capped at 240 minutes, so the longer judge fits inside the job.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This commit changes a nightly workflow constant and its README; those layers do not execute the real DRB judge. WSL on this machine has bubblewrap, but the fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, and installing it would not observe the 40-minute deadline. The check is the next nightly after this merges and syncs to GitHub: each DRB case should record citation accuracy and verification coverage instead of `running`.

## E2E user journeys

J5 skipped the real Nightly shard as soon as `GET /api/environment-setup` reported the managed Python base as `installing`. That string is the normal cold-start phase, and the HTTP server is already up, so a single read races the install. Real E2E treats the skip as a failed shard. Closes #286.

## Wait for the base J5 already depends on

`waitForEnvironmentSetup` reads the existing status immediately, then every 5 seconds, on one 180-second deadline shared with an in-flight read. `ready` and `failed` return at once. When the deadline passes, the last observation is returned, including the case where the first read never completes. J5 calls it inside the existing credential and health step, after `test.setTimeout(600_000)`, and still skips with `BLOCKED` when the returned state is not `ready`. The reader only GETs. Nothing starts a second install.

Mocked J3 keeps its immediate `expect(state).toBe("ready")`. The team journey and the runner are unchanged.

## Validation

Requested scope was this one real journey, on `f81767d0f11bce59294424e552d7c881873f6d3c`, model `deepseek-flash`.

- Real J5 (`test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh real`, `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`): Playwright `1 passed (1.3m)`, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Journey report PASS, 6/6 steps, 78.7s. The readiness step passed in 15.2s, inside the 180s bound. The run then completed a statistics request and opened a nonempty Markdown artifact.
- `check-e2e-meta` in that same run: 61 spec files, 0 errors, 11 legacy warnings.
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` was run locally before this pull request: 8 passed / 0 failed. It was not repeated for this submission.
- UT, ST, and mocked E2E were not run. This submission was limited to J5.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Browser journey J5 on the local product stack, tested SHA `f81767d0f11bce59294424e552d7c881873f6d3c`.

A researcher asks, in ordinary language, for a small coded mean and standard deviation and a Markdown report. Expected: the run reaches a completed state, a code-execution step is visible, and the named Markdown artifact opens with content. Actual: all six steps passed; the model run completed in the second step (61.3s) and the artifact preview was nonempty.

Command: `.ci/run-e2e.sh real` with `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`, `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`, `CI_E2E_SPEC=test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`, and a grep for the J5 title. Counts: discovered 1, executed 1, passed 1, failed 0, skipped 0.

## Release

User impact: none in the product. Nightly J5 no longer skips during the normal managed-Python install.

When any one of the settings requests fired at startup or on opening System settings fails (for example `GET /api/memory/settings`), the model connect card loses its whole provider preset list. The provider select then displays "Custom provider" while the card still holds the DeepSeek selection, so the provider name / Base URL / model ID fields never appear, and picking "Custom provider" again does nothing because the select already shows that option. A freshly deployed instance with one misbehaving endpoint therefore cannot configure a custom model at all. Reported on the GitCode mirror as [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137); tracked here as #281.

## Load the provider registry on its own (`App.tsx`)

`client.listProviders()` sat inside the same `Promise.all` as about a dozen unrelated settings requests, both in the startup batch and in the batch that runs when System settings opens. `Promise.all` is all-or-nothing, so a failure anywhere discarded the presets that had loaded fine. The registry now loads in its own promise in both places. Its errors go through the same reporting as before (the System settings alert, or the page error outside System settings), so a failure is still visible. Only the provider list is decoupled. The other settings stay in their batches, because they belong to the same panel and keeping them all-or-nothing is intended.

## Keep the wizard's selection consistent with the options it shows (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`)

A React controlled `<select>` whose value matches no option makes the browser display the first option, and choosing that displayed option fires no change event. Decoupling the request fixes the reported trigger, but the same mismatch comes back whenever the preset list is empty, arrives late, or drops the selected preset. The wizard therefore now resyncs when its selection is no longer offered:

- It falls back to the first preset still offered, or to custom mode when there are none, so the select and the fields always describe the same choice.
- Custom mode entered only because no presets existed gives way to the first preset once presets arrive. It does not do so if the user has started filling the custom fields, or picked "Custom provider" themselves.

## Validation

GitHub Actions on this pull request ([run 38383509722](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38383509722), head `84fdf2f7`) is green: L1, UT, ST, all four mocked L2 E2E shards, coverage, and the merge gate passed. CodeCheck on the GitCode mirror passed as well.

- **L1**: passed.
- **UT**: planned 3798 / executed 3798 / passed 3798 / failed 0.
- **ST**: planned 3 / executed 3 / passed 3 / failed 0.
- **Mocked E2E**: standard-journeys 27/27, standard-config 21/21, research 20/20, literature 6/6. **74 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.** The standard-config shard includes both new journeys and the existing model connect wizard journey.

Local runs (WSL Ubuntu, 8 CPUs, 7.7 GiB, same commit) before that Actions run:

- **L1** (`pnpm ci:l1`): planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4.
- **UT** (`pnpm ci:ut`, non-root): planned 3760 / executed 3760 / passed 3757 / failed 3. None of the 3 failures is caused by this change, and none of them failed in the Actions run above:
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` › "the run's trajectory is recorded from the model calls JiuwenSwarm makes…" fails with `one turn: the title call is not one` (expected `context.captured` / `state.committed`, got only `model.completed`). This is pre-existing. It fails the same way 2/2 on unmodified `main` `e7ba5c92`, and this PR has no diff under `services/`.
  - `services/api/src/server.test.ts` › "Agent-created Skill stays in draft until review publishes it to a Skill Library" failed once with `0 !== 1`, then passed 3/3 when rerun alone on the same commit. This looks flaky.
  - `check:research-python-ut` was blocked by the host's network: `uv` was still downloading pandas/numpy/scipy from PyPI after 30 minutes and was stopped. Rerun through a PyPI mirror, both research suites pass (16/16 for the deepresearchbench suite).
- **New and changed unit tests**: `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx` now has 27 tests, 5 of them new. All 27 pass with the fix. Without the fix, 3 of the new tests fail: no presets offered, presets arriving after an empty list, and a selected preset disappearing. The other 2 new tests guard behaviour the fix must not break: custom fields the user has started filling survive a late preset list, and a custom provider the user picked survives a refreshed list.
- **ST** (`pnpm ci:st`, run as root): planned 3 / passed 2 / failed 1. The failure is `jiuwen_swarm/tests/test_mcp_boundary.py::BoundaryTests::test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once` (`TimeoutError`). Rerun alone on the same commit it passed 2 of 3 times. Actions ran the same layer 3/3, so this is host load, not this change.
- **E2E** (this host, the two journeys this change affects plus the existing wizard journey): 3 passed / 0 failed. A full mocked subset on this 7.7 GiB VM was stopped after unrelated literature-review journeys stalled under memory pressure. Actions then ran the full mocked matrix, 74/74, including these journeys.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS**. Tested SHA `84fdf2f7`.

Actions mocked L2, shard `standard-config`: both new journeys and the existing wizard journey passed inside **21 passed / 0 failed** for that shard (full mocked matrix **74 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**).

The same three journeys also passed locally against an isolated stack (Playwright, Chromium, `zh-CN`). Command: `CI_E2E_SPEC='journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings|journey-model-connect-wizard' bash .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`. Result: **3 passed / 0 failed / 0 blocked / 0 skipped**.

- New `test/journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings.spec.ts` › *An unrelated settings request fails, and a custom provider can still be configured*:
  - Setup: `GET /api/memory/settings` is made to return 500.
  - Expected: the error is shown, the select still offers and shows the presets (DeepSeek selected, with its key link), choosing "Custom provider" reveals the name / Base URL / model fields, and connecting to a local stub model succeeds and creates the provider.
  - Actual: as expected.
- Same spec › *With no presets offered, the connect card opens in custom mode*:
  - Setup: `GET /api/providers` is made to return 500.
  - Expected: the select has exactly one option, it is the selected value, the custom fields are visible, and connecting succeeds.
  - Actual: as expected.
- Existing `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts` › full connect success / failure / config-protection flow: passes unchanged.

Baseline attribution (run earlier with the same patch on the GitCode mirror's tree): with the fix reverted, both new journeys fail at the step that expects the presets or the custom fields, which reproduces the screenshot in the GitCode issue. The existing wizard journey still passes there.

Note for anyone reproducing this locally: on a host without CJK fonts, the existing wizard journey fails its button-width assertion (48.4 vs > 50) with or without this change. Installing `fonts-wqy-zenhei`, which is what `playwright install-deps` provides in CI, fixes it.

`node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 62 spec files, 0 errors.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: Custom model providers can be configured again when an unrelated settings endpoint fails. The model connect card no longer shows "Custom provider" while hiding its fields.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #281
Refs: [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137) (GitCode mirror)

## Summary

- Add a shared E2E helper that follows a foreground Run through main-Agent background Executions and automatic wake Runs before checking final delivery. A completed foreground Run alone does not mean that its background work is finished.
- Use the helper in the Biomni, DeepResearchBench, and Research Team real E2Es. It selects only the root and subsequent main-Agent wake Runs as delivery candidates. Any active Run in these isolated Sessions, including a child Run, blocks settling because the notification dispatcher cannot admit a main wake while a Session Run is active. Main-Agent executions and pending timers also block settling; failed polls restart the quiet window.
- On generation budget expiry, stop the Session wake gate before cancelling active Runs, shell executions, and timers. Re-read Runs and activity until shutdown is verified or one cleanup deadline expires. Record `stopped`, `cleanup_failed`, or `unverified` without treating a failed read as an empty Session. Biomni and Research Team distinguish budget expiry from polling/API failure, retain partial artifacts, and fail the overall E2E on budget expiry.
- Read declared Artifact versions from the current main-Agent Run chain. For each declared Artifact, use its newest version on the current main-Agent Run chain; an acknowledgement-only wake can inherit earlier output, while a broken newer version of the same Artifact cannot fall back to an older one. The final E2E gate also checks each benchmark's requested handoff, so an intermediate note alone cannot pass.
- Add deterministic tests for deferred execution, child Run dispatch blocking, late wakes during cleanup, timer/execution cancellation, failed reads, cleanup deadline exhaustion, and versioned Artifact delivery.

Addresses #252. Related to #233, which concerns displaying the product error after an E2E delivery assertion fails.

## What the live scenario shows

I ran one focused browser E2E against an isolated ScienceDiscovery Web/API/Runner/JiuwenSwarm stack. A local scripted model made the sequence deterministic; it did not call an external model or Jina. **The E2E passed (1/1).** The screenshots are product UI states, while the Run and Execution completion states were also checked through the API. This scenario demonstrates why the E2E harness must wait beyond the first foreground Run; it does not claim that the product lifecycle itself is broken.

Read the screenshots from left to right: **the central chat shows the user's messages and agent replies; the right `Workspace → Executions` panel shows the background task's state.** The same background Execution is followed throughout.

1. **First Run ends; work continues.** In the center, the agent says “This turn is finished.” On the right, `local · main` is still **running**. Checking final artifacts at this point would be too early.

   ![Step 1: the first reply says the turn is finished, while the Executions panel still says running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/01-run-ended-execution-running.png)

2. **A new user question is accepted while the same Execution runs.** The center shows the second message and its reply; the right panel still says **running**. The browser submitted the message through the normal composer, and the two user Runs both reached `completed`.

   ![Step 2: a second user message receives a reply while the earlier Execution is still running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/02-new-run-completed-execution-running.png)

3. **The background Execution and automatic wake Run finish.** The right panel now says **completed**. The API confirmed Execution exit code 0 and the automatic wake Run at `completed`. On this still-open page, the chat had not shown the runtime notice after about 10 seconds. This is a separate UI refresh observation, not a behavior changed by this test-only PR.

   ![Step 3: the Executions panel says completed, but the live chat has not yet shown the runtime notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/03-wake-completed-before-reload.png)

4. **Reload reveals the persisted result.** The center now shows `RUNTIME NOTICE: Synced 1 background execution result(s)` and the wake reply. The scripted model uses a fixed reply, so its wording is not the subject of this test; the ordering and delivery state are.

   ![Step 4: after reload, the chat displays the persisted runtime notice and wake reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/04-execution-finished-wake-notice.png)

The [issue #252 reproduction note](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/252#issuecomment-6095525545) has the same evidence and the separate UI observation. The screenshots are stored on an independent evidence branch in the contributor's fork; they are not part of this PR's code diff.

## Versioned Artifact delivery

The E2E reads declared versions from `/api/sessions/:id/artifact-outputs` and attributes child versions to the parent main Run. It selects the newest declaration **for each Artifact ID and logical name** across the current main Run chain. A later wake declaring `notes.md` keeps an earlier `trace.md` and `answer.txt`; a newer declaration of `answer.txt` replaces only that file. The selected newer version must be readable and nonempty: a broken version cannot fall back to an older version of the same Artifact. Versions from unrelated earlier Session Runs do not count.

Each real benchmark then checks its own required deliverables: Biomni requires `trace.md` and `answer.txt`; Research Team requires `evidence_brief.md`; DeepResearchBench keeps its official report name unless a later Run explicitly hands off another file as the final report. A casual reference to `notes.md` cannot replace the official report. An explicitly handed off renamed report is recognized with sentence-ending punctuation and relative paths such as `./results/review-v2.md`. Required artifact checks prefer a main-workspace declaration over a `subagents/<id>/` copy; without a main copy, they use the latest producing Run and leave same-Run ties ambiguous. Biomni scoring reads the same selected trace and answer versions. A broken supplementary draft remains in delivery diagnostics without failing otherwise valid required outputs. The final chat reply is retained for diagnostics and, for a renamed DRB report, checked against the report's own producing Run. Intermediate files alone cannot satisfy the benchmark. Scientific quality and rubric scoring remain separate.

## Validation

- Original implementation head `9deabda`, rebased onto `main` `e9eac41`: WSL `pnpm typecheck`, 41 focused delivery/Run-chain/shutdown/scoring tests, `pnpm docs:lint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Poll-timeout follow-up at head `7a572ff` (rebased on `main` `e7ba5c9`): one Playwright read timeout is retried within the existing three-failure budget. The pure `run-poll-recovery.unit.ts` tests error classification; a mocked browser E2E in `journey-deliver-result.spec.ts` exercises `waitForRunChainTerminal` after a timed-out read. The earlier placement of this integration test in the UT suite caused CI collection to fail because that runner does not provide `@playwright/test`; the test is now in the Playwright suite. The previous local helper tests (38/38), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm docs:lint` passed before this relocation; `git diff --check` passed on the new head. A fresh local dependency install was blocked by missing offline registry metadata. Hosted UT and the new mocked Playwright regression pass. The mocked standard-config group timed out once in an unchanged compaction journey, then passed 19/19 on a targeted rerun; `merge-gate` passed. A code-identical single-commit refresh at head df03896 re-triggered the hosted gates: CodeCheck (GitCode), L1, UT, ST, all four mocked E2E groups, Coverage, and merge-gate passed. Real E2E was skipped by the PR workflow.
- The three helper suites are named `*.unit.ts` and tagged for the shared UT plan. The CI Node collector loaded all 35 tests in those files (22 delivery, 8 Run-chain, 5 shutdown); a full local UT slice was blocked by the local paper virtualenv missing `pytest`.
- Four isolated mocked browser E2Es passed after the rebase, before the final report-handoff refinement. That refinement passed the focused unit tests. The mocked cases exercised the J2 versioned delivery journey, an acknowledgement-only final reply, the background-execution notice, and localhost-only browser traffic. No external model or Jina calls were made.
- New deterministic tests cover a wake adding unrelated notes, a wake revising only one required file, an empty optional draft, a broken newer required version, renamed Artifact identity, report handoff across Runs, a later wake casually mentioning `notes.md` after the official DRB report, and punctuated/relative-path handoffs of renamed reports, and main-versus-child copies of required outputs.
- Prior real-model run on the pre-follow-up head: Biomni DA-13-3 and DRB-59/62 passed; Biomni DA-14-1 exhausted its configured 20-minute budget. These runs used the user's direct DeepSeek API with quality scoring disabled and no Jina key. Real-model cases have not been rerun after this Artifact selection follow-up.

This PR changes the E2E harness only. It does not change the product Run/Execution lifecycle. Biomni journeys remain outside the daily gate until the separate nightly-restoration PR is merged.

## Summary

Fix the Runner recovery instruction ambiguity exposed by the real E2E failure in [merge-queue run 38333929613](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38333929613). Follow-up bugfix to #275 / #265.

The model received `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`, a valid operation ID, and `wait_for_runner`, but ended with “paused, awaiting your decision” without calling the tool. It explicitly asked for extra permission to display the card because the user had prohibited host repair and machine switching. The test correctly failed: text alone does not create the pending operation or recovery card.

## Changes

- Clarify both `wait_for_runner` and the pre-dispatch failure guidance: when choosing to wait for the user's decision, call the tool rather than merely saying “paused”.
- Explicitly distinguish displaying choices from repairing/installing/switching/executing. Displaying the requested waiting card needs no additional confirmation; the user's restrictions continue to apply afterward.
- Preserve the Agent's ability to explain the blocker and finish. No forced waiting, automatic repair, execution replay, permission broadening, or UI changes.
- Add focused UT assertions and bilingual sandbox documentation.
- Add optional `CI_E2E_REPEAT_EACH` for reproducible reliability runs. Normal CI remains unchanged when omitted.

## Validation

DeepSeek official API (`deepseek-flash`), JiuwenSwarm backend, real browser, and an isolated Runner with a deliberately missing sandbox executable. The existing natural-language prompts and assertions were unchanged; one worker, zero test retries, fresh sessions and Runner fixtures.

| Scenario | Repetitions | Passed | Observed calls | Per-case duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Wait for user, restore card after reload, cancel, resume model | 10 | 10 | `run_shell` → `wait_for_runner` in every run | 41.0–48.9 s |
| Explain the blocker and finish without waiting | 10 | 10 | `run_shell`, no waiting call in every run | 34.7–36.6 s |

- 20/20 passed; zero failures, skips, or retries; browser suite duration 13.8 minutes.
- Provider-reported usage: 50 requests, 1,606,296 input tokens and 14,316 output tokens; no missing usage reports. These are token counts, not a cost estimate.
- Related UT: 71/71 passed. Full build, workspace typecheck, shell syntax and documentation checks passed before rebase.
- Rebased onto latest main (`e7ba5c9`), with no conflicts. The two affected production files and the real E2E spec are unchanged between the tested baseline and main. After rebase: related UT 71/71 passed; documentation checks passed (126 Markdown files).
- Local evidence retained in `/root/runner-wait-repeat-results/e2e-real/`: Playwright results, per-case model-protocol attachments, usage ledgers, and stack logs. Raw traces/credentials are not committed.

This is evidence that the original failure did not recur in ten trials, not a guarantee of perfect model instruction adherence. No test assertion was relaxed and no tool call was injected into model output.

Reproduce with the usual real-E2E credentials exported (never put credentials in the command or repository):

```bash
CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 \
CI_E2E_SPEC=journey-runner-recovery-real.spec.ts \
CI_E2E_REPEAT_EACH=10 \
bash .ci/run-e2e.sh real
```

Nightly and release real E2E should run alongside the hermetic checks and still produce evidence if those checks fail. The L3 merge queue must continue waiting for L2 to pass before making real API calls.

## Scheduling

| Profile | Real E2E prerequisite |
| --- | --- |
| `pr` / L2 | No real E2E; pull-request events remain credential-free. |
| `merge` / L3 | L1, UT, ST, mocked planning and every mocked worker must succeed; mocked artifacts must reconcile before real planning. |
| `daily` / L4, `release` / L5 | Start real planning immediately after the lightweight policy job, alongside L1. Real workers only wait for their own plan; UT/ST/mock completion or failure does not delay them. |

Two mutually exclusive caller jobs express the different dependency graphs. Both call the same `real-e2e.yml`, which owns planning, execution and accounting, so each run executes the suite once. Job-level `if` alone cannot remove a `needs` dependency. The credential-free policy job resolves the profile/backend independently of L1.

Existing cases, commands, shards, backend selection, timeouts and the `nightly-ci-ds` Environment are preserved. Secrets are inherited through the reusable-workflow call and still injected only into Environment-scoped real workers. Cancelling the workflow stops paid execution.

The final `merge-gate` requires every selected check plus the selected real workflow; the unused real entry point must be skipped. A passing real suite cannot hide another failed check or permit Release/assets publication after failure.

## Validation

Current head: `1669c67fa918d74b847cbed8b387b90261cdb20e`.

- `pnpm ci:selftest`: **54 passed**, including **9 scheduling regressions** covering queued/running predecessors, failures, skips, cancellation, L3 sequencing, PR isolation, mutually exclusive callers and publication gating.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned/executed/passed **4/4/4** at the current head.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 (`-shellcheck=''`): CI, real E2E, nightly and release workflows passed.
- Compared the moved real jobs as parsed YAML: after normalizing caller inputs and dependency conditions, commands, Environment, matrix, timeouts and artifact steps are identical to the previous revision.

Full product regressions were run at preceding commit `37c871a77d0cb3e68fa40bede890763135a1b06c`: UT **3754/3754/3754**, ST **3/3/3**, mocked E2E **70/70/70**, and **9/9** supplemental checks, all with zero failures or skips. Its [GitHub CI run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38340881004) also passed. Those full runs were not repeated for the subsequent workflow extraction; product code, test drivers, case definitions and dependencies are unchanged. The affected scheduling tests and L1 checks were rerun on the current head.

No live LLM calls or deliberately failing hosted nightly/release runs were used for this orchestration validation.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** at `37c871a77d0cb3e68fa40bede890763135a1b06c`, on an isolated JiuwenSwarm stack. This is prior-revision regression evidence, not a claim of a fresh browser run on the current head.

| Existing journey group | Checks | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research | Child failures/recovery, research artifacts, context and custom specialists | 20 passed |
| Standard | Sessions, cancellation, settings, tools, artifacts, Runner and environment flows | 44 passed |
| Literature | Offline source contracts and failure handling | 6 passed |
| JiuwenSwarm supplemental checks | History, tools, approval, skills, trajectory and language | 9 passed |

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`.
User impact: real E2E runs concurrently with other checks in nightly/release, while L3 and publication requirements remain strict. No migration required.

The mocked journey "完成的过程去框，运行卡片和文件操作保留" flaked on a Nightly attempt ([run 38318935663, attempt 1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38318935663/attempts/1)) while measuring the collapsed failure record's red dot: the `::after` width came back as an empty string. The same commit's push CI passed the same shard ([run 38267684440](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38267684440)), so this is a frame-timing flake, not a product change.

The dot is drawn by a `summary::after` rule that only matches the collapsed failed record inside `.messages`. `waitForRunTerminal` resolves on the API's run status; the web app then swaps the live timeline for the replay one, and the swap can briefly re-open or replace the card. Every assertion around the read retries (`toHaveClass`, `toHaveCSS`, `toHaveCount`), but the dot read itself was a single `expect(await …evaluate(…))`, so it could land on the one unsettled frame whose summary has no `::after` at all.

## Read the failure dot on a settled frame

`test/journey-compact-process.spec.ts` now polls both failure-card reads until one and the same frame shows a collapsed card with the dot drawn:

- The dot-width read returns "card not collapsed" while the `<details>` is open, then the `::after` width, and still must equal `6px`. A settled frame without the dot still fails — the check is not weakened.
- The next step's layout read (dot hugging the label text, 8px flex gap, no dot margin, label `flex-grow: 0`) is folded into a single polled frame so the geometry and the dot are judged together; a mismatch reports the actual values.

## Retry through the terminal swap for the subagent record border

`test/journey-delegate-subtask.spec.ts` read `borderTopWidth` once right after the run turned terminal — the same swap window, where the subagent section can still be remounted. The assertion is now `toHaveCSS("border-top-width", "0px")`: the same computed-style check with Playwright's retry. The three later border reads in that file stay one-shot — each follows a retrying `toHaveAttribute("open")` guard or a summary click whose state commit is synchronous, so they cannot observe an unsettled frame.

Other one-shot style/geometry reads were reviewed and left alone: the MCP placeholder checks (static settings form, no transition applies to `::placeholder`), the scroll-width/overflow checks (guarded by retrying visibility assertions, and an overflow does not resolve itself between frames), the trajectory drag measurements (drag updates commit per mouse event and the capped-height read is clamped), and the response-identity DOM-order read (structural, guarded by count assertions).

## Validation

On this branch's head commit:

- UT: planned 3746 / executed 3746 / passed 3746 / failed 0 / skipped 0
- ST: planned 3 / executed 3 / passed 3 / failed 0 / skipped 0
- Mocked E2E: planned 70 / executed 70 / passed 70 / failed 0 / skipped 0 (standard 44 + research 20 + literature 6; JiuwenSwarm backend checks ok)

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Browser journeys against the isolated local stack, mocked model:

UT currently starts 342 Node test files and five Python projects sequentially. This change overlaps independent process groups inside the existing UT job, with a default limit of two workers. It does not add Actions jobs or change the selected tests, their assertions, timeouts, or coverage requirements.

## Scheduling and isolation

- `CI_UT_WORKERS=1` retains serial order for diagnosis; values 2–4 enable a bounded pool. API files remain ordered and mutually exclusive because they share one JiuwenSwarm instance/adapter. Python projects also retain their order, while overlapping Node execution. Independent Node files use the remaining slots; tests inside each file remain serial.
- Worker execution uses asynchronous child processes, with per-group product-data directories, logs and timing records. Failures do not discard remaining groups. Timeout/cancellation terminates worker process groups and missing results still fail exact accounting.
- Preparation, collection, command checks and coverage aggregation remain outside the pool. Other slices remain serial. `ut/tagged/timing.json` records group durations, the worker limit, peak active groups and host CPU/memory capacity.
- Nine harness regressions cover bounded scheduling, resource locks, failure/cancellation accounting, actual Node/Python overlap, spawn errors, timeout, descendant cleanup and bounded output.

## Performance validation

The same commit and byte-equivalent frozen plans were run with coverage at each setting. Each command and its children were restricted to four logical CPUs with `taskset`, matching the CPU count of a [standard public Linux Actions runner](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners). Dependencies/build output were prepared before timing (`CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`). Timings include SDK startup, collection, tests, command checks, coverage aggregation and cleanup.

| UT workers | Full command wall time | Test-group execution window | Planned / executed / passed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 15m 14.4s | 831.8s | 3730 / 3730 / 3730 |
| **2 (default)** | **8m 53.8s** | **469.7s** | **3730 / 3730 / 3730** |
| 4 | 9m 24.7s | 494.5s | 3730 / 3730 / 3730 |

Two workers reduced wall time by 41.6% in this comparison; four provided no additional benefit. The serialized API lane remains the critical path. Both parallel runs peaked at approximately 3.4 GiB summed RSS, sampled every 0.5 seconds including SDK daemons. This is a single local measurement per setting, not a statistical guarantee: the host has 31.2 GiB RAM, no 16 GB hard memory cap was imposed, caches were reused, and CPU hardware differs from hosted Actions. The serial RSS sample omitted reparented SDK daemons and is not used for memory comparison.

## Validation

Tested commit: `fcd081e4aab2e5fcf8707f395837e05615a26ab0`.

- L1: 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed.
- UT with coverage, workers 1, 2 and 4: each 3730 planned / executed / passed, zero failures or skips; identical full plans. Each produced all 342 expected Node LCOV records and a Python coverage report, with the same Python process accounting.
- Harness self-test (included in UT): 57 Node tests and 8 Python tests passed, including the nine new scheduler/process regressions.
- ST with coverage: 2 planned / executed / passed (API smoke plus the SDK contract command; the latter ran 69 pytest cases without failures or skips).

## E2E user journeys

PASS — browser and local product stack, JiuwenSwarm backend with mocked models, on the tested commit above. `pnpm ci:e2e -- --backend jiuwenswarm` ran all 70 planned browser identities: 70 executed / 70 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, plus all nine SDK supplemental checks passed. Research (20), standard (44) and literature (6) fixtures passed in one complete run. Session/task lifecycle, cancellation and recovery, research delegation, artifact versions, settings/skills and literature journeys produced their expected UI/API outcomes.

The first local collection attempt did not start browser tests because the new worktree lacked the Playwright dependency link. Completing `npm ci --prefix .e2e` fixed the workspace setup; no source change or test weakening was needed. The counts above are from the subsequent complete run, not combined partial runs. No paid real-model suite was run for this scheduler-only change.

## Hosted CI

[GitHub Actions run 38277729199](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38277729199) completed successfully. L1, UT, ST, all four mocked E2E partitions, Coverage and merge-gate passed.

The [UT job](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38277729199/job/114907445288) took **11m 10s** including setup/uploads; its `Run UT` step took **10m 20s**. The downloaded artifact confirms **2 configured / 2 peak workers**, **4 available CPUs**, **15.6 GiB host RAM**, and **3730 / 3730 / 3730** with zero failures/skips. The selected entries match the local plans. Hosted merge candidate: `32f175e81e60614930a08136e2e3c8814f89f77a`.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`.
User impact: shorter CI feedback; no product behavior or configuration change.
Compatibility and migration: none. Existing job names, artifacts and merge gates remain unchanged.

Replace the L3 numeric/MCP probes with seven real-model user journeys adapted to ScienceDiscovery's public product interfaces. The same cases and assertions run with `--backend jiuwenswarm|legacy`; backend choice remains independent of case selection.

## Coverage

Every case below uses a real LLM and the local product stack, browser and public HTTP API. None uses a model stub or an LLM judge.

| Case | User task | Required outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | Ask for a short streamed response | Actual content/reasoning deltas, a normal stop, a completed Run and nonzero per-Run input/output usage |
| `tool` | Read an uploaded file containing an undisclosed random marker | A real `run_shell` result and the final answer both contain the marker |
| `files` | Update one file while preserving its neighbour | Downloaded target bytes match the requested edit; neighbour bytes remain unchanged |
| `memory` | Reopen a Session and continue the conversation | Persisted history is available, the next request carries it, and the reply recalls the random code |
| `artifact` | Deliver an artifact and continue chatting | The same artifact version and content remain readable after another turn and reopening |
| `workspace` | Edit a relative path in one of two Sessions in the same Project | The other Session's same-named file remains unchanged |
| `cancel` | Cancel after actual model output, then continue | The Run becomes cancelled, the next turn completes, and no queued/running Run remains |

The transparent proxy counts meaningful stream deltas and finish reasons; role-only and keepalive frames do not count. Usage assertions apply to each completed Run, so title-generation usage cannot mask a missing task usage record.

L1/L2 remain unchanged. L3 still selects 7 cases; L4 and L5 each select those 7 plus the existing 10 research cases (17 total). Existing quarantine, timeout protection and the absence of suite token/request budgets or release baselines are preserved. This PR changes four test/documentation files and no workflow or product implementation.

## Validation

Tested commit: `dc53ea7ae4fbe4ef268d22a08ba9b70b31aef08b`.

- `pnpm ci:ut`: 3722 planned / executed / passed; 0 failed or skipped.
- `pnpm ci:st`: 2 planned / executed / passed; 0 failed or skipped.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: 70 planned / executed / passed; 0 failed or skipped, plus 9 JiuwenSwarm supplemental checks passed.
- L1 4/4 and CI self-tests 37/37; build, test typecheck and E2E metadata validation passed.
- Both backends select the same L3 identities; merge=7, daily=17, release=17.

The initial local UT attempt hit the Unix socket path-length limit in its temporary directory. The complete UT suite passed after shortening that test directory; no assertion or source change was needed.

## E2E user journeys

PASS: the seven real journeys above completed on the tested commit with JiuwenSwarm (7/7, about 2.2 minutes) and native/legacy (7/7, about 2.3 minutes), with no failures, skips or automatic retries. These are the recorded real executions of this unchanged commit, not a claim that every research benchmark was rerun.

Reproduction, after preparing an isolated stack and configuring test credentials:

```sh
CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend jiuwenswarm
CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy
```

Session reopening does not test server restart. Optional memory-graph observe/claim-persist calls returned HTTP 500 during the real runs; the primary Run/file/artifact assertions passed, and these journeys do not certify memory-graph availability. Long L4/L5 research tasks were checked for selection inheritance but not rerun.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`.
User impact: stronger basic real-model regression coverage; no product behavior or migration change.

Related: #248. Scenario reference: [DeepSeek Harness tests](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/d743267388641bc76f17c45ce8b4c231aed1d32c/apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests).

recent_merged.body: # fix(runner): decouple readiness and add agent-controlled recovery Target: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery:main` Closes #265 ## Summary Keep the workbench usable when a local sandbox is unavailable. Report execution readiness independently from service availability, and let the Agent explicitly choose whether to wait for the user. - Startup and launcher no longer require a working local sandbox. Execution remains fail-closed. - Add cached Runner readiness with explicit target-side refresh and authenticated capability endpoints. - Add `check_runner` and `wait_for_runner` to the shared tool registry. A pre-dispatch failure returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`, `dispatched: false`, and an operation ID; it does not automatically wait. - An explicit wait shows a conversation card with the blocked operation, cause, repair suggestions, and actions to recheck, switch to an authorized Runner, or cancel the operation. - Every choice returns to the Agent. Neither rechecking nor switching automatically replays code. The Agent must verify the environment/workspace and issue a new execution call. - Keep decisions independent for different blocked operations, validate session/Runner access, release external waits on cancellation, and bound pending waits. - Add English and Chinese documentation. ## UI changes 1. Conversation: a Runner-blocked card appears only after `wait_for_runner`, with repair/recheck, authorized Runner selection, and operation cancellation. 2. Runner settings: execution readiness and a manual recheck button; periodic reads use cached status rather than automatically probing for repairs. Actual Chromium screenshots of the PR's React components and application CSS, using fixture API responses. These are component previews, not a full application/real task E2E run. Images are hosted on a separate evidence branch in the contributor fork and do not add binary files to this code PR. ### Conversation waiting card ### Runner execution readiness ![Runner settings report compute unavailable while the workbench remains usable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/0f615363bc3bb46901d501ec4f857984230baae5/issue265-ui-runner-readiness.png) Browser checks passed: switching to the alternative Runner sends the expected decision and removes the card; rechecking refreshes the displayed capability. These checks use fixture responses, not a running Runner backend. ## Verification Passed locally: - Execution bindings: 19 tests, including unavailable/offline targets, explicit wait, repair, switch, cancel, failed recheck, abort, and authorization boundaries. - Independent execution-block decisions: 4 tests. - Execution readiness HTTP handler contract: 1 test. - Scripted Mock LLM Agent-loop tests: 2 tests, covering final response without waiting and explicit waiting without replay. - Execution readiness UI components: 2 tests. - Runner environment settings: 4 tests. - API and Web builds, API/Web type checks, test TypeScript check. - Markdown lint, standalone package architecture validator, and `git diff --check`. ### Real-model browser E2E (2026-10-12) Added `test/journey-runner-recovery-real.spec.ts`, tagged `@tier:l3 @model:real`. Both cases enter the existing **merge queue / merge_group L3** selection (not the ordinary PR L2 gate). The frozen merge real-E2E plan includes both new cases; no separate workflow allowlist or stored key was added. CI uses the existing E2E model variables/secrets. Run locally against the **JiuwenSwarm backend**, real Chromium, and the **DeepSeek official API / deepseek-flash**. The model is not mocked or forced to call a particular tool. A disposable real Runner has an intentionally missing bubblewrap executable; user prompts contain no recovery tool names. | Scenario | Result | Browser-test duration | Model requests | Input tokens | Output tokens | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | User asks to wait if blocked | Passed | 34.650 s | 3 | 96,137 | 761 | | User asks to explain and finish without waiting | Passed | 36.918 s | 2 | 63,820 | 592 | Observed first-case sequence: `run_shell → RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE → wait_for_runner → visible card → browser reload preserves card → user cancels → cancellation returned to model → completed`. No code was dispatched to the unavailable Runner and no execution was replayed after cancellation. Observed second-case sequence: `run_shell → RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE → final explanation`. No wait tool or card, and no execution dispatch. Provider-reported total: **159,957 input + 1,353 output = 161,310 tokens**, with zero unreported calls. Durations exclude stack provisioning. Full model-request/tool-result evidence, Runner HTTP paths, per-case usage ledgers, and browser journey reports are retained in test artifacts; credentials are not included. The relatively large input count includes the product's normal Swarm context/tool descriptions, not extra research work. Also passed: **18** tests covering the fault Runner and CI selection/real-proxy policies; Markdown lint/link checks (126 files); E2E metadata validation; `git diff --check`. Boundaries: this is one successful real-model run per scenario, not a reliability-rate measurement or a full-suite pass. Real-model repair/retry and switch-to-another-Runner journeys are not covered by these two cases; those branches retain deterministic backend/UI coverage. ## Boundaries - No host/unsandboxed execution and no expansion of Always Allow. - No automatic repair loop or implicit code resubmission. - Browser reload can recover live waiting cards; recovery across API process restarts is out of scope. - A failed recheck returns to the Agent; waiting again requires another explicit tool call. ## Manual validation 1. Start with an unavailable local sandbox; confirm the workbench opens and Runner settings report compute unavailable. 2. Request a shell operation; confirm the Agent receives an undispatched error, without an automatic waiting card. 3. Have the Agent call `wait_for_runner` for that operation; confirm the card appears with cause and suggestions. 4. Repair and recheck, or choose an authorized alternative Runner; confirm the choice returns to the Agent and does not execute the old command. 5. Cancel another blocked operation; confirm only that operation is cancelled. Confirm different pending operations do not share decisions.

The mocked browser suite currently runs its standard, research and literature stacks sequentially. Run the same 70 browser identities on four isolated Actions runners, including two partitions of the standard fixture.

## Execution and isolation

| Worker | Existing fixture | Browser cases | Supplemental JiuwenSwarm checks |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| standard-config | standard | 19 | 9, once |
| standard-journeys | standard | 25 | 0 |
| research | research | 20 | 0 |
| literature | literature | 6 | 0 |

The shared frozen plan generates the matrix (`max-parallel: 4`, `fail-fast: false`). Standard specs declare fresh-library, global-state or session isolation requirements. Files and their steps stay together, with one Playwright worker and zero retries. Fresh-library cases must precede global mutations. Each Actions runner owns its services, runtime data, SDK instance and reports.

Backend selection remains orthogonal: JiuwenSwarm and native select the same 70 browser case IDs. The existing serial `pnpm ci:e2e` entry point is preserved; `--shard` selects one partition. Both standard partitions keep the standard fixture.

The existing merge gate reconciles the exact union of worker plans and results against the parent revision, source fingerprints, backend and identities. Missing artifacts, duplicate/skipped/failed cases, and incomplete or repeated supplemental checks fail the gate. Failed cases remain visible in executed/failed totals. The real-job planner performs the same check before paid calls. The combined `e2e-results` artifact preserves per-worker report links.

The response-continuity journey waits for its actual reasoning event before checking the held-open stream. Its approval, Markdown, reload and response-identity assertions remain intact; agent preparation is no longer timed with a 10-second UI assertion.

The CI operating guide and its GitHub reference now document the cumulative L1–L5 profiles, merge-queue credential rules, four-worker mocked scheduling, result artifacts and reproduction commands. They clarify that real tests wait for UT/ST/mock completion and that `Account for real cases` reconciles results without rerunning journeys.

## Validation

The documentation follow-up at `aad09590d6a0f88ea60f42d08c13a164de3c52fb` changes only the CI skill and its GitHub reference. Local L1 **4/4**, CI self-tests **45/45**, all **9** relative links/anchors and `git diff --check` passed. Full UT/ST/browser results below belong to the preceding code commit; those suites were not repeated locally for this prose-only update.

The complete code validation below was performed at head `f58d5a2565890d45ca64f10633e2b78729f0ff6d`. [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38241597852) also passed, including `merge-gate`. Its merge candidate `007faae0d10a018dd514a70a2359a19f8f8b13cb` has the same selected entries, source hashes, evaluator fingerprint and backend configuration as the local plan.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Local UT | 3730 planned / executed / passed; 0 failures or skips |
| Local ST | 2/2 passed |
| Local L1 / CI self-tests | 4/4 and 45/45 passed |
| TypeScript / E2E metadata | Passed; 11 existing legacy metadata warnings |
| Hosted four-worker run | 70/70 browser cases and 9/9 supplemental checks; reconciliation PASS |
| Fresh local four-worker run | 70/70 browser cases and 9/9 supplemental checks; reconciliation PASS; 9m30s |

The local complete pass used one network namespace per worker and independently copied, verified micromamba/package caches for offline scientific-environment setup. Dependency preparation is excluded from its timing. Both complete passes use JiuwenSwarm; native was checked for identical selection, not executed as a browser matrix.

Failed exploratory attempts are retained separately. Shared-host attempts encountered Chromium `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` and concurrent SDK port allocation; an offline attempt lacked micromamba dependencies. A loaded-host ST invocation timed out in the existing 100-call MCP contract. One earlier delivery journey failed to keep a tool detail open during terminal UI refresh; its assertions and product implementation were not changed, and it did not recur in the complete isolated local and hosted passes. No retries, skipped cases or results assembled from partial runs are used to claim a pass.

## Measured effect

The hosted mocked stage took **10m06s**, including the 22-second matrix planner. The previous [serial sample](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38225160202/job/114730919803) took **25m37s**: approximately 61% less elapsed time in these samples. Summed planner/worker job duration increased to **32m28s**, so the shorter wait uses more runner capacity. This is a stage comparison, not a guarantee for the full pipeline or billing.

No paid API calls were added. The real E2E matrix is unchanged. Related: #248; the L3 real-agent journeys are proposed independently in #272.
